cells.remarks: The Śaka date is wrong by two years. Records gift of land to a certain Narasi- Pantulu, probably a doctor.
Gift of the village Oṛaṅkākoḍi for maintaining a feeding house at Trichinopoly to a certain Iruḷappa-Mudaliyar of Dēvapāmpāṭṭam.
Gift of land for a feeding (annadāna) institute, to a certain Subbaya-Bhāgavata; mentions Virapratāpa Vīra-Veṅkaṭadēva- Mahārāya, ruling at Ghaṇagiri (i.e., Penagoṇḍa).
In modern characters. Evidently a forgery. Mentions gift of land to a certain Pandārakkuṭṭi of Toṇḍipāṭṭaṇam by (a class of people called) Muḍaliyāṇḍi-Paṇṇaiyār of Iravuśari.
Mentions that Muḍḍurāmalin̄ga-Toṇḍi and the king were together in the Paḷḷamaḍam at the time, they gave a copper-plate charter to a certain person at Fajutaṇḍi Kuppaṇichi Ambalakāraṇ.
Gift of another copper-plate charter to the same person by the king and Kijavan Sētupati Muḍḍurāmalin̄ga Paṇḍudaiyār Toṛai, when they were together in the Paḷḷamaḍam.
Gift of land for feeding (people) and providing a water-shed.

cells.king: Lakshmaṇasēna, in his victorious camp at Vikramapura.

cells.remarks: Gift of houses and lands at Aṭṭiyūttu alias Muḍḍuvijayaraghunātha-Sētupati-bhāgapuram to 14 Brāhmaṇa families.
Gift of land and a copper-plate charter to Āhōbalayya of the Kauṇḍinya-gōtra.
Gift of five villages to the temple of Raghunathasvāmin and Parvatavardhani-Amman (at Rāmēśvaram), for worship and offerings.
Gift of eight other villages to the same temple.
Records the construction of a mal (palace) for Rāya-Pāṇḍyanar, the Zamindar of Bōḍināyakkanūr, and the gift of a copper-plate charter by him, to four maṇrāḍis of the village of Agamalai.
Records an agreement between the Dharmakarta (called Ramanatha-Pandaram) and the 512 Ārya-mahājanas of the Rameśvaram temple.

The Kali and Śaka years do not agree and the cyclic year Plavanga does not correspond with either. Registers the construction of a maṭha called Tirunīlakaṇḍar-maḍam at Paḷanīmānagaram (i.e., Palani) and mentions specified fees for its maintenance.
The plates are very badly engraved. The characters look more likely to have been impressed, than cut, on the plate.
Registers the renewal of grants of certain villages to the darga of the Bāb-ayya at Peṇugoṇḍa.
Refers to certain Neyakas who emigrated from ūdagiri (i.e., ūdayagiri) and to the privileges granted to them, by Virapratapa-Bukkarāya in Šaka 1805, Prabhava (wrong). Evidently a forgery.
Gift of some villages near Trichinopoly to the Darga of Bāb-ayya.
Evidently a forgery. Confers the right of Hōḍi on a private individual.
Registers the bestowal of Gauṇḍrika or the right of Gauḍa-ship, on a certain Yarligaṇa-gauḍa, over five villages in the Rayadurga-rājya.
Grant of the village of Kāsara to the temple of Ka[j]ahasti, for mid-day worship and the maintenance of a feeding institute.
Gift of the village U[ra]jain [u]hīre-named Veṅgaḷāmbapura, to a certain Lakshmi-pathibhaṭṭa.
Gift of the village of Tirukkaṭtappalli to the temple of Yajñēsvarattu-Mahadēva, at the request of Cho]la-Mahārajar.

Gift of land to a Vaishpava-maṭha at Tiru-maliruñjolai (i.e., the modern Alagarma lai). 'I wo other records written in continuation register grants to the temple of Vikrama-Pandva-Vinnagar-Alvār at Ki]lai-Koduma]ūr, in the 2nd and 15th years' of the same reign.

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of the tax idangai vari payable by the Pallis living in the villages surrounding Chandragiri, as a gift of money for offerings to the same temple by the people of the villages of the same temple, built by a resident of Padi.

cells.location: Kallavi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records that a dancing girl of the Tiruvengambam-Udaiya-Nayanar temple at Kanchī consecrated the image of the goddess Tiruvallidayam-nachiyar in the temple (at Tiruvallidayam) and presented both to the God and the Goddess a number of jewels.

cells.location: Kallavi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built at the beginning. Seems to suggest that the temple of Tiruvallidayam-Nayanar was situated in . . . . chintamanipura, a suburb of Tiruvallidayam and records a gift of two gardens and two houses by Sahasra Narayan Yadavarayan.

cells.location: Kallavi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a lamp by a certain Sōmanātha-nārāyaṇ of Paramēśvaramangalam in Sembur-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the south and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of land (?) for maintaining lamps in the temple, by the mahajanas of Padi-Tiruvallidayam, in the name of the Saluva chief Sommayadēva-Mahārāja. Mentions Rājarāja-Chaturvēdimangalam alias Agaram Kurattiyur.

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the eighteen professional castes (paṭṭaḍai) of Padi-Tiruvallidayam, to the temple of Tiruvallidayam-Udaya-Nayanar, by the order of Mallappa-Udaiyar.

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Tiruvallidayam for the repair of the temple and the feeding of the Mahēśvaras therein. This inscription ends with the signature of Ganda-gōpāla.

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase, for two lamps.

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the north wall of the mandapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Sale of the village Nulappiyur-Mananjēri alias Nyayap[ri]pattai, to the same temple

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of the village Nulappiyur-Mananjēri alias Nyayap[ri]pattai, to the same temple

cells.location: Kallavi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of the village Nulappiyur-Mananjēri alias Nyayap[ri]pattai, to the same temple

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of the village Nulappiyur-Mananjēri alias Nyayap[ri]pattai, to the same temple

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On a slab lying in the courtyard of the sāṁē temple.
cells.remarks: Sale of land for a lamp to the temple of Mahādēva at ‘Tiruvāļidaiyil in Tuḍamunī-nāḍu, a subdivision of Puliyūr-kōṭṭam, by the assembly of Kuṟaṭṭūr alias Pārāśaka-chaturvēdimangalam in Ambattūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Puļai-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: Kallavi †
cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a perpetual lamp to Mahādēva at ‘Tiruvaļidaiyil in Puḍamunī-nā’u, a subdivision of Puliyūr-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: Kallavi
cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of paddy for offerings to *thrine built by a certain Śēnganlijan ‘Tiruvēļaibhaṭṭan [in the temple of] Mahādēva at ‘Tiruvalidayil, in Tuḍamunī-nāḍu.

cells.location: Conjeeveram
cells.place: On the south base of the Jvarahārēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of tax on looms to the temple of Jvarahāramūḍaiyār in the city (nagara) of Kāñchīpuram in Eyir-kōṭṭam a district of Jayangoṇḍachōļa-maṇḍalam, by the Pallava chief Tipurādar- Nallaśītaran of Ambalur.

cells.location: Conjeeveram †
cells.place: On the north base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land by Sundara-Sōla-vēlār, a native of Viśalur in Virpēḍu-nāḍu, a subdivision of Kaliyūrkōṭṭam which was a district of Jayangoṇḍachōļamaṇḍalam, to the temple of 'Suraśvêta[l]ammuḍaiya- Nayanar

cells.location: Conjeeveram †
cells.place: On the same base
cells.date:
Kīlaka [i.e. Śaka 1291]. [date-calculation appendix, No. 230: 5th year. Sādhāraṇa, Kārttika, śu. 1, Monday, solar eclipse.
In A.D. 1130 (= Sādhāraṇa), on Sunday, October 5, Śukla 1 ended at •28 of day and eclipse was on previous day. Neither śu. 1 nor eclipse was on Monday.]
cells.remarks: Gift of the privilege of supervision in the temple of Sandra(twō) nda-Nayanar, to a certain Ajāgiyaturasan-bhubalamuḍaiyār, son of Bhuvanāikabahudēvar.

cells.location: Conjeeveram †
cells.place: On the south base of the temple of Dēvanāyakasvamin, at Ilambaiyangōṭṭur.
cells.remarks: Records that the stone temple was built by the panḍāri Sivachārarayyan alias Śivapādachēkhara-Mahāvāṇḍa-vēlān.

cells.location: Conjeeveram †
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a lamp to the temple at Ilambaiyangōṭṭur in Kaṇṇiūr-nādu a subdivision of Maṇavūrkōṭṭam in Jayangoṇḍachōļa-maṇḍalam, by a native of Vallam in Puliyūr-kōṭṭam alias Kulōttungachōļavaļanādu.

cells.location: Conjeeveram
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Kaliyiyanallūr in Tiruvaļur-nāḍu to the same temple, by Madurāntaka-Pottappichchholan Vira-Gaṇḍagōpālar.

cells.location: Conjeeveram †
cells.place: On the west base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Retera to a former gift of land by Sēngui Ammanayappan Vāṇiyan Sambāvavarajan, to the temple of Ilambaiyan-gōṭṭaiya- Nayanar at Koṭṭur alias Sōlajōlōbhada-chaturvēdimangalam in Kaṇṇiūr-nāḍu.

cells.location: Conjeeveram †
cells.place: On the north base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a lamp, by a temple-woman.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of 5 oows for a lamp by Kulōttungasōla-Chobam-buvarāyam alias Alagiya-sōlaṇ, to the same temple.

cells.location: Narasingapuram
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Narasimha-Perumal temple
cells.remarks: A fresh copy of No. 17 of 1896, noticed on page 4 of the Annual Report on Epigraphy for 1896-96, paragraph 12.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Monday 22nd September 1263; •99; Nak. commenced at •95 of day. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 238]
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Periya-Puliyur surnamed Narasimhapuram to Brahmanas for the merit of the king by Uttara-pillai, on the occasion of the consecration of Lakshminarasimha.

cells.location: Narasingapuram
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of the same chief for the merit of Periyanayasi Narada-nayaka, on the occasion of the consecration of Prahaladhapurandara -the name given to the image carried in processions in the Lakshminarasimha-Perumal temple-at Kuyarramallur surnamed Narasingapuram, in the Kānyan-kuppam subdivision of Tepkarai Manavīl-kōţtam in Chandragiri-rāja, which belonged to Jaj yangondachola-mandalam.

cells.location: Narasingapuram
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land and a house for the merit of Periyasvami Nārasa-Nayaka in the presence of V[i]jhalēśvara on the banks of the Tungabhadra (river), to each -sa lhai ādānan to recite the dravida vēda and the puranam known as Bhaktisēvījitvini, in the same temple.

cells.location: Narasingapuram
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land to a Brahmana on the occasion of the consecration of Lakshminarasimhāmūrti.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of a house and some special privileges by the mahājanas of Narasingapuram to the watchman in the temple of Lakshminarasimhāmūrti.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Gōlūri Onuraja and seems to regulate the festivals and the daily services in the temple of Alagiyasingar at Kuyam Tyāgasamudramallur alias Narasinhapuram.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On the south wall of the Nachchiyar shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records that an Uśvattiyaṇa shrine (apparently for Rama, Sita and Hanuman) was built in the temple of Mudurantaka-Vinnagar in Kupur-nādu, a subdivision of Mapayir-kōjjan, and a gift of it, of oil for two lamps, by the inhabitants of Kadarangondagōpuram in Pāsali-nādu of the same kōţtam.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers the consecration of the same shrine by a certain Vaniyau Pappandandi Surai alias Strama-dūta of Kidārangondasolapuram ; and provides for offerings and lamps.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land to Vāsudevan Rājasundaran, a resident of Iruniganūr apparently by the assembly Madurāntakamallallar. Mentions Ilambaiyan gōttūr.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Contains portions of the historical introduction of Kulottunga I beginning with the words pugal-mādu.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Seems to register a sale of land by the assembly of Kōdūr alias Sōlavichadhira-chaturvēdimangalam in Kōdūr-nādu, a sub-division of Manayir-kottam in Jayangondasōla-mandalam. Mentions also Madurantakanallur in the same kōttam.

cells.location: Narasingapuram
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the inhabitants of Madurantakallur to the god, goddess and Taiyalvar (i.e., Lakshamī) in the temple of Madurantaka-Vinnagar Alvar.

cells.location: Narasingapuram †
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the main gopura of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Remission of taxes in the village of Kovan, Narasināyakkarpuram, by the certain Sakkaranāyaka [li]-nganayaka for the merit of Siga-TimmayadevaMahārāja, son of Rāmarāja-Tirumraya.

cells.location: Ejaiyarpakkam
cells.place: On the north base of the siva temple
cells.remarks: Built at the bottom. Records a gift of two lamps to the siva temple at Ejaiyarpakkam in Purisai-nādu, a subdivision of Mapavīr-kōtam in Jayangondasōla-mandalam.

cells.location: Ejaiyarpakkam †
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 85 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Tiruppadkkaqudniya Mahādēva at Purisai in Purisai-nađu, a subdivision of Magavir-kötīam in Jayañgondsahoļa-manđalam.

cells.location: Ejaiyarpakkam †
cells.place: On the south base of the same temple ..
cells.remarks: Built in at the bottom. Gift of cows in exchange for a land at Parisai (a devadāna village of Tirup-pachakkudaiyar), granted by a Brahmaņa lady of dayāyappakkākam alias Rajavidyādhara-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Ejaiyarpakkam †
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Damaged. Sale of land by the residents of Parisai to the temple of Tiruppachakkudaiyar at Idai-yāruppakkam alias Rajavidyādhara-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Nandivanam
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Ganesa temple
cells.remarks: Gift of a perpetual lamp to . . . . . . at Nandi-pura by a certain Sēkkilān Kuñjara.

cells.location: Uraiyūr
cells.place: On the base of the Agastyéśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Pāṇalittāṅgal, a hamlet of Uraiyūr-tiyūr in ... a subdivision of Iṟaiyūravēli-paṟṟu alias Śeṅgāttō-kōttam in Jayakoṇḍachōḻamaṇḍalam, to the temple of Tiruvaṇgaṭīśvaramuḍaiya-Tambirānār, for the merit of Sāṇvarna-Appanayakkar. Records that maṇḍapa, gōpuram, gardens, images, etc. were built in the (Śiva and Viṣṇu) temples at Oṟaiyūr, by a certain Avaṇigaṇḍala Paṭṭa(bhi)- rāmuḍu.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the same temple
cells.remarks: Records that mandapas, gopuras, gardens, images, etc. were built in the Siva and Vishṇu temples at Orattar, by a certain Avanigadĵala Paṭja (bhi)-ramudu.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Varāha-Perumāḷ temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Tiruvaṅdavāḍi to the temple of Mahādēva at Oṟaiyūr, belonging to Īlāyirattu-nāḍu, a subdivision of Kalyāṇapuramgōṇḍaśōḻa-kōttam in Jayakoṇḍachōḻa-maṇḍalam. Mentions a number of officers in the king's service.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Mentions the residents of Komalajam alias Vīraśōlapattinam in Paḍuvūr-nāḍu, a sub-division of Amur-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 29th ,, [date-calculation appendix, No. 260: 6th year. Date can be calculated, but cannot be verified.]
cells.remarks: The residents of Taiyūr in Kuṟiñji-nāḍu, a sub-division of Amur kōṭṭam, received 16 kalañju of gold from a merchant of Koḍuṅgoḻūr in Malai-nāḍu and agreed to pay interest in paddy to the temple of Ālvār at Tiruvandandar, in order to feed 30 Brāhmaṇas.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money by a merchant of Mayilarppil in Puliyūr-kōṭtam, to the shrine of the goddess in the temple of Ālvar Varahadéva at Tiruvidavandai, from the interest on which oil was supplied to feed a perpetual lamp, by the assembly and the residents of Tiruvidavandai.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 15 kalaĵju of gold by a merchant of Alaiyūr in Sonadu, from the interest on which the residents of Mađambakkam alias Anuttiramangalam in Nedungunra-nādu of Puliyūr-kōṭtam, agreed to supply oil for a perpetual lamp to burn in the temple at Tiruvidavandai.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the north base of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of 20 kalañju of gold by a merchant of Pūrusthāna-maṅgalam in Vaḷļuva-nāḍu, a district of Malai-nāḍu, who deposited the gold with the assembly of Varāhadēva from the interest on the amount to be supplied as interest on the amount by the residents of Paḍuvūr in Paḍuvūr nāḍu, a district of Amūr kōṭṭam.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of the image of Mahāviṣṇupērumāḷ to the temple of Varāhasvāmin by two Brāhmaṇa residents of Taḻaiyānasappuram alias Taiyūr; and also of gold (for offerings) by the same two individuals.

cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 93 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Varāhadēva at Tiruviḍavandai by a resident of Talaiśayanappuram alias Taiyūr.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 48 sheep for a half-lamp to the same temple.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 30 kaḻañju of gold by a merchant of Tiruvorriyūr in Puḻar-kōṭṭam, to the same temple. The residents of Taiyūr, on receiving this amount, agreed to pay interest in oil and paddy to the assembly of Tiruviḍavandai for burning a lamp in the temple and feeding 35 Brāhmaṇas.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 30 kaḻañju of gold by a native of Vaḍagarai Innambar in Śōnāḍu. The money was received by the residents of Tiruviḍavandai who agreed to burn a perpetual lamp in the temple of Maṇavāḷapperumāḷ.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 kaḻañju of gold for a lamp by a native of Taiyūr.

cells.place: No
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp to the temple of Varāhadēva where, the wife of a certain Āḷattūḷāṉ Raṇakēsari of Paḍuvūr had set up an image.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: An unfinished historical introduction of Vīrarājēndradēva I., commencing with the words tiru vaḷar.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.date: 27th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 272: A.D. 1436-37 Nala, Tai, Saṅkramaṇa.]
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the same temple by the residents of Taiyūr alias Rājakēsarinallūr in Kumiḻi-nāḍu, a subdivision of Āmūr-kōṭṭam which was a district of Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 168 kaḻañju of gold by a merchant of Kaḍarpaṟṟalli in Malai-nāḍu for feeding 12 Brahmans in the same temple for 30 days in the month of Kumbha.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the west base of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Dedication of 12 families for conducting a seven-day festival called Rājarājadēvar tirunāḷ which fell on the nakshatra Śatabhishaj in the month of Āvaṇi.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by a native of Śiṟudavūr.

cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of land at Karaivaḻi-Neṉmali by the inhabitants of Āyiravēli-paṟṟu, to the shrine of the goddess in the temple of Varāha-Nāyaṉār at Asurakulakālanallūr alias Tiruviḍavandai, for maintaining a worship established there by a native of Neṟkuṉṟam in Mēlūr nāḍu which was a sub-division of Kulōttuṅgaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Purchase of land by the temple trustees (tānattār), in a public auction.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of money for offerings by a Brahmaṇa lady of Śiṟudavūr.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Fragment. Gift of land to the shrine of the goddess.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 9 drums for a lamp, by a resident of Satyayakulakāla-chaturbvēdimangalam in Kalattūr-kōttam.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of paddy which was of Tiru-mamalam a village of Puliyūr-nādu which is a sub-division of Puliyūr-kōttam alias Rajendrasōla-valanādu, for feeding 50 Brāhmanas in the Kaji hobingāyam erected by the residents of Tiruvidāvandai.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to record a gift by a Brahmapa lady. Mentions Sembūr-kōṭtam.

cells.location: Tiruvandandar †
cells.place: On the north wall of the same mandapa.
cells.remarks: Gift of paddy for feeding 12 itinerant (apūrvi) Brahmapas, by a native of Vamanamāngai in Tiruvajundūr-nađu, a sub-division of Rājanārayana-vajanađu which was a district of Cbōja-manđuam.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in Tiruvalīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Seems to register sale of house-sites to the weavers and dancing girls of the temple at Vittūr, in Tiruvalakkōyil-nādu, a sub-division of Madurāntaka-chaturvēdimangalam, a taniyūr in Jayangondasōla-mandalam.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil †
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Records a gift of land at Vittūr, the northern hamlet of Madhurantaka-obaturvėdimangalam a village in Kalattūr-kōṭtam.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil †
cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Gift of taxes collected within the manđavijlaga of the temple of Tiruvalakkōyiluđaiya-Nayaṇar at Vittūr, for festivals, worship, etc., in the same temple.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of three vēli of land for conducting worship in the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil
cells.place: On the same wall ..

cells.remarks: Records that Tiruvēdaganathar [granted] the field called nāchchap maniyām to the temple of Tiruvali-yappan, for the merit of Vīrappanāyakkan-Ayyar.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of houses, lands and certain privileges to the dancing girls, whom a certain Varadarāja had newly appointed for service in the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 8 cows for two lamps by a certain Pushpa-giri-jiyer.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil †
cells.place: On the west wall of the mandapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Timur-naśāyaya of Nāranapura built this (mandapa) for the merit of Malaiyappai-yan.

cells.location: Tiruvaģakkōyil †
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of a house and land for a dancing girl who took up service in the temple of Tiruvaiyakkōiludaiya-Tambirāpar, for the merit of Timmarašaiyan son of Rāmarasaiyan of Nāranapura.

cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vyāghrapādēśvara temple at Pulipparakoyil
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of certain taxes on the residents living in the tirumaḍaiviḷāgam of the temple of Tiruppulippagava-Nāyaṉār.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine ..

cells.remarks: Records the remission of Vāśalpaṇam granted by the trustees (tāṉattār) of the temple to the Kaikkōḷars living in its tirumaḍaviḷāgam.

cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Kanakkaṉpaṭṭu alias Śēdirāyaṉallūr, to the temple of Tiruppulippagava-Nāyaṉār at Paṭṭūr the northern hamlet of Madhurāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Kaḷattūr-kōṭṭam, a district of Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam, by Dēvappaṅgaḷ, son of Annadāta-Daṇṇāyaka, for the health of the king.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same maṇḍapa ..
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions a number of chiefs who were apparently subordinates of the king and seems to register certain privileges agreed to by the Mahēśvaras, priests and the Kaikkōḷars of the temple, in the presence of a certain Kaṇḍiyadēvar.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Agaram [Va]ḍudippākkam, the northern hamlet of Madhurāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalam.

cells.place: On the east wall of the same maṇḍapa ..
cells.remarks: Gift of taxes payable within the four limits of the tirumaḍaiviḷāgam, for worship in the temple of Tiruppulippagava-Nāyaṉār.

cells.place: On the same wall ..

cells.place: On a slab set up in the same temple ..

cells.place: On a slab set up in a street of the same village.

cells.location: Nagar

cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Naḍuḍaiyaperumāḷnallūr, which was split from Kiḻpākkam, by a native of Nagar alias Dīnachintāmaṇinallūr in Ōyma-nāḍu alias Vijayarājēndra-vaḷanāḍu, to the temple of Naḍuḍaiya-Perumāḷ in the latter village. It is recorded that 600 kuḻi of land in this village belonged to the temples of Tirunāgīśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār and Naḍuḍai-Vināyakappiḷḷaiyār.

cells.location: Nagur †

cells.location: Nagur †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a street of the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged. The king bears Śāluva titles.

cells.location: Nagur †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to record a gift to Brahmana-s, one of whom in a suppliant attitude is figured on the stone.

cells.place: On a boulder in a field at Āmūr

cells.place: On the same door-posts

cells.remarks: Mutilated. Gift of (90) sheep for a lamp to the temple of Sri-Mūla-sthānamudaiya-Mahādēva at [Nalūr] in Sērrūr-kūṟṟam, a brahmadeya in Śērrūr-kūṟṟam. cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the top and damaged. Seems to record a sale of land.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam †
cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Damaged. Sale of land to the temple of Tirumaya-namuḍaiya-Paramasvāmin, by the assembly of Nalūr.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam †
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of money for a lamp to the temple of Tirumayānam-Uḍaiyār in Nalūr alias Upavāp-mādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam in Śērrūr-kūṟṟam which was a district of Kulōttuṅgaśōla-vaḷanādu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of land to the same temple by the assembly of Naḷūr.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam

cells.remarks: Gift of land (by the assembly of P) Paḷaya Sambiyāy-caturvvēdimaṅgalam on the southern bank (of the Cauvery).

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Records that the assembly of Naḷūr sold the right of collecting the tax called aṅgādi-kūli from stalls opened in the bazaar, to the temple of Mūlasthānamuḍaiya-mahādēva of Tirumayāṉam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Sale of land for offerings to the temple of [Lakuḷī]śvaramuḍaiya-mahādēva of Tirumayāṉam, by a merchant of that village on the occasion, when the assembly of that village had met at the big hall (?) called Rājarājan in front of the temple of Tirumayāṉattu-Mahādēva.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Sale of land by the assembly of [Nalūr ?] to a resident of Vaṇavṇmadēvi-baturvēdimangalam in Segrūr-kūgram which was a subdivision of Kulottunga-Cholja-valaṇaṣu.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a gift of land to the temple of Tirumayānattu Paramasevāmi and mentions also the temple of Samaparēsvarattu-Perumā.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Seems to record a gift of land for the lamp.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land (?) for a lamp to the shrine of Krishna (Tirukkaṭṭiyāḍi-aruḷina-Āḷvār) in Tirumayāṉam, a hamlet of the village of Sōrrūr-kūṟṟam which was a district of Kabaṭṭiyā-sikhāmaṇi-vaḷanāḍu. On this occasion the assembly of Naḷūr had met at the ‘big hall’, called Gaṇḍarādittan.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Śama[p-pe]rē-śvarattu-Perumāṇadigal at Naḷūr, by the assembly of Akkiramāka-chaturvvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēyam in Teṉkarai Tirumayāṉaiyūr-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged and built in at the end. Seems to record a gift of land by the assembly of Aruṇācheri, a hamlet of Tirumayāṉam, to the temple of Tirumayāṉam in Naḷūr.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 Iḷa-kāśu for 12 lamps, by a merchant of Naḷūr, named Naṟaṇan Sōḷadēvan alias Tirumayāṉa-māṇikkam, to the temple of Tirumayāṉattu Para-mēśvara.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam †
cells.place: On the south wall of the mandapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of two lamps by a lady from Sembiyankudivayil alias Alampadi, to the temple of Tirumayanam-Udaiyar.

cells.location: Tirumeyjñānam †

cells.date: 16+ 1st year.. [date-calculation appendix, No. 352: Monday 9 July 1520; -92; -91; tithi was ba. 10 not ba. 11.]
cells.remarks: Registers a decision of the assembly of Nalor alias Vanavagmadevi-chaturvedimangalam. States also that a certain class of people were considered as gramadröhins.

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai
cells.place: On the south wall of the Jagannātha-Perumāḷ temple
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Gift of land by Pañchanadivāṇaṉ Tiruvaṇṇāmalai-Perumāḷ Laṅkēśvaradēva, to the temple of Tirumaḻiśai-Emberumāṉ at agaram Tirumaḻiśai in Māṅgāḍu-nāḍu, a sub-division of Puliyūr-kōṭṭam in Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †
cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai
cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai

cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Gift of land to the temple of Tirumaḻiśai-Emberumāṉ by Pañchanadivāṇa Aruṇagiri-Perumāḷ Nilagaṅgaraiyaṉ. Mentions also the temples of Agattīśuram-Uḍaiyār and Subrahmaṇya-Piḷḷaiyār in the suburbs of Tirumaḻiśai.

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Order of Nilagaṅgaraiyaṉ recording the gift of (the tax) poṉvari-māḍai in the hamlet of Arayappākkilañchēri, to the temple of Tirumaḻiśai-Āḻvār.

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple under the orders of the same chief.

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Sale of land to the temple of Jagannātha of Tirumaḻiśai-Viṇṇagar at Tirumaḻiśai alias Pukkaturaivalla-chaturvēdimaṅgalam.

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Gift of three lamps to the temple of Tirumaḻiśai-Emberumāṉ at [Tirumaḻiśai] in Māṅgāḍu-nāḍu, a sub-division of Puliyūr-kōṭṭam alias Kulōttuṅgaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu in Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †
cells.place: On a pillar in the mandapa in front of the central shrine of the Uttirāsvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a lamp to the temple of Agai-t-tārumudaiya-Nāyanār at agaram Tirumālai alias Pukkatturuvaiśa-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †
cells.place: On another pillar in the same mandapa.
cells.remarks: Gift of money for the Tiruvātirai festival by Sittiramoḻi alias Kūttan, a goldsmith of Tirumāl-māsi.

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai

cells.location: Tirumaḻiśai

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.location: Tirumaṅgalam †

cells.place: On the base of the same shrine

cells.location: Mudūr

cells.location: Poonamallee

cells.place: On the same base

cells.location: Poonamallee
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of agaram Śēranādyachakravartinālamakam which was split up into shares (bhāga) and made a sarvamānya grant "to the assembly of that village. The figure of a fish surmounted by an akshala is, depicted on the right margin of the record.

cells.location: Poonamallee
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Records that the Chāra king who conquered Sundara-Pāndya, granted (the village) Chirapāndya (śēnam), re-designated for the enjoyment of the Brahmanas.

cells.location: Kīlpakkam

cells.remarks: Records that a son of Kaļigaśaraya named Apatsahaya Pallavaraiyan renovated with stone the dilapidated wooden roof of the Ardhamandapa in the temple and plastered it with flat tiles.

cells.location: Kīlpakkam †
cells.place: On the north and west bases of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of a dancing girl by a certain Sālapapar, to the temple of Rājakulaṛ-Nāyanar Rajendrasōļa-Perumal.

cells.location: Kīlpakkam †
cells.place: On the south base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Seems to register a gift of land and refers to Kīlpakkam the eastern hamlet of Nittavinōda-chaturvēdimaṅgalam and to the god Rājāditta-Vitaṅka in the temple of Rājādittīśvara.

cells.location: Kīlpakkam †
cells.place: On the south wall of the same temple
cells.remarks: Records that the great assembly of Niyavam-chaturvēdimangalam in Mēnmali-nāḍu in Jayangoṇḍaśōḷa-maṇḍalam, having assembled in the temple of Śrīkailāsa alias Muṇai-aḍi-īśvar-amuḍaiyār in that village, borrowed 20 kaḷañju of gold from the temple of the village committee and placed in the hands of the village committee (ār-vāriyam) to supply oil, re interest on the amount borrowed.

cells.location: Chingleput — Tamil Nadu

cells.location: Nallūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Kalyāṇasundarēśvara temple

cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to record a gift of lamp to the temple of Ilangōyil-Mahādēvar.

cells.location: Naḷḷur †

cells.location: Nallūr

cells.location: Naḷḷur †

cells.location: Naḷḷur †
cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Nallūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp to (the same temple) by a certain Vaṇḍōvaraiyar.

cells.location: Nallūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of lands clubbed together under certain specified names.

cells.location: Nallūr
cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Nallūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gives a list of all the tax-free lands enjoyed by a temple whose name is not clear on the stone.

cells.location: Nallūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of a matha to the teacher called Tattanudaiyār by a lady, his disciple. Later on, the epigraph registers the grant of an additional land to the same matha.

cells.location: Chingleput † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of land to the temple by a native of Kiliyūr in Pāṇḍukulāśani-vaḻanādu. Records also the gift of a cow for a lamp, to the same temple by a certain Vađuganatha-Pillai, in the oyclic year ikkira (i.e., Vikrama P)

Unfinished. Plates missing in the beginning, in the middle and perhaps also in the end. The preserved Saneskrit portion records the grant of the village, Dayamukhamaṅgalam to 308 Brahmanas at the instance of the chief Dayamukha. The Tamil portion, of which much has been lost, mentions the waste land lying to the west of Tangattottam in Teukrai-Nayniyū-nadū of Sola-nadū. It was perhaps this land that was granted under the name Dayamukhamaṅgalam.
Plates missing in the middle and in the end. The king and his father Kamaraja boast of many conquests; see below, Part II; paragraph 67.
Plates missing in the middle. Gift of the village Vellaṅgolli surnamed Virabhūpasamudram to a number of Brahmanas, at the request of Vira-Kriabha, a Nayaka of Madura.

Provides for a gold jewel worked in a slab and pearle, from the accumulated income of a land evidently presented by Adigal Acchan, one of the junior elephant-manate (taya-kuñjiramallar?) in the army of Udaiyār-61. Raje ndra-Cholādēva commanded by Sōlamūvendavēlar, to the templof Tirunāgīsvara-Udaiyar at Tiruvippagar-Tirunagīsvar.m in Tiraimūrnādu, a sub-division of Uyyakkondār-valanādī.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 48 sheep for half a lamp to the same Mahadēva (Śiva) temple by a palace woman (pendāti) Tiran Satividangi for (the merit of) her daughter Araiyan Uttamadani (a resident) of Udaiyār-Ānaimōrūnjinār-vēlam alias Abhimānabhūshna-terinda-tiruvandikkappu-vēlam. Mentions Jananāthapuram in Tiraimūr-nādu.

cells.location: Tīrtham
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Partly damaged and built in. Registers the jewels, gold and silver vessels, etc., owned by the temple, with the permission of the king which was obtained at the request of a [temple] servant named Kandān Kōvalanādēn. Tirunāgiśvaramudaiya-Mahadēva is stated to have been situated in Tirukkudamukku in Pambūr-nādu, a sub division of Uyyakkondār[valanādu].

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Records that the assembly (mīlla-parud-tiyār) of Tirukkudamukkil received 100 kāshu from Mānikkān Māva|i alias Vikikramasīnga-Pallavaraiyan, a native of Marudam in V.nukurra-kōṭtam, a sub-division of Jayaṅgondaohōla-maṇdalam. This money was utilised by them for repairing damages caused by floods to the irrigation channel. Interest at the rate of 1 kulam of paddy on each kāshu was set apart for providing offerings in the temple of Tirunāgiśvaram-Udaiyār and for expounding the Śivadharma in the assembly hall called To uchchirrumbalamudaiyān built in the temple by the above-mentioned Vikikramsīnga-Pallavaraiyan.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine

cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Tīrtham
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Gift of land to the temple of Tirunāgiśvaramudaiya-Mahadēva at Tirukkudamukkil in Pambūr-nādu, a sub-division of Uyyakkondār-valanādu, by Narakkan Krishnan Raman of Kēr|antaka-obaturvedimangalam in Vepnādu, another sub-division of the same valanādu. The 24th and 31st years of the king are quoted in the body of the inscription. Mentions also the coin Rājēnītrasōlāy-kāshu.

cells.location: Tīrtham
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of 1½ vēli of land to the same temple by the assembly of Madāmamangulum a bruhmadēya in Tirunaraiyūr-nādu. Tiruvipnagar-Tirunāgiśvaram is stated to have been a dēvadāna in Tiraimūr-nādu. The cost of the land viz. 101 kularīju, 6mā and 1 kāshi was the fund formerly deposited for offerings by the princes Arījīgigai-Pirāṭtiyār who was a Bāna queen and the daughter of prince Arikulakēsari. An introduction of Rajadhirāja beginning with stinga|er taru is inscribed next to this; but is much damaged and incomplete.

cells.place: On the same wall

cells.place: On the north wall of the first prākāra of the same temple ..

Refers to a kalaiyīdu-lease given to the tenants, by prince, Kośalarāyar. Much damaged. Begins with the historical introduction pū-maru-viya-pojil, etc., and seems to record a gift of land.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the assembly of Si-Auṇundai to Kō.Im.y.ilai alias Parantuka-Māvendavela of Siṇṇingan in Iṅgagavo, 'feeding 20 apūrvins reversed in the Vedas and 5 Si-, ogins in the temple [śrīkkyīl] of Tirukkiljkōṭṭatti Peruma.'

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the same person for feeding 50 Brahmāņas.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. An inscription to the left of this on the same wall has its beginning built in and records a gift of land for maintaining a lamp in the temple of Tirukkalukkuṉṟamuḍaiyār.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Side of land to Kōyilmuṉṟaiyali alias Parāntaka-Mavēṇḍavēḷāṉ by the assembly of Tirukkuḍamūkkil, which he presented as a bhaṭṭavritti to those who expounded Prabhākaram (in the temple).

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 96 sheep for a lamp. Mentions Śrī-Uttamaśōḷa-Nambi-rāyār.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Quotes the 3rd year of . . . . Kēsarivarman and seems to record a gift of 70 Iṭukkāsu, for offerings.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Gift of 80 kuṭañju of gold for feeding Brahmamas.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Do. Gift of 96 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Tirukkikōṭṭattu-Mahadōva, by a certain Kāri Vijuppuraiyan.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 96 sheep for a lamp.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land by Vīraṇārāyaṇiyār, daughter of Tirukkuḷattū-uḍaiyāṉ (varma) [rājā] of Śrī-Uttamaśōḷa-Nambirāyār, for providing garlands of flowers to the temple of Tirukkuḷattū-Perumāḷ.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for lamps by two private individuals.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by a kaikkālap named [Dejvan] Rajadittan.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for lamps.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Gift of 97 sheep for a lamp by a certain Dovan Nakkan.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Sale of land by the assembly of Tirukkuḍamūkkil for maintaining a lamp in the temple of Tirukkuḷattū-Puramuḍaiyāṉ, in the name of Kōri Kōjaṉbēḻ, a Kaikkōḷaṉ.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp by Taṉuvadi Aṉiṉa Pāṇḍyavaṉ, a native of Kuruvūr in Mīḻalai-kūṟṟam, to the temple of Tirukkuḷattū-Bhaṭṭāraka.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of land for feeding a Brāhmaṇa, by a merchant of Naṉḍipuraṉ.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 kuṭañju of gold for a lamp, by Pāvan Kannan of Nedumpuraiyūr in Malai-nadu.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the end and damaged. Sale of land by the assembly of Tirukkuḍamūkkil for feeding two persons in the temple of Tirukkuḷattū-Perumāṉaḍigaḷ. Mentions Ayiratt-iṉ-kīḻa-kūṟṟam a sub-division of Teṉ-kaṉai-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by a certain Muiñjañ Kavaiyañ, a native of Aliyyāru in Tirunnapiyārnađu.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by Kađigavañ Kallāp, one of Uđaiyār-Virasōla-teriñja-Kaikkōlar.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp by Kalayan Māṇikkam, to the temple of Tirukkoṭṭai-kōṭṭatta-Perumāṇaḍigaḷ.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of land for providing a lamp and burning incense (śānti) in the temple of Tirukkoṭṭatta-Perumāṇaḍigaḷ and for maintaining two lamps in the shrine of Sūryadēvar.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of 105 pie-s of gold (tuḷaippon) by Villavan Peraraiyan alias Sīdupavan Pāṇḍan, a native of Kāvūr which was a devadāna of Āyirattali in Kijār-kūrram a sub-division of Teṇkaṇāḍu, for conducting festivals in the same temple.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged at the right end. Sale of land in Ariālar by the assembly of Tirukkudamākkil to the temple of Tirukkil-kōtťattu-[Parama]levani, for 600 kulañju of igold, in order to pay a part of 3,000 kulañju levied upon them as an impost (danđam) by Madiraikonđa-Uđaiyar in his 38th year. Mentions the army of the Pāndya (Pāndi-piđai) and (the temple of) Jalasayana.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Gift of land for providing offerings to the image of Salvappiran in the śrīvimāna (central shrine) of the temple of Tirukkoṭṭatta-Uḍaiyār, by the assembly of Tirukkuḍamukkil in Pāmbūr-nāḍu, a sub-division of Uyyakkondār-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the north wall of the manđapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a Brāhmaṇa lady, for maintaining certain festivals in the shrine of Madandāipāga-Nāyaṉār situated in the temple of Tirukkoṭṭatta-Uḍaiyār at Tirukkuḍamukkil in Pāmbūr-nāḍu, a sub-division of Uyyakkondār-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction, Grōmuni-irumūḍi-śūḍi-dēśi. Gift of land for repairs and jewels to the same shrine by a certain Kaṭṭāḍum Tiruvāṇaiśvaramuḍaiyār Madandāipāgaṉ. A gift of land by Kaṭṭāḍum Tiruvāṇaiśvaramuḍaiyār Māṇikkavāśagaṉ to the shrine of Kaṭṭāḍum Tiruvāṇaiśvaramuḍaiyār-Uḍaiyār himself in the temple of Tirukkoṭṭai-kōṭṭam-Uḍaiyār, is recorded.

cells.location: Kumbhakōnam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king: Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kōnēridēva-Mahārāja, lord of the best of towns.
cells.remarks: Registers that Tirumune (surnameḍ) Madandāipāga-Koṅgaravaṉ, son of Śeṇāyara-Māṇikkam, was granted food, house and land by the authorities managing the temple of Madandāipāga-Nāyaṉār at Tirukkuḍamukkil, a brāhmaṇadēya in Pāmbūr-nāḍu, a sub-division of Uyyakkondār-vaḷanāḍu, for the services rendered by him to the temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Records that a certain Ālvar Tiruppurambiyam Udaiyān alias Sembiyān Pallavaraiyan of Vētūr had set up an image called Tiruppurambiyam-Udaiyar in the eastern enclosure of the temple of Tirukkilkoṭtam Udaiyar and presented 17,000 kādu for offerings and lamps to that image and for a makara-tōrapa to Tirukkilkoṭtam Udaiyar.

cells.location: Sayavanam
cells.place: On the north wall of the prākāra in the Sayavaneśvara temple
cells.remarks: Records that at the instance of a certain Piđaran-Nayakan some dēvadāna lands belonging to the temple of Tiruochohāyakkad-Udaiyar at Kavirippumpatṭinam in Nangūr-nadu, a sub-division of Rajadhiraja-valanadu, were restored by the king for a flower garden, henceforward named Rajarājantirunaudavanam. The royal secretary (tirumandiraōlai) was Pānđitasōla-Mūvēndaveļān. Mentions some other officers of the king as signatories.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records the distribution of paddy collected by the temple, for offerings and for repairs, under orders of Piṇḍi Ambaraḍaiyār Kāliṅgarāyar.

cells.location: Sayavanam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land for an additional ½ lump in the temple of Tiruochohāyakkad Udaiyār, 1 ½ having been previously provided for, in the 7th year of Periyadēvar by a certain Malaimēlmaundu alias Vānavan Viļupparaiyān of Marudamangalam in Tiruvindaljur-nadu, a sub-division of Rajadhiraja-valanadu.

cells.location: Sayavanam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that certain tenants in the dēvadāna villages of the temple, did not pay their dues till the 17th year of the king and that in the 18th year they were made to sell back their holdings to the temple in payment thereof, on the representation made by Vānakóvaraiyān. The royal secretary was Rajanarāyana-Mūvēndaveļān.

cells.location: Sayavanam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Unfinished and stones out of order. Mentions KavirippūṣṣāppaŧŧiǤaṇ in Naṅguṓi-nāḍu, a sub-division of [Rājādhirāja RājanāraǤa-Ṍcānāvarādaṇ].

cells.place: On the west wall of the same prākāra
cells.remarks: Damaged. Lease of a temple land and a house to Uttarapati. Nāyayakan alias Tiruchchohayakkattalaivan, the headman of Val-nāḍu, for the supply of 8 Şārggaya ṣāṣī of pepper every day, to the temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same prākāra
cells.remarks: Damaged. Begins with the introduction pīrāndai miḍānḍu, etc.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Gift of land for presenting rice to Brāhmaṇas.

cells.location: Sayavanam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that a minister of the Chōla king named Mukunda paradipati Tiruchchigrambalavan built a matha and presented land to it for feeding 60 Brahmanas (of Śayavanam) in Pugarnagar (i.e., Kavirippumpattinam).

cells.location: Sayavanam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the temple of Śayai Nayakar, by a certain Gunakara.

cells.location: Sayavanam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Undinished. Mentions a certain Gangaikondachōlanāyan and the temple of Tiruchchirārakkadaiyār.

cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine of the Pandya Pallavanēsvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Built in at the bottom and damaged. Seems to regard a gift of land to the temple of . . . at Kaverippumpattinam in Hajadhiraja-valaṇādu.

cells.place: On a stone set up in the courtyard of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings, festivals, repairs, &c., to the temple of Pallavanicharam at Kāvērip-piņtanam in Kāvērippūmpattina-m, a sub-division of Tiruchchykattik-timul, by a Rajakiraja-valanādu.

cells.location: Tanjore — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a pillar of the kitchen in the Bṛihadisvara temple
cells.remarks: The beginning and end of the inscription are lost. (Gives the measurements of certain images made of alloy (called tars) and set with jewels. These were evidently meant to be placed in the temple.

cells.place: On another pillar built into a wall of the Chōla same kitchen.
cells.remarks: The face now exposed refers to one of the five-bodied images (pañchamurtti) at Tanjore, placed (for worship) by Raja-rājēsvaranṭu, by the king, until his 29th year.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Ghritashanchēvara temple
cells.remarks: Damaged at the beginning. Records a gift of 30 kuli-s of gold for a lamp, by a certain Sembiyan [I khattavaijan citar Parihājan Māravan Nakhan.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of 25 kalāṇju of gold for a lamp to the temple at Tiruneyttānam, by a certain Korraṇ Arumoļi alīas Vānayan Pēraraiyan. The land purchased for this amount bordered on that of Nangai Valra)guna-Perumānar, which was also purchased on account of a lamp (see No. 287 below).

cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Apparently records gifts by Kūtan Nikalankan, a member of Samarakēśari-teriñja-Kaikkōlar and by another of Vikramasīñga-teriñja-Kaikkōlar, to the temple of Mahadśva at Tiruneyttānam, a dēvadāna in Kilpilagu of Poygai-nādu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Evidently records gift to the same temple, on behalf of Mallap Araiyan], one of Samarakēsari-terinija- Kaikkōlar.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Seems to record a gift of gold for offerings in the same temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end and damaged. Gift of gold for a lamp. Mentions Kongarpervali.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for a lamp to the temple of Mahādēva by Kugavan Pundari (a native) of Kumārapāți in Paidavur-nādu, a subdivision of

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of two gold forehand-plates (pattam) to the temple at Tirunettānam by Ayan Kamakkōdapar, the superintendent of temple affairs.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 30 kalaṇju of gold for a lamp, by Nangai Šattaperumānār, a concoubine of Sōja-p'erumānadigal. The assembly of Tiruneyttānam used this amount for construoting a bathing hall (namanu-maṇdapa) to Tirunettanattu-Mahadēva, assigning instead, some temple land for maintaining the obarity.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 96 sheep for a lamp by a certain Vujavakōn Paraniyar to the temple of Tirunettāntu-Mahādēva (at Tirunettānam).

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 100 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Tiruneyttāttu- Mahādēva by Kadamba-mādēvi, wife of Vikki-Anagan on whom was bestowed the title Sembiyan Tamilavēl together with other distinguishing marks of dignity, by the Chōla king and the Chēra (Śiraman) Sthānu-Ravi.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 50 kalaṇju of gold for two lamps to the same temple, by Tenpavan Pirudimarāsan alies Kaṭti Orgiyuran and by Varagu-Perumānār, queen of Parāntaka-lāngovēlār.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of paddy for offerings by Kanantharanan, a native of Mundangudi.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Do. Gift of gold for a lamp by Kakkan Nangali of Tirunettanam.

cells.location: Tillaisthānam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by [a native] of Parāntakanapuram in Kōngu-nādu.

cells.place: At the entrance into the gopura of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Sale of land to the temple of Tirunettanam-Uđaiyar at Tirunettanam in Poygai-nādu (a sub-division) of Rajaraja-vajanadu, by two residents of the same village.

cells.location: Sulamangalam
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the central shrine in the Kritivasesvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of money for offerings to the temple [at] Sulamangalam which was a [brabmadēya] in Kiļiyūr-kūram a sub-division of Nittavinōdavalanādu.

cells.place: On the north wall of the mandapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Sale of land to the temple of Kari-uritta-Nayanar at Sulamāngalam by three Brāhmapa brothers who were natives of Tirukkudandai (i.e., Kumbahakōpam).

cells.place: On the south wall of the same maṇdapa
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Tirunaṇuđaiyar of Danavinōdanalār, a dēvadāna village of the goddess in the temple of Tiruvalavayuđaiyar (in Tayandagarkuđi-nādu a sub-division of Paṇđi-maṇdalsm), set up an image of Tirunavuđaiya-Pillaiyar in the temple of Kariyuritta-Nayanar at Sulamāngalam, a brahmadēya in Kilāy-kōṭram of Nittavinōda-vajanadu and presented lands for offerings.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Refers to the assembly of Śōlamangalam and a settlement which it made for the benefit of the temple of Kāriyirṛa-Nāyaṇār.

cells.location: Sulamangalam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king: Tribhuvanachakravartin Kulottuṅga-Choladeva [who was] pleased to take Madurai (Madura), Ilam (Ceylon), Karuvur . . . and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Sale of land servants to the temple of Kari-uriṭṭa-Nāyanar at Sōlamangalam, by two accountants of the temple of 'Irrukkurōnam-Udaiyār at Sōlakula[l]i[p]paṭṭinam, a village in Paṭṭinakkunram, a sub-division of Gēyanārikka-vaļnādu.

cells.location: Anantavaram
cells.place: On a stone in the house of the village muṆsiﬀ
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of a village to the temple of Vinaittīrtta-Tam-brānar (perhaps a temple of Anuntavarasvāmin) for bathing and offerings, by [a native of] Puliyūrkkunru (i.e., Valitīrttanā-rānasuvāmi [kōvil]).

cells.location: Kavaḷakudam
cells.place: On a stone in the Kaṅkudōtta-Vināyaka temple
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions the Mahāmāṇḍalēśvara Achiylappa-Nāyakkar-Aiyyan.

cells.location: Erukkur
cells.place: On a detached stone built into the entrance of the Pērumāl
cells.remarks: Fragment.

cells.location: Maya-vāram
cells.place: On the south wall of the mandapa of the Mayurānathasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. (Gives the latter portion of the historical introduction beginning with kāḍalśilanda.

cells.place: On the three faces of a pillar set up in the street in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Damaged.

cells.location: Valāchēri
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Daṇḍīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Tirunāvukkarasa-mudaiyā-Mahādēvu at Valāchēri, a brāhmadēya in Kōṭyūr-kōṭṭam which was a sub-division of Jayangoṇḍachōla-maṇḍa-lam, by a Brāhmaṇa lady, the wife of one of the managing (sthalattumaiyar) of the village.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land by Śēdiyarāya to the matha of Tirn-nāvukkarasan at Tiruvāmiyūr in Kulōttuṅgachōlanallur, a sub-division of Jayangoṇḍachōla-maṇḍalam. The land granted was situated at Valjchēri alias Jinachintāmaṇi-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Valāchēri
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings and lamps to the temple of Taramani-Mahādēva in the hamlet of Valichēri in Kōṭyūr-nādu, a sub-division of Polyūr-kōṭṭam. Mentions Amudan Piōchohan alias Sembiyan Kiļa-nāṭṭuppukkōṇ, a native of Vaiguhonōhēri in Kilār-kuṛram which was a district of ŚōṆādu (i.e., the Chōla country).

cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Records that the assembly of Velichēri a brahmadeya in Kōyūr-nādu of Puliyur-kōttam, sold 1,500 kuli of land to the temple at Velichēri-Mahādēva, made over to the temple as devadāna, and receiving 13 kasū made the land tax-free. Records also that 23 kāśu were presented for a lamp by a Brāhmaṇa lady of that village.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Records that two persons of Arkkaṇṭu-kūram in Sonaṇdu, purchased land from the assembly of Velichēri in Puliyūr-kōttam and presented it to the temple of Velichēri-Mahādēva for burning a lamp thereat and for providing offerings to the shrine of Ganapati built by themselves in that temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money for two lamps by the karanattīy of Velichohēri alias Jinachintamani-chaturvēdimangalam in Kōtṭūr-naḍa which was a sub-division of Puliyūr-kōṭtam alias Kulōtungasoļavalnaḍu in Jayaṅgopdachoļa-manpdalam, to the temple of Tirudandīsvaramudaiya-Nayaṇar

cells.location: Valāchēri
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by Paṭṭangati Kaļakkumara-kramavittan one of the managing members in the village of Velichēri a brahmadeya in Kōyūr-nādu which was a sub-division of Puliyūrkōttam in Jayankondachōla-mandalam, to the temple of Tirudandisvaram.

cells.location: Valāchēri
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 3rd year [date-calculation appendix, No. 309: 12th year and 125th day=Kumbha 8th day. This would mean that the king came to the throne on the 188th day (abt. 26 Sep.) of a particular year, whereas Kielhorn has found that he came to the throne between 6th and 8th July A.D. 1178.]
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the same temple. Mentions a native of Arryūr one of the villages in Vesalippadi.

cells.location: Valāchēri
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money for two lamps.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Damaged. Sale of land which was held by the non-Brahmana of Velichēri, to the temple, with the permission of the king.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the god Tirukkarrali-Mśhadēva in the temple of Tiruttandīsvaram at Velichohēri, by one of the managing members of that village.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a lamp to the image of Nayanar-Tiruchchhirambalamudaiyār set up in the temple of Tirudandisvaramudaiya- Nayanar at Velichēram, by Velichēri alias Jinasikhāmanichaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Valāchēri
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a lamp to the same temple at Vel[ich]ēri alias Jinasikhāmaṇi-chaturvēdimangalam, by a native of Kiraṅgudi in Oholamalayālam.

cells.location: Valāchēri
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Tirudaṇdīsvaradēva at Velichēri of Kōyūr-nādu of Puliyūr-kōttam, by one of the managing members of that village.

cells.place: On the south wall of the Sōliyammaṇ temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the temple of Septamatrikkal, by Tiruvetpūrudaiyan Dēvadīgal, a native of Tiruvetpūr in [Ma]la-nadu, a sub-division of Šola-nadu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of land for a lamp and offerings to the temple of Kala-Bhatari at Velichecheri in Puliyūr-kotṭam, by the assembly of that village.

cells.location: Maḍambākkam
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Dhēṇupurīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of 20 ēli of land from Maḍambākkam alias Ulaguyya-vanda[śō]la-caturvvēdimangalam, a village in Neḍunguṇra-nāḍu which belonged to Puliyūr-kōṭṭam alias Kuḷōttuṅgaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu a sub-division of Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam, to the temple of Śirrēri-Aluḍaiya-Nāyaṇār, under orders of Paḍaiyāḷi-dēvar.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records that eight house sites of the sthānattār being lost to them, fresh sites were provided for, in the street of the Kakkāḷar. Mentions Śirrēri-Aluḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at Maḍambākkam alias Ulaguyyavandaśōḷa-caturvvēdimangalam in Neḍunguṇra-nāḍu, a sub-division of Ārkkāṭṭu-kūṟṟam, a sub-division of Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam. Kuḷōttuṅgaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, in Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam. Incomplete and damaged.

cells.location: Maḍambākkam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete and damagad.

cells.location: Maḍambākkam
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of two cows for providing curds to the temple of Śirrēri-Uḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at Maḍambākkam alias Ulaguyyavandaśōḷa-caturvvēdimangalam.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Quotes the 15th year of Peruñjingadēva and records a gift of land to maintain lamps, offerings and festivals in the temple of Širrēri-Āludaiya-Nāyaṇar.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Maḍambākkam in Neḍunguṇra-nāḍu a sub-division of Puliyūr-kōṭṭam in Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam, to the same temple, by order of Aruṅgiri-Perumāḷ Nāḍu.

cells.place: On the south wall of the verandah round the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Maḍambākkam to the temple by a certain Viṭṭappar, with the permission of the king. A number of obligations and limitations were enforced on the temple.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same verandah
cells.remarks: Damaged. Sale of houses in the tirumadaiviḷagam to temple servants.

cells.location: Valuvādūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Agnīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Registers that eleven lamps were burnt by Brahmans who had borrowed small amounts of money from the treasury, in the temple of Tiruvagnīśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at Valuvādūr.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of money for six lamps to the same temple.

cells.place: On a stone set up at Muṟṟukkāḷum near the same village.
cells.remarks: Mentions Tirukkaḷukkunṟam in Kaḷattūr-kōṭṭam a sub-division of Jayaṅgoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam and perhaps also the temple of Tirumalai-Aḷuḍaiya-Nāyaṇār of that village.
