Keller; (m) Lucas L. Hemanok. 8 13 1662.

cells.place: On the wall of the temple kitchen on the same hill.
cells.date: 6th year. Details not enough for calculation. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 330]
cells.remarks: Perhaps damaged at the right end. Registers the names—'W. Silvester, H. Steed . . . . "Geo: Dawson lived in this Choy. Fm. 18. Ootr. to 9. Decr. 176 '.

cells.place: On the west wall of a ruined maṇḍapa in the north main street of the same village.
cells.remarks: Stones missing. Seems to record a gift of land and perhaps Gaṅgikoṇḍaśōļa-chaturvēdimangalam which was another name of Kaļattūr.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Munkundīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Stones damaged. Records that a merchant who was a resident of Nēduntāṇgam underar at Tiru-Mayilāpūr in Puļiyūr-kōṭṭam to the temple of Peruntirukkōyil-Mahādēva at Kaļattūr a village in Kaļattōrkōṭṭam which was a sub-division of Jayangoṇḍaśōļamaṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records that Aravindavalli a dēvadāsi of Tiruvorriyūr set up an image in this temple in image of Changdēvarasan and presented money for a lamp. Also, the merchant mentioned in No. 333 gave a lamp-stand.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the village of Sīra-Tēndalam by one of the parikkāttu-perugudai of Valudulai-Mambakkam in Valla-nādu a sub-division of Dāmar-kōṭṭam, to the temple of Avudaiya-Nāyaṇār at Kaļattūr.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money for lamps by two dancing girls

cells.place: On the same wall.
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp by a Vāṇiyan.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall.
cells.date: 13th year †
cells.remarks: Gift of land by certain dancing girls of the temple. Mentions Kajattūr alias Gaṅgikoṇḍaśōļa-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of two lamps to the temple of Peruntirukkōyil-Mahādēva at Kalattūr by a Brahmana resident of that village.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of money for two lamps.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of three lamps.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the same temple by Kankunayakan one of the Kakkāḍars of the temple. Mentions Gaṅgaikoṇḍa-śōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings by Āluđaiyanāyaka, another Kaikkōļa of the same temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land [for offerings] by Mallandai, a third Kaikkōļa of the same temple. The donors in Nos. 342 and 843 were his brothers.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land by two sisters who were the dancing girls (dēvaraḍiyāḷ) of the temple. Registers that one of these set up the image of the goddess in the same temple. Mentions Pāḷipakkam, a hamlet of Kalattūr.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers an order to the chief Toṇdaimān on the 293rd day of the year, to grant certain lands in and around Kalattūr clubbed together under the name Kulottunga-ōļa-Tiruttonđattogei-nallūr as a dėvadāna to the temple of Peruntirukkoyiluđaiya-Mahadėva for the tirumađaivilčpam and a flower garden Anapaya-Mūvēndavelaṇ is stated to have been the royal secretary (tirumandira-ōļui).

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a dancing girl (dēvaraḍiyāḷ) of the temple.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 1.152 kuļi of land by another girl of the same temple. Mentions Oļtippākkam, a hamlet of Kalattūr. Mentions Kalattūr-kōtšam and a certain Paremēšvara.

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor of the Mukha-maṇḍapa in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of 1.152 kuļi of land by another girl of the same temple. Mentions Oļtippākkam, a hamlet of Kalattūr. Mentions Kalattūr-kōtšam and a certain Paremēšvara.

cells.place: Round the Amman shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift [of the village] of Kalattūr to the temple of the Peruntirukkōyil-Nāyinār for the merit of Vīra-Narasiṅga-rāyar, by a certain Yirappa-Nāyaka, son of Vīramāy-Bhavattar.

cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Aruḷāḷapperumāḷ alias Rājarāja-Viḷuppa-rāyan constructed the shrine of the goddess and presented lands to it for the merit of his mother.

cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Tīruvalīśvara temple at Tiruvanakkōyil (near Kalattur).
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp to the temple of Tiruvalakkōyiludaiya-Mahādēva at Kalattur-kōttam, sub-division of Jayanigondasōla-mandalam, in the hamlet of Talakkur in Kulattūr-nādu, a native of Kuvalai in Vengunram-kōttam. Mentions the Kālakhu priests Gōmaddāta Jñānarāśi-Pandita and Sailārāśi-Pandita.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1320 [date-calculation appendix, No. 353: [Both Sāluva dates are the same but the 2nd is ascribed in the Annual Report to Sāluva dynasty and the 1st to Vijayanagara. In 1518-19 Aśvinī and Siddha-yōga concurred on Friday śu. 7, 7th January 1519, while Rōhiṇī and Śubha-yōga concurred on Pausha śu. 13, Dhanus-Mārgali, Tuesday 14th December 1518.]]
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the hamlet of Uttamasōlavilagam to the temple of Tiruvalakkōyiludhaiya Nayaṇar at Kalattūr, by Vēnavudhiyaṇ, one of the Kaikkōla Mudalis of the temple. It is stated that Uttamasōlavilagam was originally granted to the temple by Viru-Kaupana-Udaiyar for worship and repairs. Mentions Pundarikaṇ Rajendrasōla-Familadarniyaṇ-Atkandaṇ Mandalapurushaṇ.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 3rd year [date-calculation appendix, No. 354: Friday 28th February 1505 (= Raktākshi = Śaka 1427 current, not Śaka 1429); •56; f.d.n. •04.]
cells.remarks: Gift of 16 cows to the same temple by Mallinadaṇ Rajanarāyaṇa Śambuvaraśaṇ.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the central temple of Tiruvalakkōyiludaiya- Mahādēva, by the merchant of 'Tiru-Miyilayil; api in Puliyūr-kōttam mentioned in Nos. 333 and 334, above.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Taraṇa (= Śaka 1320). [date-calculation appendix, No. 356: Friday 3rd September 1530 (= Vikṛiti, Śaka, 1453 current not Śaka 1455); •42; f.d.n. •08.]
cells.remarks: Purchase of land at Puduppakkam by Vēnuvāduyan, one of the Kaikkōla Mudalis of the temple, perhaps for presentation to it.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 4 cows for a lamp by a native of Uprukkātu-kōttum. Mentions the two Kalamukhu priests referred to in No. 352.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Śirō-Iradalaun to the god Chandēśvarahāra at Tiruvalakkōyil by a number of people of whom was a native of Koduvur (in Pāppīna-nādu a sub-division of Sambūr-kōttam) and another, of Pāppīnam.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of the king on the 298rd day of the year, to present certain lands in the village of Arumbakkām, a suburb of Ulalar alis Rajarajānallōr in Kalattūr-kōṭṭam, clubbel together under the new name Anapayanallōr, for maintaining worship in the temple of Tiruvalakkōyiludhaiya-Mahadēva. The royal secretary was Anapaya-Muvendavelāṇ as in No. 346.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp. Mentions Gōmaddatu Śailārāśi-Pandita.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 3rd ,, [date-calculation appendix, No. 361: Saturday 16 February 1521; -54; f.d.n. -41. Note.—Saka 1444 was not yet begun, though it was at hand.]
cells.remarks: Gift of 16 cows for half a lamp by one of the Kaikkōl[ar] belonging to the temple of Tiruvalakkōyiludaiya-Nāyanar. Mentions the Kaikkōla measure Rājākēsari-nāli.

cells.location: Kaļattūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that the residents of Kalattūr-pargu gave Nariyaṇśeri alis Pundarikanallōr, a hamlet of Kalattūr to the Kaikkōla mentioned in No. 361, as a sareamānya grant.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers an order to the chief Tondaiman on the 293rd day of the year, to grant some lands in the village of Nenmali in Vallanadā, clubbed together under the new name Kulottungasolān Tirunxruohobōjanallar for maintaining worship in the temple. The royal secretary was Anapaya-Mūvendaveļān as in Nos. 346 and 359.

cells.place: On the east wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Records that the tirumadivilāgam and the surrounding lands, were given as a free tax-free grant to the a[n]dāṇar of the temple, for maintaining worship and repairs.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of land by a certain Karikalasōḷa-Tamiladaraiyan for burning a lamp on the hill north of the temple of Tiruvaiṅkar-kōyiluḍaiya-Nāyanar.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyūr
cells.place: On the east wall of the second prākāra in the Ādhipurīsvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of a cow, a bull and a calf, for a lamp to the temple of Tiru-voyirudaiya-Nāyanar, by a devotee in the Kulandaiyanvār-maḍam at Kujattūr in Veppanrū-kōṭṭam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of salt-pans in the village of Maṇali in Puliyūr-nādu as dēvadāna to the temple of Tiruvorriyūr-uḍaiya-Nāyanar [at Tiruvorriyūr] in Puliyūr-kōṭṭam of Jayangoṇḍa-sōḷamaṇḍalam, by certain persons of the-llai village. Mentions the salt-pan called Īḍaṇpakānyakapāpērajam.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Interrupted by a wall in the 'middle.' Registers that the king was present at the Rājarājan-tirumaṇḍapam, to see the Aṇi-festival of the temple of Tiruvorriyūr-uḍaiya-Nāyanar. The chief of Puliyūr-nādu in Puliyūr-kōṭṭam, sub-division of Puliyūr-kōṭṭam alias Kulōttungasōḷa-vaḷanādu being reported to be leasing waste for want of tenants, the king ordered that it may be leased out to certain persons specified in the inscription.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 buffaloes for a lamp by Āriyan Uḷiruchirambakk-uniyāyin Paduman alias Kāṭmāṇ of Kisaikkuyana to the temple of Tiruvorriyūr-Uḍaiyar [at Tiruvorriyūr] in Puliyūr-kōṭṭam, a sub-division of Vikramaśōḷa-vaḷanādu in Jayangoṇḍa-sōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 32 cows and a bull for a lamp by a certain Tiruvēṅkaṭa-chaṟaiyappan, the headman of Nuḷappiyāgu in Ambattūr-nādu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Interrupted by a wall in the middle. The king is stated to have been present on the occasion of Panguni-Uthiram festival in the temple of Padambakka-Nāyakadēva, when in the same place were also present Chōtaranana-Pandita, who owned a matha in the temple, and Āchala-tapasvi-Pandita of Aludaiyār-Tirumēni-siddhānta, hearing some dispute at Aludaiyār-Tiru-Nalattulār-dāna village Vaduguppuramhakkam being reported (to be lying waste for want of tonunta)? The king ordered it to be leased out to a certain mudaliyār from Periyur Soman.

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor, at the entrance into the sāmanya prākāra.
cells.remarks: Registration by Niravaijanagurar of Tiru-ongattur to the temple of Nayanar. The land is stated which he had constructed at that village. It is stated that the assembly of Mangali sold the land to Niraijanagurar. Mention one of the signatories whose name was Pernnialakkavadi (ivon) one of the signataries.

cells.location: Nārāyanavanam
cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of the central shrine in the Kalyana-Venkatesperumal temple
cells.remarks: Records that certain Virupaksha founded a town called Venkatādrismudram on the borders of Narayanyapuram and constructed there the temple of Venkatesa-Perumal for the merit of Venkatādirāya-Maharaya. To this temple he gave for offerings, with the permission of the king, some complete villages.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Registers an oral agreement (vākkupuram) among three private individuals.

cells.place: On a slab fixed into the floor of the mandapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Registers that Vikkiyan-Kuppan, vippaparippugam of the [Chōla] lakki facility, and two others, the chiefs of Vethiya-nādu in Kumili-Kōttam, gave certain privileges to the Vellalas of that district.

cells.place: On the inner gōpura of the same temple
cells.remarks: Gift of a village for offerings and festivals to the temple of Kalyana-Venkatesvarasvāmin of Narāyanapura, by the Mahāmandaliśvara Venkatādrināma, son of Srirangasāju and grandson of Kattari Salva Maharaja of the Kasyapa gotra and the Āpastamba-sūtra.

cells.place: On the outer gōpura of the same temple
cells.remarks: Built in at the left end. Records gift of tolls by common consent to the temple of Kalyana-Venkatesvara, by the mercantile community (viz. the chiefs of Ayyavole including persoane like Villiyan-Kappu-Nayanar) and others.

cells.place: On two detached slabs built into the floor of the Vahana-mandapa in the same temple.
cells.remarks: (Gift of tolls). Records gift of tolls by the temple of Kavalivaram-mudaiya-Nayanar at Nārāyanapuram in Uruvanguda-kottam, by the mercantile community.

cells.place: On two other detached slabs built into the same floor.
cells.remarks: Gift of 20 pock-bullooks to the temple of Kavariśyaram-Uḍaiyar, by a certain Periyapiljai alias hajanārayana-Śerekōn, one of the subordinates of Yadavaraya.

cells.place: On two detached slabs built into the mandapa opposite the main entrance into the same temple.
cells.remarks: Seems to record the gift of the village Pondejapakkam in Say-nādu for repairs and other requirements, to the temple [of Kawaramudaiya-Nayanar*].

cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Pārēsvarasvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Tamil

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor of the courtyard in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Xippatoṇgali to the priests of Kalahasti on the occasion of the kumbhāḥhihēka (i.e. the renovation) of the temple of Agastiésvara (also called Paradarésvara), by Katṭari-Salva Maharája Bommarajudéva-Maharaju.

cells.location: Kēmpulapālayam
cells.place: On the base of the central shrine in the Chōla Agastyēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of two madai for a lamp to the temple of Tiruvagatisvara-mudaiya-Nayanar at Narayanamur in Vattiyar-nādu, a sub-division of Kunnarvatthanakkottam in Jayangondachōla-mandalam by Rajanarayana-mudaliyār-Pillaigal, son of Damar-kōttam.

cells.place: On the beams of the mandapa in the Amma-nachchi Amman temple in the same village
cells.remarks: Registers that the Mahāmandalésvara Seshachalapatirājudéva-Maharája, son of Ramaraja and grandson of Jundōli-Kriebnamaraja, of the Kaśyapagōtra, repaired the Sabha-maṇdapa of the temple of Ammanachohamma (called Amnayakshi in Sanskrīt) at Naráyanapuram, the northern entrance to Kaśohipṭha.

cells.location: Karumbeedu
cells.place: On a slab in the kitchen of the Nēgēśvarasvara-svāmin temple
cells.remarks: Records that Tiruveṇgalamba, the queen of a prince of the family of Katṭari Salva Maharája built a shrine for Sōmasundarésvara and Minakshi, in the temple of Nagadhiésvara situated on the bank of the river Kuśathali.

cells.place: On a slab built into the wall of the Utsava-mandapa in the same temple.
cells.remarks: States that the mandapa was built by Tirumalatandana, wife of Mēlītuvar, the daughter of the sister of the mahādēvar Veliānji Kasuvarāja. The name of the village is given as Khathirapura on the bank of the Kussathali river.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Dēva-Vinayaka temple at Sattravada
cells.remarks: The residents of Tirani-nādu in Nedu nadu, and others gave to certain Melituvars, the village of Tirani as a rudrappattu to be fabricated to the Dēva-māvala temple at that place. This refers to the events of Sīnisi-damayakkattar and Vira-kōdiyar from entering it.

cells.place: On a slab set up at the side of a wall in the Vijaya-samssame village.
cells.remarks: Records a charter granted to the Sēnis by Daiyav Sriranga-Rāvnular.

cells.place: On the east wall of the mandapa in front of the central shrine of the Chidambareśvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Built in at the bottom. Mentions the Śaiva and Vaishnava shrines of Chandragiri-rājya viz. Kāñohipuram, Tirukkajatti. Tiruvorgiyur, Tiruvalangaḍu Tiruppalaivanam and others. Refers to the vidhati-kāṇithkai collected in the temple of Alagiya-Tiruchohirrumbalamudaiya-Nayaṇar at Sattirapadi in Maṅgalār-naḍu, a sub-division of Kungre[vattankō]ṭtam in Jayaṅgondachola-maṇdalam and to certain royal jorders (rḍyasam) issued to Ariyappa Daṇdayaka, Bhikshavṛitti-Ayyagal and Dēvarāya-Udaiyar of Chendragiri.

cells.place: On the west and north walls of the Varada-rāja-Perumal temple in the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1459, Hēvilambi. [date-calculation appendix, No. 390: 12th year. A.D. 1144; Wednesday, November 8; f.d.t. ·15; ·53.]
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions Mangalur-nādu, a sub-division of Nayanarsppurapura in Kunravattana-kōttam of Jayangonda-chōla-mandalam.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the main street in the same village.
cells.date: Friday 26th November 1546. Śrāvana commenced at •95. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 391]
cells.remarks: Registers that Gaṇḍaragaṇi Maraya-nāy-i-tkar son of Mahāpradhāni Sōmaya-Dēnnāyaka gave to the temple of Alagiya-Tiruch-chhirrambalamuḍaiya-Nāyanār, a piece of land with the right to take water from the tank of Vaaarāyappamal [nē]rt.

cells.location: Kuruvēnganār
cells.place: On detached slabs round the central shrine in the Tiruvēnganatha-Perumal temple
cells.remarks: The fragments appear to have included this and two other records concerning a gift of land by the same person. It was registered gifts of land to the Siva temples at Varayarapuram in Sēda, a sub-division of Kuṇyavattana-kōṭṭam. Some of the temples mentioned are Avimuktisvaramuḍaiya-Nāyanār, Laksmiēśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyanār and Akkasālēsvaramuḍaiya-Nāyanār. Mention o. certain Vira-Narasingadēvan alias Vairāvarāyar. Also a fragment is found of an unnamed Saiva king.

cells.location: Sēnūr
cells.place: On the north wall of the Agastyēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of two villages to the temples of Tiruvengatāṇamudaiya- Nāyaṇār and Paohchhavana-Perumāl as Sēnallur for repair and worship.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged and mutilated. Seems to contain portions of a historical introduction. Copied from a palm-leaf copy of a stone and copper-plate inscription recording gifts of land to the temples of Tiruvangadēva and Tirumandēvam, on account of the drummers who beat drums during the śrī-bbali ceremony.

cells.location: Aḍaipalam
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Kalakaṇṭhēsvara temple
cells.remarks: Registers that Appai-Dīkshita constructed the temple.

cells.location: Mullandram
cells.place: On the south wall of the Svayambhūnathēvara temple

cells.remarks: Gift of land by a Brahamaṇa lady to the shrine of Aruṇachalainatha built by her, in the temple of Svayambhunatha for the merit of herself and her husband Kumarar-Dīdhimar Appamalainathar.

cells.location: Aṭṭirala

cells.remarks: Gift of 1 maḍai for a lamp to the temple of Tiruvirāniśvaradeva at Aṭṭirala, a brahmadēya in Pulinādu, a sub-division of Adhirājendrachōla-mandalam, by a native of Nenaṭṭukku.

cells.place: On the outer prākāra wall of the same temple.

cells.remarks: Gift of 12 madai for lamps by the wife of Poungunraṇi Vattreddi, to the temple of Parasurāmisvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at Tiruvayatturai, in Pottappinādu, a sub-division of Mōr-Pakkai-nāḍu in Adhirājendramandalam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 2 māḍai for providing a flower garland to the same temple (here called Tiruviramiśuramudaiya-Nāyaṇar).

cells.location: Aṭṭirala
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: (Gift of 12 maḍai for a lamp to the shrine of Vairavapillaiyar at Tiruvayatturai by a native of Puḍōli.

cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Aṭṭirala
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 15 madai for lamps and garlands to the temple of Parasāranārāyana-Nāyanar, by a native of Mandappalli.

cells.place: On a slab set up at the ruined main entrance into the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records an agreement by the residents of the Pottappi-nādu district who had met in the mandapa called [Chitramēli] to raise 1 madai from each village in order to construct an embankment on the side of the river and to prevent any injury from floods to the temple of Parasāranārāyana-udaiya-Nāyanar.

cells.place: On another slab set up in the same place
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Registers that Apnamarusayya came to Araturevulu, enquired into the affairs of the [Kritri]svara. Parasurameśvara and the Bhayirava temples and seeing that the income had been stopped in the interval, restored the temple lands at Proli, for the merit of king Naraśingayyadeva-Mahārāja.

cells.place: On a third slab lying broken in the same place.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentione among others, the districts Yeguva, Pottapinaṇu and Maliki-naṇu and the temple of Parasurameśvara at Araturevula-mahārthana. Refers to a number of tanks, canals and villages founded and called after either the name of the king or one of his birudas.

cells.location: Pōli
cells.place: On the south wall of the Śiva temple
cells.remarks: Gift of 1 madai for a lamp by a certain Reddi, to the temple of Kalyana-Uliyakānyar at Pūdōli in Mer-Pakkal-nādu, a sub-division of Adhirājēndra-mandalam.

cells.place: On the east wall of the Vardarājasvāmin temple in the same village.

cells.place: On the same wall

cells.place: On a slab set up in the courtyard of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. The king has a long list of birudas.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the south wall of the same temple.

cells.date: 27th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 448: 13th year of (?) See paragraph 19 of Part II of the Report. The eclipse was presumably one coinciding with Nak. Pūrva-Bhādrapadā. The indication is that of a solar eclipse. Such a coincidence can only take place at the end of ordinary lunar Māgha; while a coincidence of Nak. Pūr.-Bhādrapadā with a lunar eclipse can take place in ordinary lunar Āśvina. It is curious that a coincidence of each of the two kinds took place in the 13th year of one Pāndya, viz., Māyāvarman Kulasekhara. The first kind of coincidence took place in A.D. 1281, Thursday, February 20; •34; •75. The second kind of coincidence took place in A.D. 1280 on Monday, September 9 ; f.d.t., •38 ; •73.]

cells.location: Urkud
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōshthīppar temple
cells.remarks: Built in, in the middle and in the right end. Gift of land to the shrine of Kahētrapala in the temple of Tirukkōṭhiśaviocha[ra]m-Udaiyār. Begins with the introduction pūviz kilatti, eto.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of land for maintaining a flower garden called Sundarapandiyan-tirunandavanam after the name of the king, to the temple at Rajaraja-chaturvādimaṅgalam in Mull-nādn, at the instance of Malavarāyaṇ. On this occasion some other lands owned by the temple were also made tax-free (iraiyili).

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Built in the middle and damaged. Refers to the gifts mentioned in Nos. 519 and 520 and to the temple of Tirukkuṭṭiśvaran Udaiyār.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Records that a certain Pallichchai Vikramāditya Adichchadēvar alias Aḻagiyār of Malai-maṇḍalam completed the building of the temple of Tirakkōṭṭi-Īśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār, which had been left unfinished.

cells.location: Kiḷachchēval
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Veṅkaṭachalapati temple
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Gift of land (made tax free) to a certain Kanaviniya Perumajdasar, by a native of Karittyaii in Malai mangdalam. The temple is referred to as Kapaviniya-Pandiya Vinnagarajvar at Tep Tiruvayottiyai. The document is signed by a number of offiners in 'the department of taxes.'

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king: Māṛavarman alias Tribhuvana achakravartin Sundara Pāṇḍyadēva.
cells.date: 11 + 3rd [date-calculation appendix, No. 524: (= 1540-41). Apparently an error in week-day.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction pimalar tirusemm, etc. Refers to the same Kanaviniya Perumajdasar who was maintaining the flower garden named Viradēkharan tirunanduvanam, and to the land granted to him at Dēsimāpikkanallār.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: The same formulae as in the previous numbers are repeated. Refers to the order of the king made at the request of Aṇṇan Tamilappallavaraiyan, perhaps, recorded here.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Records a gift of land to the Śiva temple of the same place and worthy with the permission of [Paṇṇaiyā-kaṇ]. The land was made tax free (iraiyili) by the king, at the request of Gāṅgēyarāyaṉ, chief of Tañjāvūr.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Records that Tiruppulanidasar of Sēravum-mahadevi ohaturvēdimangalam having built the temple of Kapaviniya Perumal, a certain Pamuiyakkan had endowed it with the necessary land (nattam) required for temple buildings, gardens, and the Brahmana village called Tentiruvayottiyai. At the request of Gāngēyarayan, chief of Tuñjalor, the king made the nattam under reference, tax free (iraiyili). At the end of this record is engraved another of the 8th year of the king, which refers to the same temple and to the Brahmana village Tentiruvayottiyai-vilagain.

cells.location: Iḷañji
cells.place: On the west wall of the Iśvaramuḍaiya shrine in the Kumārakōvil temple
cells.remarks: States that the temple was restored from the foundation to the pinnacle by 'king' Aḷagan Kuḷaśēkharadēva.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: The claim of a certain priest in the temple of Iravikku-Īśvara-muḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Iḷañji alias Sundarapāṇḍyanallūr in Teyvāri-nāḍu being overlooked by the [king's] elder brother on the ground of the priest having been distributed among these others in the kin, while also in the Śiva temple of Tirukkōṭṭi-Īśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār, decided on the representation made by the priest's sons, that a fourth share must be restored to the original claimants.

cells.place: On the south wall of the mandapa in front of the Subrahmanya shrine, in the same temple.
cells.remarks: The king while encamped at Vāsudēvanallūr in Iḷaṅgai-nāḍu, was pleased to grant land for lamps to be burnt in the temple of Tiruppuḍaimarudūr-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Sundarapāṇḍyapuram, there being none of the Śivadvija (Śivadvija) community at that place to undertake the work.

cells.location: Śērmādēvi
cells.place: On the north wall of the first prākāra in the Bhaktavatsala temple
cells.remarks: Stones out of order and damaged. Seems to record a gift of money and mentions Śērmādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam. The same wall refers to a gift of old and to the Mahābhārata-vṛtti, one of the requirements provided for, in the temple.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same prākāra
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of money for a lamp to the god Paramasvāmin was pleased to stand in the temple of Bhaktapriya at Śērmādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya in Muḷi-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 6th ,, [date-calculation appendix, No. 533: Sunday, 23rd October 1222 (= -26 Tulā)—Read 26 Tulā.]
cells.remarks: Gift of one āṭai-achu to the temple of Bhaktapriya. Emierum at Śūravaṇamāchaturvēdimangalam by Kōvittan-Śūrabhadra, a native of ... in Meḷ-Vēmbanāḍu.

cells.location: Śērmādēvi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of money for a lamp by a Brāhmaṇa lady.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same prākāra
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of money for a lamp by Vaṅgipuraṭṭu Mādhava-bhaṭṭa of Jaina-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of money for a lamp by a resident of Tirunelvēli in Kil-Vēmba-nāḍu.

cells.location: Śērmādēvi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: [18] + 1st ,, [date-calculation appendix, No. 537: Wednesday 30th July 1292. Simha not Mina. śu. 15 not śu. 5 and Nak. Śrāvana ended at -80 and -09 respectively. Note.—Tamil ū indicates tithi may be read as Paurnami or pañchamī indifferently.]
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of oil for maintaining 20 lamps.

cells.location: Śērmādēvi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete and damaged. Refers to the gift of the image of goddess to the temple and mentions Aṉaimēṉiṉrār.

cells.location: Śērmādēvi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 sheep for a lamp.

cells.place: On the north wall of the second prākāra of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers that a piece of land granted for a garden was made tax-free at the request of Kaliṅgarāyar. Mentions Ariōchandraṉ alias Pallavarāyaṉ of Śēluvattūr in Tirukaḷappōr-kōṭṭam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records the gift mentioned in No. 540 and mentions Aiochandraṉ alias Pallavarāyaṉ of Śēluvattūr.

cells.location: Śērmādēvi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that the land granted by a certain Sundara-Pandya Brahmadhirayaṇ for lamps, was made tax-free.

cells.location: Śērmādēvi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of land mentioned in No. 542 and the order of the assembly of Śēravaṉmahādēvi chaturvēdimaṅgalam, to utilise the income from the land for lamps.

cells.place: On the east wall of the same prākāra
cells.king: Jaṭāvarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Vīra-Pāṇḍyadēva. [He conquered the Kongu and Sōla-maṇḍalam, conquered the powerful chiefs] and was pleased to perform [the anointment of heroes and victory] at Perumbara-ppuliyūr.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers the gift mentioned in No. 540 and perhaps also another gift of land to supplement it, under the orders of the assembly of Śōravanmādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam. The taxon on this land are stated to have been deducted in the account registers.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Sunday, 26th March 1187; f. d. t. .39—Suits 9th year only. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 545]
cells.remarks: Registers a eulogistic poem in praise of the king.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same prākāra
cells.remarks: Records that a native of Irāyiravaiyūr was required to provide for the navarātri-festival in the temple on receiving from the assembly of Śrīvaikunṭham, a specified piece of land.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Refers to the same gift and to the permission supposed to have been granted by the god.

cells.place: On a lion-pillar in the gōpura of the same temple.
cells.date: 26th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 548: Wednesday, 12th August 1271 ; •62; f.d.n. •10.]
cells.remarks: Registers that [the gift] of Kīlakkīla Padma-nābha-Bhuṭṭanōṇṇaiyin.

cells.location: Kōvilkuḷam
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Tenṇalagar temple
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a festival, to be celebrated each month on the Śravaṇa-nakshatra, in the temple of Śrī-pattirivīra-Eṇbōruman at Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam, a brāhmaṇa-dēya in Muḷi-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 2+19th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 550: Wednesday 22nd May 1230; f.d.t. -37; f.d.n. -10]
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Tiruppuṇṭi-yil-Vīṇāgari.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of 25 sheep [for] a lamp, to the temple of Tiruppuṇṭi-yil-Vīṇāgari [for] a lamp, by Kujam in Maḷi-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 sheep [for] a lamp, by Nayabēnakki, the wife of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Kōvilkuḷam — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of money for a lamp.

cells.location: Kōvilkuḷam — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of land for offerings to the temple of Śrīpattirivīra Āḷvār at Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Aḍaichōṇi — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone lying near the sluice of the tank
cells.remarks: Gift of privileges in respect of tanks and ponds to the residents of the village—Tippanatturayan, for the merit of Muttavirappa-Vēḷār.

cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the Kuḍal-Aḷagar temple
cells.date: 14th year, Śaka 1537 and Kollam 792. [date-calculation appendix, No. 556: Regnal year may be 32nd or 39th, i.e. 1210 or 1217 A.D.]
cells.remarks: Records that stones were supplied for the building of the Ardha-maṇḍapa and the garbhagṛiha of the Kuḍal-Aḷagiya-Perumāḷ-temple, by Kaṇḍaḍai Kōṇamman, for the merit of Kaṇḍaḍai-Aṇṇan and states that the work was finished during the administration of Vēḷār. It also mentions Rājēndra-Chōḷadēva-Mahārāja and his subordinate Timmappa-Nāyakkar [son of] Yāśavanta-Nāyakkar.

cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of the central shrine in the same temple.
cells.date: 14th year, Śaka 1537 and Kollam 792. [date-calculation appendix, No. 557: Saturday, 17th July 1210; but no week day in inscription.]
cells.remarks: Damaged and unfinished. Gift of money and a house for offerings to the same temple by Yāśavanta-Nāyakkar Timmappa-Nāyakkar.

cells.location: Teṅkāśi, Tenkāsi taluk, Tinnevelly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Gift of three villages for offerings and festivals to the temple of Kûdûl-Alagiya-Perumâl by Timmappa-Nâyakkar, son of Vâla-vana-Nâyakkar for the merit of Ramarâja-Vitthaladeva-Maharaja.

cells.location: Teṅkāśi, Tenkāsi taluk, Tinnevelly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a pillar set up in the Collector's bunga-low in the village.
cells.remarks: Registers that a certain Innamottideva of the Nandikêśvara-dēva-sannidhāna in the Amurudâ-matha, built in the name of Annan-tîrthasâstâra in Vadagarai Varagavâi-pattinam in Mulik-kudindu, a matha called Manpperiya-madam and endowed it with 10 md of land, which the king made tax-free (iraiyili).

cells.place: On one of the stone beds in a second cavern on the same hill.
cells.date: Thursday 23rd May 1230; -37; -10 same tithi and nakshatra. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 563]
cells.language: Vaṭṭe-luttu (verse) †
cells.remarks: Registers the several acts performed by a certain Pallidaraiyan, while he was in the service of the Pandya king (Vatud-Mînavan).

cells.location: Pulip-patti
cells.place: On a rock near the Ayyar temple
cells.language: Vatteluttu. (verse) †
cells.remarks: Damaged and damaged. Seems to record the gift (the village) Sîrvalkulam to Poliyundaya-Nâyenar by (the residents?) of Padikkadi, in Teyyappu-nâdu.

cells.location: Periyapatnam — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On four slabs kept in the courtyard of a mosque
cells.remarks: Examined by Dr. J. Horovitz, Ph. D., Epigraphist for Moslem inscriptions, Aligarh; see below, Part II, paragraph 74.

cells.location: Tenkasi — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Viśvanāthasvāmin temple

cells.location: Tenkasi — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Refers to the gift of the village of Kāśikkuvāykkanallūr founded by the king in Kurumaṟai-nāḍu, as a dēvadāna to the temple, in his 33rd year.

cells.location: Krishnapuram, Tinnevelly taluk, Tinnevelly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end; gives a eulogistic account of the king and of his building the Viśvanātha temple and refers also to his gift of the dēvadāna villages Teṉkāśi, Parākramapāṇḍyanallūr, Vīrapāṇḍyanallūr and others.

cells.location: Krishnapuram, Tinnevelly taluk, Tinnevelly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Registers that the king on his birthday (Mṛigaśīrsha) established a special service in the temple to be called Parākramapāṇḍi-yaṉśandi and made a gift of the villages Teṉkarai-Karikuṟichchi and Piḷḷaiyārkuḷam, for its maintenance.

cells.king: Jaṭilavarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Parākrama-Pāṇḍyadēva [alias Kulaśēkharadēva] 'born on the asterism Kārttigai.'

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of houses and shares in the village of Vira-Pāṇdya-ohaturvēdimaṅgalam to 24 Brahmapas for reciting the Vēdas, reading the Pañohāṅga (the Indian Calendar) and the Purāṇas as already made (but on a smaller scale) in the Śaka years 1869, 1878, 1382 and 1884.

cells.place: On the same walls ..
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Refers to lands granted to Brahmaṇas, who had to recite the Vēdas in the temple of Viśvanātha at Teṉkāśi alias Vīra-Pāṇḍya-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Teṉṉāri-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tenkasi
cells.place: On the same walls ..
cells.remarks: Grant by common consent to the temple of Viśvanāthaṉ, of a certain quantity of paddy from lands harvested for kār and paśāṉam, by the agriculturists of Kurumaṟai-nāḍu, Teṉvāri-nāḍu, Vaḍavāri-nāḍu and Kuṟṟila [mai]-nāḍu on the Śiṟṟāṟṟaṅgarai.

The money was distributed among 16 villages which were required only to pay interest at 2 kulam of paddy per year on each kātu borrowed, without disturbing the principal.

These were: (1) the stone prākāra wall, (2) the eastern and the southern gōpuras, (3) the guies (?), (4) the kitchen and the southern varandah in front of it, (5) the assembly hall, (6) the paving of the courtyard, (7) the ranga-maṇṭapa for Bāna, Lakshmaṇa, Bhairava, Vighnēśvara, etc.

cells.location: Gorrepalle — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: A copy of the deed by which Matikadahaļi surnamed Mahalakshmipura was granted to the temple of Mahālakshmi by Timmiawa son of Apparsa, of the treasury, at the instance of Tirumappayya of Penugonde.

cells.location: Gorrepalle — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift by Peda-Chinnappa-Nāyaka [sati] surnamed Lakshmikaṇṭam in Antayanna Kodagahalli-sthala, of Guyyuluru-sime in Rod[d]anādu which was a district of Penugonde-aīya, to the same temple by Krishnappa-Nāyaka son of Sani Chinnappa-Nāyaka at the instance of Virappannayya.

cells.location: Gorrepalle — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that the above documents were caused to be engraved (vyavahāra) by Sēnābōva of Chau[da]ppanayya, Timmayyanṇa's clerk (sēnābōva) Timmayya of Gōrepalle with the approval of Viraprunayya of Penugonde.

cells.place: On stone beams in the Iśvara-temple at Chola Moda.
cells.remarks: Contains the major portion of the historical introduction beginning with tirumanni vaļara.

cells.location: Konakoṇḍla — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Bhōgīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Much damaged. The king receives the title samastabhuvan-āśraya 'the asylum of the whole world'. Mentions Āḍapa-Nāyaka and Koṇḍakuṇṭe (i.e., Konakoṇḍla).

cells.location: Vānavōlu, Hindupūr taluk, Anantapur district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab built into the wall of a private house in the same village.
cells.remarks: The Mahāpradhāna [Ko]ṭṭeya Māchaya-Daṇṇāyaka was ruling at Penugoṇḍeya-nelavīḍu and gave the village of Benagūru as a koḍagi gift to a certain gauḍa.

cells.remarks: Mutilated. In archaic characters. Mentions in the beginning a certain Mahārājādhirāja whose name is not clear on the impression. Registers perhaps the gift of the village of Vennaṅgūru.

cells.location: Parigi — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On two fragments of a slab near the Honnaṭikamma temple
cells.remarks: A piece of stone is, evidently, missing in the middle. Records the presentation of a bell to the temple of Bhīmēśvara at Guruguñjikōla-bayalu [below] the tank of Haruve (i.e. Parigi) in Haruve-nāḍu and the gift of 800 . . . of land measured by the rod called drōharamalla, for oblations, lamps, etc.

cells.location: Kaggallu
cells.place: On a slab set up in a garden
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register the gift of the village of Kaggallu surnamed Ti[mma]samudra to the temple of Mallikārjuna.

cells.location: Pulaguṇṭa
cells.place: On the Garuḍakambha in front of the Āñjanēya temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the pillar by a bōya.

cells.location: Chōḷasamudram
cells.place: On the wall, right of main entrance into the Chauḍēśvari temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the building of the temple of Chauḍēśvari-Amma at Chōḷasamudra and to a tax fixed on each loom (magga), by Timmarasu and others.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the courtyard of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Registers a gift to the temple of Chauḍēśvari at Chōḷasamudra, by Rāyasa[m] Koṇḍamarasayya, son of Timmarasamantri who was one of the sons of Śilpatyāchārya, chief of Poḍatūru in Draviḍa-dēśa and the ornament of the Udayagiri-Kannaḍiga sect. The gift was made in order that the king may be blessed with children.

cells.location: Lēpākshi
cells.place: On the wall of the verandah round the Vīrabhadra temple
cells.remarks: Gift of Chikanandicheruvu surnamed Dēvarāyapura, a village near Doppaṟu in Sadali-sthaḷa of Chalūrachāvaḍi to the temple of Vīrēśvara on the Kūrmaśaila hill at Lēpākshipura, by Vīrapaṇṇayya of Penugoṇḍe. It is stated that the donor purchased it from four Brāhmaṇas who had acquired the village as a sarvamānya grant from king Prauḍhadēva-Mahārāya.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that half of the village of Sadadavipura surnamed Devarayapura also near Depparu, was purchased from two Brahmans and granted to the same temple by Virapannayya. As in the previous instance the Brahmans had acquired it from Pradhānēdēva-Mahāraya.

cells.location: Lēpākshi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of some vritti-lands in the sērumāṇdya-agraāra Nüvängere known as Kuhmaryasudru, to the same temple, by Virangappanayyan and his brother Virana-Nāyaka. Nagaragere is stated to have belonged to Tum[bo]kallasthala in Roddanādu which was a sub-division of Penugonde-rajya.

cells.place: On a slab set up at the entrance into the Isvara temple at Gorantila .
cells.remarks: Registers that Sînarajata, the agent of Vakiti Adealpa-Nayaningāru freed the Tummala servants of the temple of Sūnesvara at Gōraṇṭla from supplying leaves (used in eating food) to that temple free of cost, on the condition that they repaired the temple, built the sikhara and constructed a compound wall of mud

cells.place: On a slab lying in the Madhavarāyasvāmin temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Records that a certain king Narasimha of the Saluva family built the temple of Vishnu. His ancestors had the birudas Madināgaṇḍa-Gōpāla Krishṇa-Raya-Saluvu and Dhanagarshana.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab lying in a field at Vanavolu .
cells.remarks: Begins abruptly and states that Gangasa[ni]daughter of Payiđiseṭti of Pāmiđi entered into the fire (i.e. performed sutise) at Penugonđa. To her memory [was, perhaps, erected f] a bīn-idevana at Vanavo[lu].

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.remarks: Krishṇarāya's rule never extended so far. Registers that Yadava Narasimharāju, Hamalingandohari, Kannapali, Peddavi Nayudu and Chinadovi Nayudu, Kaipa Basavajulu and Nala'enkappareddi of Kasanuru paid their shares towards clearing with 60 varahas and received certain offices and service-inams in the village of Iómada. The inscription specifies the mēra, mirā and other income due to the servants of that village.

Registers that two Reddis of the Frommanayaka family sold to the anattu and children to the village Havulakollu and got permission to construct a village near the hill, by Yara-Timmaraja who was then governing Ghaṇḍikōṭa. Its boundaries, ore division and service-inams are settled. The grant was written by Teliki Bala-Batuŋu.

cells.remarks: The car festivals at Conjeevaram of the gods Ekāmrēśvara and Ādipurīśa were attended by several chiefs including an officer of Haradā Aṇavarādkānu-Nāyappu i.e., Hazrat Anvarādin Khān Ṣāhēb P). They found on that occasion that some-thing was wrong with the movie glory of the images. The cause of this not known they onsulled one Kanumanuru Rangāchārya. The latter by his magical powers put right and got from the chiefs the privilege of collecting certain specified annuities from different classes of people living in the 56 countries.

cells.remarks: This is a document which professes to settle certain disputes between Baḍugulavaru and Painan-viruḷu, in regard to certain paraphernalia used during public processions. The judges, evidently, were the Śaivas, Vaishnavas and other great men of Conjeevaram.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.remarks: The boundaries of the village Keūntāru which was a surname of Tiruvenga]anellār in Gutti-rajya, are first described. Then follow details of mēra, mirdī and other service-inams granted to village servants. This record pretends to belong to the reign of Praudhadēva-Māharaya (Śaka 1371 to 1887). Incomplete. The genealogy of the Karṇata kings with which the inscription begins, is identical with that given in the Kallakursi grant of Kāṅga VI, as far as Venkuṭa II. The sew] bears the legend īrī-Venkaṭāsa.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Provides for a flower-garland and offerings by Oṙṙi-araşan son of Paiyūrāṇḍalvāł Vājapeyam-āiyāł, who is evidently identical with the donor mention-ed in No. 108 above.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 buffaloes (for a lamp) and a lamp-stand (shaped like himself) to Tiruvorryar-Udaiyār, by Tiruvarahgam-Udaiyān alias Danmaparipalān Kajadhiraja Malaiyarāyān, son of Mugaiyadaraiyān alias Kulottunga-Cholad-Malaiyarayān of Naduvilmalai Tirunedumpirai in Perumār-nādu, a sub-division of Manavil-kottam. Records also the gift of 12 buffaloes (for a lamp), a similar lamp-stand and a silver bugle (kālam) to the goddess Āludaiya-Nachchiyār. The lamp-stands were called Daṇma-paripālaṇ after the donor.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 26th year, Tula 28rd day, ba. di. 14, Āśvati, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Gift of 82 ewes for a lamp and a lamp-stand of two flats, by a resident of Velur which was a devadaya village of the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 82 ewes for a lamp by one of the worshippers in the same temple, named Suryadevan alias Vyākarana[pdna-bhatta.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.date: 10th year, Kapṇi, ba. di. 5, Saturday, Pusam.
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 ewes and two rams for a lamp, by Perumāl- Nachchi senior queen of prince (pillaiyar) Pañchanaḍīvayan Nilagaṅgaraiyan.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Tiruvorriyur-Uḍaiyār at Tiruveriyur in Pulal-nādu, a sub-division of Rajendrasōla-valanādu in Jayangoṇḍaśōla-maṇdalam, by Seyyān Orriyikoṇḍan son of Orriyiyur alias Solyavallava-Muvendavelar, a native of Īppūru in Purashigaram-bal-nādu, district of Sola-maṇdalam.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by Madamadall Īlāṇamarti Paṇditas alias Madurāntaka-Brahmanadirājan of Vatar-gāru, a native of Nalur and the commandant of forces (senāpati) of Chakravartin Kulōttuṅga- Chōladeva.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Kulappakkam alias Śivapādaśekharanallur in Puliyur-kōttam alias Kulōttuṅgasōla-valanādu and of gold ornament to the god Vyākarapadāna-Perumāļ and his consort, at the request of a female mendicant called Tiruviyur-ammai. The king is here referred to as Ulaguyyavandar.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp to the god Śiva at Ādhipura by Jñānamūrtiā alias Madhurāntaka, perhaps identical with the military officer mentioned in No. 119 above. Published in Ep. Ind. Vol. V., p. 206.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 19th year, Simha, su. di. 3, Utiraṭṭādi, Sunday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 122: 1913.]
cells.remarks: Gift of five women and their descendants for husking paddy in the temple, by Vayalarviļavan alias Vēgambaṇ-Uḍaiyān Sōndamanikkappan alias Vayirādarayan, a native of Virugaṇpakkam alias Sempinallur in Peru-nādu, a sub-division of Pulali-nādu alias Kulōttuṅgachōḷa-valanādu which was a district of Jayangonḍachōḷa-maṇdalam.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 96 ewes for 3 lamps by Kulōttuṅgachōḷamahipāla, son of Āy-arar-nāḍuvan, a native of Eyilnārmil Amur alias Cholendrasiṅganallur-palli in Paiyyr-kōttam a sub-division of Vikkiramasōḷavaḷanādu in Jayangonḍasōla-maṇdalam.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp and 90 sheep by a native of the Chola country named Araiyan Kljāndraśōlan alias Rājasekhara-Mūvēndavēlar.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king: Parakesarivarman alias Trihuvanaohakravartin Ulaguyyavanda-Perumal (i.e. Kulottuṅga III).
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Refers to a certain Pugal-nārāyaṇa of Karuveli in Mililai-kūrram in Pāṇdi-nādu, who received from the king, while the latter was encamped at that place, the chiofship of Pommārun in Kalavāy-nādu, a sub-division of Palliyar-kōttam in Jayangoṇḍachōla-maṇdalam, which was a division of Tondai-maṇdalam.

cells.place: On the south base of the same shrine
cells.king: Parakesarivarman alias Trihuvanaohakravartin Ulaguyyavanda-Perumal (i.e. Kulottuṅga III).
cells.remarks: Records that the vimana (i.e. the central shrine) was built by the architect Ravi alia: Vira-Chola at the bidding of Chaturangana and under the auspices of Rajanīra-(Chola I), son of Rājarāja.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Records that for the merit of the temple's first Brahmana lady, Ariyavammal wife of Prabhattar Bhatta of Markāṇdāpura in Arya-dēsa, for the purpose of feeding the Mahēśvaras in Rajasekharan which was evidently a matha built by her in the temple.

cells.place: On the west base of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Built-in. Records that some waste land in Śiṅgapura-chaturvedimangalam was reclaimed by the order of the king and being named Vīravajandravalagam after the king, its produce was utilized for services in the temple.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the assembly of Kurattur in Ambattar-nādu, a sub-division of Puḷal-kōttam for conducting the daily services in the temple of Tiruvorriyur-Uḍaiyar Karināi-Viṭaṅkadevar. Tiruvallivāy is stated to have been a village in Tuḍamugi-nādu, a sub-division of Puliyur-kōttam.

cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Registers that Kuḷāmuḷār Ēraṉ Kuttaṉār alias Rājarāja-Mūvēndavēḷār, an officer (adhikāri) of the king held an enquiry into temple affairs in the maṇḍapa called Rājarājaṉ (within the temple) and assigned some money for the service called Vīrarājēndraṉ-tiruppaḷḷi-eḻuchchi.

cells.place: On the west and south bases of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of lands by purchase, by the military officer (sēnāpati) Rajarājan Paraņiparak-hasaņār alias Virasōla-Iļaņgöveļār, in order to conduct the service called [Tiruchohān] dāđal of the god Karaņai-Viťankadēvar. The lands were purchased in five different villages. Partly published in South-Ind. Invers. Vol. III p. 182.

cells.place: On the same bases ..
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land by the assembly of the brahmadēya villages of Sundaraśōḻa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam and Vaṉavaṉmahādēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam. It was purchased by Nāgalavvaichchāṇi alias Āriyammai wife of Prabhākara-Bhaṭṭa a resident of Megalapuram in the Ārya-dēśa and a devotee of the temple of Tiruvoṟṟiyūruḍaiya-Mahādēva. The purchased land was given to the maṭha called Rājēndraśōḻaṉ which was built by that lady. Records also other sales of land to the same lady and for the same purpose, by the residents of Eṇṇūr in Navalūr-nāḍu which was a sub-division of Puḻar-kōṭṭam and by the merchants (nagarattār) of Tiruvoṟṟiyūr in the years 31 and 27 of the same reign, respectively.

cells.place: On the north base of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the residents of Eṇṇūr in Navalnāḍu a sub-division of Puḻar-kōṭṭam for midday services in the temple and for feeding a Brahmaṇa learned in the Vēdas and a Śivayōgin, the money being paid by the officer Ādittaṉ Tarparamporuḷār alias Madurāntaka Mūvēndavēḷār a native of Ariḍayamaṅgalam in Muḍichchōnāḍu which was a sub-division of Kalyāṇapuraṅgoṇḍaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.date: Śaka 4448, Bhava (wrong), Kārttika, 6th day, Thursday, ba. di. . . .
cells.remarks: Unfinished.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the residents of Elinuḷai, a village in Paiyyūr-kōṭṭam a sub-division of Jayaṅgoṇḍaśōḷa-maṇḍalam, for the Rājēndraśōḻaṉ-maḍam. The price money for the land was paid by Tiruvaraṅgadēvaṉ alias Mummuḍiśōḷa-Brahmamārāyaṉ a native of Vīranārāyaṇa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam which was a taṉiyūr in Rājēndrasiṅga-vaḷanāḍu of Śōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Tamil

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Tamil

cells.place: On a pillar of the verandah round the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Tamil

cells.place: On the second pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: No

cells.place: On the third pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: No

cells.place: On the fourth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: No

cells.place: On the fifth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of money by the members of the assembly of Maṇali alias Siṁhaviṣṇu-cchatravēdimangalam. The money was deposited on interest (in paddy) with the revenue accountant (puravarivariṇai-naṇṇu-nāyakan) of Siyappēḍu alias Mummuḍi-śōlanallur, for conducting the festival called Madi-Miṅgam.

cells.place: On the sixth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by Vējjla Madurāntakaŋ alias Tandanayakan Rājēndrarāja-Ilangovēlaļ of Naijūr, a village in Irairum-nāḍu which was a sub-division of Uyrakkoṇḍa-vaļanāḍu in Sōļa-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the seventh pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: The inscription stops with the introduction of the King beginning with "Śingāśara taru, etc.

cells.place: On the eighth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 miļavu cows for pakṣhōpapya and lamps, by Achchan Tiruchchirrambalamuḍaiyān alias Guru-kalarājar of Ponparri in Milai-kūrrram, a district of Rājarāja-Paṇḍi-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the ninth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Registers that the officer Rajendraśinga Mvendavēlār enquired into temple affaire in the hall called Vakkānikkum-manđupam and fixed the details of service to be maintained from kuryadandam and 'excess-paddy' collected from the servants of the temple and the tenants of the dēvaldna villages.

cells.place: On the tenth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 95 sheep for a perpetual lamp to the temple of 'Tiruvorriyār-uđaiya-Mabādēva by Chaturaṇ Chaturi, wife of Nāgan Perungađaṇ and a dancoing girl (dēvarađiyā!) (of the temple).

cells.place: On the eleventh pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of paddy for offerings by certain Perumaŋ Madurāntakaŋ alias Rājēndrasōļa-Vengaṇāttarai-yaŋ, from whom he purchased the land in Janiur alias Chōlēndrasiṁhanallūr.

cells.place: On the twelfth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 92 sheep for a lamp by a certain Sundaraśōļa-Pandiya Vilupparaiyān who was a servant of the temple (paṇimagan) and a resident of Kachhipuraŋ in Eyil-nāḍu, a sub-division of Eyilr-kōṭṭam.

cells.place: On the thirteenth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Contains only the historical introduction beginning with tiru-maruviya teṅgōl, etc., and the date.

cells.place: On the fourteenth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged at the beginning. Gift of money for providing every day, a bundle of grass for a cow and for other services.

cells.place: On the fifteenth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Do. Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by a native of Tirukkāna-Pērtur in Tirukkana-Pērtur-nāđu which was a sub-division of Rajaraja-Papdi-nāđu.

cells.place: On the sixteenth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land by the residents of the dēvadāna village Ilgaiyūr to Śattay Irāmadariyar who is called the anukkiyar (anukki servant?) of the king. The purpose of the sale was to maintain 12 dēradīriyar in the temple, to serve (i) the goddess .

cells.place: On the seventeenth pillar in the same place.
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the residents of Iganaiyūr to Śīraļan Guņamadātya alias Irumadiśōla Vilupparayan of Kōyammangalam in Tirunagaiyūr-nādu, a sub-division of Kshatriyaśikhāmaņi-vaļanādu which was a district of Śōla-maņdalam. The land was situated in the quarter called Śankarappādi[ja]liyār Rājarāpperundēru at Tiruvorriyūr.

cells.place: On the eighteenth pillar in the same place.
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land, for maintaining a flower garden and supplying garlands, to Nāgalabbaṭtar, daughter of Arindama-Bhaṭṭa, an inhabitant of Mōrka[i]pāram in the Arya-dēśa. The land belonged to the village of Alambakkam and Śavappa in Surattur-nādu, a sub-division of Paliyar-kōṭṭam.

cells.place: On the nineteenth pillar in the same place
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the assembly of Mugali alias Sinhavishņu-chaturvedimangalam to a native of Parittikkudi in Negamali-nādu, a sub-division of Arumolidēva-vaļanādu which was a district of Śōlamaņdalam, for presenting it to the temple. In the reign of king Rājarājachōdava (I).

cells.place: On the west wall of the same verandah.
cells.remarks: Gift of 32 cows for a lamp by a native of Mugaļippādinādu in Naduvil-nādu.

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor of the same verandah.
cells.remarks: Gift of ārkkai[varm]ani-gold for a lamp to the god Tiruvorriyūr-Mahādēva by Ametti alias Kurumbubbhūti, daughter of Sūryan Pukali[nar]kō-Nāryāṇakōvaraiyan, son of Perunganat[tu] T[h]anatt- [30 kalanju] was placed in the hands of the assembly of Adambakkam (a hamlet) of Tiruvorriyūr, and the Amritagana (committee), on interest at 3 mañjādi per pe[r]unjūru [every year].

cells.place: On the second slab in the same place
cells.remarks: A portion of the slab at the bottom is apparently out cut off. Gift of 60 kaļañju of ārkkaihemmai-gold for offerings and a lamp, by Puṭṭangāndar, chief of Kattur in Vadagarai-nādu, a district of Sōla-nādu.

cells.place: On a third slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of a lamp to the temple of Tiruvorriyūr-Mahādēva by Mārayi Paramēśvaran alias Sōmbiyan Sōliyarayani of Śirukuļattur in Poyyik-kūram, a sub-division of Tenkarai-nādu which was a district of Sōla-nādu.

cells.place: On the fourth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: A portion of the slab at the bottom is apparently out off. Gift of gold (30 kaļaṅku) for a lamp to the same temple by Sappakkak alias Patradani who was a concubine (bhōgi?) of Vairamēgad alias Vāṇakōvariyar, son of (Śtāmi-Araiyar, a resident of) Valaṇ-nāḍu, a suburb of Tiru-vorriyūr and the Ampiṭarigaṇs (committee).

cells.place: On the fifth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Do. Gift of gold for offerings by Paļiyapilli [one of the queens] of Vidēviduga-Pallavaraiyar of Umbuļa-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the sixth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Do. Gift of gold (30 kaļaṅku) for a lamp by the queen Mahādēvi-Adigal to the temple of Tiru-vorriyūr-Mahādēva. The assembly of Adam-pā[kkam] (a suburb) of Tiruvorriyūr in Puliyūr-kōṭṭam and the Ampiṭaraigaŋ (committee), received the gold on interest.

cells.place: On the seventh slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged at the top and bottom. Gift of gold for two lamps by Kōđandarāmar, eldest son of the Choļa King Parakēsarivarman. A portion of the gold seems to have been burrowed on interest in the 36th year of the king, by the residents of Veljivayil, a village in Puļal-erikki]-nādu.

cells.place: On the fifth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of gold for a lamp by Kūrāņi Vilupparaiyar Aiyan Puttan. The assembly of Vayilpārai (in charge) of Tiruvorriyūr received the amount on interest.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the ninth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of an image of Śribalidēva, eight bugles, (kāla) and 24 Ag-whisks [?] with gold handles, by the king

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.place: On the tenth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by Dēvan Kēsari alias Kufjiramalla-Pallavaraiyan, a resident of Perumpangūr in Veļar-nādu a sub-division of Soļa-nādu.

cells.place: On the eleventh slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of gold (50 kalañju) for feeding 2 mahāvratis every day, by Ilađaipperqariyan alias Soļasikhamani-Pallavaraiyan.

cells.place: On the twelfth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for a lamp by Iraavi Nili, daughter of Vijayarāja [va]dēva, the Chēra king. The amount was apparently invested on a field in Drāvuṇiyūr which yielded the annual interest, viz., 4 kalanju.

cells.place: On the same slab
cells.king: Madiraikoṇḍa Parakēsarivarman †
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for a lamp by Arindigai-perumanar, son of Chōla-Perumanaḍigaļ, to the god Śiva at Adhigrāma.

cells.place: On the thirteenth slab built into the floor of the same verandas.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to record a gift of gold which was received on interest by the assembly of Adambakkam (a suburb) of Tiruvorriyūr and the Ampiṭarigaṇa (committee).

cells.place: On the fourteenth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to record a gift of gold for feeding a Brahman.

cells.place: On the fifteenth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions the wife of Koralu Ku[rā]mbu alias Parakēsari-Mavendaraiyar, of Vaļadaiyangalīlam in Tirukkalappappur-kūṛṛam in [Aru]nāḍi-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the sixteenth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 27 kaļaṅku of gold for offerings by Padi Arindigai wife of Vidēvidugu Ilaṅgōvēlar of Kō-nāḍu. The money was placed in the hands of the residents of Vaļkaṭṭar (a suburb) of Tiruvorriyūr, on interest at 8 mañjāḍi per kaļanju per annum.

cells.place: On the seventeenth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a sale of land which was situated in Igaṇaiyūr a village of Tiruvorriyūr.

cells.place: On the eighteenth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for a lamp by Sembiyan Mūvēndavēļāy alias Sattan Ulagalanda [mū]nru[kai]maṅgala[r]in Tiruvorriyūr-nāḍu [of Sōļa-nāḍu]. The gold was deposited for interest with the residents of Kuļumaṇipakkam near Maṅgāḍu in Puliyūr-kōṭṭam.

cells.place: On the nineteenth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for a lamp by Narsinghayyaŋ, son of Iha[ba]nna, a merchant in the camp (kaṇaka) of the Vaļļabha [(ka]rnat[a] king. The merchant was a native of Manyakhēṭa. The gold was deposited with the residents of Śorappuḍu in Tujumurnyūr-nāḍu, a district of Puliyūr-kōṭṭam.

cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp and one lamp-stand by Tārpurnēhabbataṛ of Kaļakkakuḍi.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur
cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for a lamp by the mother of the Vallabha king Kannara[dēva. The gold was deposited on interest with the assembly of Kurarūr alias Parāntaka-nhaṭuvarō-maṅgalam in Ambattar-ēriki-nāḍu, a sub-division of Poļay-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the twentieth slab built into the floor of the same verandah.
cells.remarks: The upper portion of the stone is missing. Gift of land by purchase from the residents of Igaṇai-mūṇḍūr, for offerings to a shrine called Sōlamal-Īsvara in the temple at Oyiṇṇudur (i.e. Tiruvorriyur). The donor's name is lost.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the twenty-first slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of money (100 nishkas of pure gold) by Chaturanana-Paṇḍita, the pupil of Nirañjanaguru, for providing bali in the temple at Tiruvorriyūr. The Grantha portion gives an interesting account of the early career of Chaturanana.

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for feeding a learned Brāhmaṇa by a native of Eṭṭiyarkurichchi in Pāṇḍi-nāḍu, who had accepted service in the temple.

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: In incomplete characters. Appears to record an order, of Maṭṭi-nāḍu-uḍaiyār, who was the minister of Hajarat Dāyudu-Khān, authorising a certain Ulli-Veṅkaṭa-Seṭṭiyār to conduct the charities connected with the temple.

cells.place: On a second slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp and one Īla-lamp-stand, by a native of Soļa-naḍu.

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a third slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to register a sale of land as bhaṭṭavritti by a certain Mūrtiperumāṇār.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxviii||198" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXVIII, No. 198</button>

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the fourth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of two iḷa-lamp-stands, 360 sheep for maintaining two perpetual lamps and a short with a gold handle, by Māvaṇḍa-Pallavaraiyan alias Adittapidāran, son of Vīra-Nārṇa-Pallavaraiyan alias Aruṇmoḷi, who was a native of Kūgūr in Vaḍa-Puṇagāḍu-nāḍu a sub-division of Mīkūru in Soḷa-nāḍu.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxviii||199" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXVIII, No. 199</button>

cells.location: Tiruvorriyur, Saidapet taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu

cells.place: On the east wall of the central shrine in the same temple, left of entrance.

cells.remarks: Gift of land for archandvītti, i.e. the maintenance of worship, in the temple of Varadaraja at Kurumāvi in Puli-naṭu, a di-triot of Chī[ttūri]-rājya, to a private individual.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field at Guttapalle
cells.remarks: Records the death of a horo at Modumapalli when Selvagahgamarāyan, after capturing his enemy in Marāyappadi, was bringing back the cattle.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field at Chalamaṅgala.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions the Mahdeśmantādhipati [Rā]ngappa-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On a viragal set up in the backyard of a house in the village.
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.place: On the base of the Sōmēśvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Fragment. Contains a portion of the introduction of, Rājēndradēva I which refers to the setting up of a pillar of victory at Koḷḷapuram. Mentions Purāśirāmaṇvarman of Āṇiyūr at 'Ippirāmbeḍu in Śilaināḍu, a sub-division of Veṇkuṝakkōṭṭam. Ippirāmbeḍu is the ancient name of the modern Gaḍimalam near Rēṇiguṇṭa.

cells.location: Moḍugalapalle
cells.place: On a viragal set up in a field
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Seems to mention Mahārājādhi.

cells.place: On another viragal in the same place
cells.remarks: Refers to a cattle-raid and the death of a hero.

cells.place: On a slab set up to the west of the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to a certain Sāmantavallava, son of Dōsaiyarasa.

cells.place: On another slab set up in the same place
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Refers to the raid on Puli-nādu by the Nolamba king, under orders of Kotigunī-svarar and to the capture of Kōyir[ūr]. On this occasion of the conquest of the country, Dōsaiyaran, the chief of that country, fought and fell. Mentions Kōyigūr and a certain Indragani.

cells.place: On a third slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Do. Mentiones Koyāgrū and a certain Indragapi.

cells.location: Bhīma-ganīpalle
cells.place: On a slab set up in the north prākāra of the Bhīmēsvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Bhīmapuram near Mōdugalapalle to the temple of Bhīmēsvaram, by Susa[gāri] Mamma-Chikkaraya who constructed the temple and also repaired the village tank.

cells.location: Karshana-palle
cells.place: On the east and north bases of the mandapa in front of the central shrine in the Arkēsvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of tax on oil-mills, to provide a lamp in the temple of Ādugai-kāmam-īsvaram-Udaiyār at Muttukūr alias Erivīrappattanam in Puli-nādu which was a sub-division of Tyāgābharana-valanādu in Jayangonda-chōla-mandalam, by Chōlēndrasimha-Mavēndarādiyar, who was the revenue officer in charge of the district, for the prosperity of the emperor. Records the construction of steps (sēpāna) by certain Adāris (karumān).

cells.place: On a pillar of the poroh of the same manđapa.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of steps (ešpđna) by certain dādris (karumān).

cells.place: On a slab built into the Nandi-mandapa of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Fragment.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the same temple
cells.date: Šaka 1332, Vikrita, Chaitra, su. dī. 5, Thursday, lunar eclipse (=Thursday 91st March 1809).
cells.remarks: Gift of a portion of income accruing to the royal treasury from certain lands at Muttukūru, in favour of the temple of Angahartavarandarāja-Nayinār at that village which belonged to Vada-Puli-nādu, a sub-division of Nigarilichōla-mandalam, by the chief Sommayd Vīra-Odayadēva-Chōlēndrarāja.

cells.location: Somala, Punganūru taluk, Chittoor district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On another slab set up in the same temple.
cells.remarks: States that the king returned from Chōl[ō]nādu, entered Nojambavādi and camped at Kōlāla in Gangavāsi (district). On this occasion he raised Kirtigā[vu]da to the position of Nojamba-gāvuda of Puli-nādu and gave him as a kōdage the village Kiriya-Belagatturu [in that district].

cells.location: Āvulapalle, Punganūru taluk, Chittoor district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a third slab set up in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records that Sīravādi-bhatara, son of Gā[v]da-bhatara set up the minor images in the temple and presented three (stone) oil-mills to it.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field in the same village.
cells.remarks: Refers to the death of a hero at Kuṭi[lā]la, on the occasion when Ballaha took up arms against Kaḍuvaṭṭi for exacting tribute. The hero was a servant of Bāṇarasa Vijayitta (i.e. Vijayāditya), who was ruling Gaṅgaṟu-sāsira.

cells.location: Basinikoṇḍa, Madanapalle taluk, Chittoor district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: Seems to record the death of the Gaṅga king (?) Prithuvīpatiyarasa.

cells.place: On another slab set up in the same place
cells.remarks: Records the death of a private individual of Muttukūru.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxviii||343" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXVIII, No. 343</button>

cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: Mentions the death of a hero (?) at Muttukūru and the grant of land to him below the southern tank, as koḍage.

cells.place: On a third slab set up in the same place
cells.remarks: The top portion of the slab is lost.

cells.location: Kōvilūr (Javadis), Polur taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the fourth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: The top portion of the slab is lost. Records that the gāmuṇḍas of Muttukūru presented some wet land to the son of a deceased hero.

cells.location: Kōvilūr (Javadis), Polur taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the fifth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Records that while [Vi]kkiyaṇṇa, son of Prithuvīpati was governing the Puli-nāḍu sixty (district), a quarrel arose between him and Pallava Dhavaḷa, in which he and a hero died. The latter's brother Kundiga raised this monumental (stone) in memory of the dead hero.

cells.place: On the sixth slab in the same place
cells.remarks: Mentions a servant of the king named Chāmuṇḍa.

cells.place: On the seventh slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Much damaged.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxviii||349" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXVIII, No. 349</button>

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.place: On the eighth slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Mentions Muttukūru and the death of a hero in a cattle raid (?).

cells.location: Dēvikāpuram, Arni taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the ninth slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Mentions the Pāṇḍya and the Chōḷa (kings) and the death of a hero.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxviii||351" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXVIII, No. 351</button>

cells.place: On the tenth slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to mention the chief [Ba]gigayya-[ma]indembam-Baṅkarasa and the death (?) of one of his servants.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field at Sōmala
cells.remarks: Gift of Nōlapalle to a private individual, by another private individual.

cells.location: Āvulapalle — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Śrīnivāsamūrti temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of a dēvadāna to the temple of Prasanna-Veṅkaṭēśvara at Āvulapalle, by Chikkarāya Timmayagavuṇigāru of Su[ga]ṭūru.

cells.location: Dēvikāpuram, Arni taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab set up at the tank bund in the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift by Vīrayagauṇivāru of Ānekallu, to the temples of Prasanna-Veṅkaṭēśvara and Mallikārjuna at Āvulapalle. Mentions Su[ga]ṭūri Chikkarāya Timmayagavuṇigāru.

cells.location: Basi-nikonda
cells.place: On two slabs lying in a field
cells.remarks: One of the slabs is mutilated. Registers that the 1,500 merchants of the four quarters including nādu, nagara and nānādēsi, met at Sīrāviralli in Mōgai-nādu, a sub-division of Pūrani-Mārayapādi of Jayangonda-chōla-mandalam and resolved to convert the village Sīrāvalli into a nānādēsi-Tiruchchirrambalam-pattana and to grant certain privileges to the residents of that village.

cells.location: Sōlapuram
cells.place: On the south base of the ruined Śiva temple
cells.remarks: Gift of certain taxes silvari to the temple of Rajarajāvaram-Uđaiyar at Uyyakkondan-Solapuram and other adjoining temples, by Seṅgēni-Ammuriyappap Kapṇudai-Perumaj alias Vikkiramaśola-Sambuvarayaṇ.

cells.place: On a stone lying in the same temple
cells.remarks: Fragment. Registers a sale of land to the temple of Rājēndrasōla-īśvaram by the residents (of this city).

cells.place: On two detached stones lying in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Mentions (Kippu), a disciple of Tirumala-āgariyar 'and a gift of laud made by him. The land con-sisted of the field Puttavadipatti (evidently called after Puttavadi, i. e., Buddha) and others.

cells.location: Dēvikāpuram, Arni taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the Śiva temple at Kovlur (Javadis).
cells.date: Śaka 1377, Yuva, Karkataka, su. di. 7 Monday, Sōdi. [= Monday 21st July 1455].
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Gapapatimadu in Maṅgala-nādu near the hill called Rajagambiraṇ-malai to the temple of Tirumūla-Nayiṇār, by a certain Timmaya-Nayake, for the victory of the king.

cells.location: Dēvikāpuram, Arni taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1355, Virodhakrit, Makara, su. dī. full moon, Thursday, Pūṣam, lunar colipse. (=Thursday, 17th January 1492, lunar colipse). [date-calculation appendix, No. 347: 17th January 1432 (Lunar eclipse).]
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Palavarai in Pediri-parru near Rajagarambur, to the temple of Tirumala-Nayinār in Mangala-nādu, by Appamālainātha, son of Narasińgadēva, chief of Mului-perru, for the victory of the king.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records the death of a certain Villi in a tiger-hunt.

cells.location: Viralūr
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Pañgava-nātamman temple
cells.remarks: Refers to the guild of merchants. The record may be about the time of Rājarāja I.

cells.location: Dēvikāpuram, Arni taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Ganēśa temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Records that four hamlets in Śīromuri-Paṅgala-nādu were caused to be granted by the king at Vijayanagara, to the temple of Arulajanatha-Nayaṇar and Unṇamulai-Naebohiyar, while Mallappa-Daṇnayaka was the Prime Minister.

cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Tirumala-T[i]d[i]siya-Nāyagar at Devakkappuram by Rayappudaiyan for Kodaipalli and others.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxviii||365" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXVIII, No. 365</button>

cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāra of the same temple.

cells.remarks: The king bears Saluva titles. Registers a lease of certain temple lands to Tirumalai-Nāyaka, one of the Kappadiya-Nāyakas, living in Marudarāsar-Paḍāvīdu, by the temple treasurer Īsāna-Siva-chārya of Bhikshā-matha at Dēvakkapura on the southern bank of Seyyūru, in Mūgaiyūr-village near Rājarāgambhīran, in Mūgaiyūra-nādu which is a sub-division of Melkūru-nādu in the district of Palagaupra-kōttam in Jayangondaśōla-mandalam. Registers the right of cultivation of temple lands (ulavu-kānyakāshi) granted to a certain Sadāśiva-Nāyaka of Marudarāśar-Paḍāvīdu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1441, Bahudhānya, Kārttigai, su. di. 13, Tuesday, Siddha-yōga.
cells.remarks: Registers the right of cultivation of temple laude (uļavu-kāpiyākehi) granted to a certain Sudáśiva-Náyaka of Marudarasar-Pađaiviđu.
