cells.remarks: Registers a similar right granted to a resident of Devakkapuram by the temple trustee, gurukkal, and Īśvarēsvara-Śivāchārya of Bhikshā-matha and others.

cells.location: Devīkapuram
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1422, Raudri, Karka-taka, su. di. 7, Friday, Attam.
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the dēvadāna village of Sēmbiya-mānallūr, to Devana-Bhatta, and food in the matha to two persons who had to feed in the temple. The grant was made by Tūmalal-Nāyaka and Īśvara-Nāyaka, sons of Ettappa-Nāyaka, for the merit of Nārāsa-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Devīkapuram — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1455, Vikriti, (wrong), Śinga, su. di. 10, Friday, Uttiram.
cells.remarks: The king has a long list of biruda's. Records that the king made a gift of certain lands at Tiru-mārudarāsar-Paḍāvīru, was granted the right of supervision, etc., in the temple and the enjoyment of certain lands at Murugamangalam, from Īsāna-Śivāchārya of Bhiksha-matha, the trustees and the Kaikkōlas of the Tirumala-uḍaiya-Nayinār temple at Dēvakkapuram.

cells.remarks: Gift of land and a house in the village Kailāsa, to a certain Sumaraponagava-dīkshita for the merit of king (rēdmi) Narasa-Nāyaka 'who went to Śiva-lōku (i.e. died), by (his subordinate) Tirumalai-Nāyaka.

cells.remarks: The king has Sajuva titles.- Records a gift of revenue, amounting to 38½ paṇam to the temple of Tirumala-uđaiya-Nayiṅar at Dévasthánam Dévakkápuram by Haribara-Náyuka, son of Mallappa-Náyaka of the Kannadiyu-Náyakas living at Marudarasar-Pađaiviđu, for the merit of the king and Tirumalai-Náyaka.

cells.place: On the same wall ..

cells.location: Devīkapuram — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Records that Sadāśiva-Nāyaka provided ghee for lamps during the festival of Tirukkārtigai in the same temple, for the merit of chief (svāmi) Tirumalai-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Dēvikāpuram, Arni taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the same prākāra ..
cells.remarks: Gift of ghee for the same festival by the daughter of the Kannaḍiya chief Dēvappuḍaiyar at Marudaraśar-Paḍaiviḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of ghee for lamps by Śrīraṅganāthar the maṇiyakāraṉ (monegar ?) of Iḍaittuṟai, for the merit of Namaśśivāya-Nāyaka, son of Mallappa-Nāyaka of Marudaraśar-Paḍaiviḍu.

cells.location: Devīkapuram — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: The king bears Sāḷuva titles. Grant of the tax paṭṭaḍai-nūlāyam, at 1½ paṇam per annum on each loom, to the temple, for the merit of Kāḷattīśvara-Nāyaka.

cells.remarks: Gift of land and a house in the dēvudāna village Śorappundi to Vadamalaiyar one of the Pandits (vidēṇ) of Āgravānpadi, by Vivēsvara-Śivacharya of the Bhiksha-maṭha at 1Dēvakkāpuram, the Kaikkola-mudelis and other trustees of the temple. cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.date: Śaka 1444, Vikrama, Kumbha, śu. di. full-moon, Friday, Uttiram.
cells.remarks: Gift of land and two houses to a certain Aṭṭavaṇai Veṅkappa who secured for the temple the village of Śōrappūṇḍi as a gift from the king.

cells.location: Devīkapuram
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.date: Šaka 1452, Sarvadhāri, Karttigai, su. di. 10, Utti-ram, Saturday.
cells.remarks: Registers that the trustees of the temple granted to a certain Ambalattāḍi the right of cultivating (uḻavu-kāṇi) the dēvadāna village of Kāmākshirāvuttaṉ-tāṅgal and fixed 15 paṇam and 20 kalams of paddy to be paid to the temple every year.

cells.place: 1o
cells.date: Śaka 144[4], Vikrama, Kumbha, śu. di. 10, Saturday, Punarpūśam.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Ūvattūr with its hamlet Taraipāḍi, to the same temple by a certain Ammaiyappa-Nayiṉār, as a tirunāmakkāṇi. On receiving this, Īśāna-Śivāchārya of the Bhiksha-maṭha and other trustees of the temple made the same donor the lessee of the village and presented a house.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1453, Virodbi, Sittirai, su. di. 10, Attam.
cells.remarks: Registers the permanent lease (dēvadāna-paṭṭai) of Dēvarāyan-paṭṭaḍai to a Kaṇṇaiya-Nāyaka of Gaṭṭapuram in Puṅgala-nāḍu.

cells.location: Devīkapuram
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka, 1450, Sarvadhari, Ani, su. di. Uttiram, Monday.
cells.remarks: Gift of ghee for a lamp.

cells.location: Devīkapuram
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of ghee for a lamp by a lady of Marudaradar-Paḍavīḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1451, Śukla, Makara, su. di. 17, Sunday, Tiruvōpam.
cells.remarks: Gift of the hamlet Śāyavaram-paṭṭaḍai near Paḍavīḍu, by the trustees of the temple in Tiruppari Vēśāvaṇa-Uḍaiyār, by Tirumalai-Nāyaka, son of Eṭṭappa-Nāyaka, and others. The donee was evidently an officer in charge of the works connected with the temple.

cells.location: Dēvikāpuram, Arni taluk, Arcot North district — Tamil Nadu

The gift consisted of a talaparigi-channel below the tank of Nagarugere and of a tank called Goljasetikunte in Ādubārahalli village. Mentions Virabbopa the brother of Penugonde Virappanga who was the son of Nandi-Lakiseti of Lepākshi.

The grant was made at the instance of Narasa-Nayaka, brother of Virapannya of Penugonda.

cells.remarks: Records a sale of land to the same three shrines by the mahājunas of the Sarasandha-agrahāra, being Kaifatiyendra alias Pratāpasēvayāpura in Penugonda-rājya, belonging to the gift of Achyutadēva-Maharāya, when He made the grant gifts named kāmāthana, kalpavriksha and vīrachakra in the presence of the god Virupaksha on the banks of the Tungabhārā river. Lēpākshi is stated to have been a village in Sadali-nādu which belonged to Rodd-nādu a sub-division of Penugonda-rājya.

cells.remarks: Much damaged. Gives the usual long genealogy commencing with the Moon.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same prākāra

After the long prālaśti which is identically the same as that of the Unamafijeri plates it is recorded that the king weighed himself against pearls at Kāñohi in the Śaka year 1455, Nandana and that he made the gift called Kāñohanamārse in Śaka 145 [6], Vijiya.

cells.place: On the east wall, left of entrance into the tavern temple at Old Lēpākshi near the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 160[8], Durmati, Vaiśākha, su. di. 3, Monday, solar colipse, (= Monday 9 May A.D. 1681) [date-calculation appendix, No. 581: Monday 9th May 1681.]
cells.remarks: (Gift of tolls by the merchants of all countries headed by Pṛithvīchēṭi Rayana-Bhāskara, to the temple of Santa-Narjunēśvara at Lēpākshi.

cells.place: On the same wall, left of entrance

cells.date: Śaka 160[2], Monday, vai. śākha, su. di. 3, Monday.
cells.remarks: Gift of fields and gardens to the temple of Santa-Narjunēśvara, by the merchants and Karnams of Old Lēpākshi, for the merit of the king.

cells.place: On the nēgalabāṅga rock near the Pēda-cheruvu tank in the same village.

cells.location: Penukonda
cells.place: On a pillar in the compound of the Sub-Collector's office
cells.remarks: A portion of the pillar on the right side has been apparently cut off. Seems to record the gift of this lamp-pillar. Mentions ['eṇuko]jinda.

cells.remarks: Registers that a certain [Ja]kharan son of Kappa-Naya[ka] of the Hīraṇgu-Madahāri (i.e., Mudaliyāra of Parigi) family, constructed a maṇḍapa in front of the temple of Haṇumantadeva at Chauluru and mude some grants to it.

cells.place: On a second stone not up near the same temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a gift to the mahdījanus of Chauluru by a number of Vipravinōdine who belonged to various iākhas and sūtras.

cells.remarks: Gift of land to a certain Duggueśti a member of the Pasunđi-Bōva (community P), by the 300 great men of Kaguru.

cells.place: On a stone set up near the Āñjanēya temple below the tank-bund.
cells.remarks: Broken at the bottom. Seems to refer to the Nolamba who ruled the country extending up to Kañchi.

cells.location: Bichchaṁpalle
cells.place: On a stone set up near the Āñjanēya temple
cells.remarks: Registers the exemption of fishing (P) taxes granted to the Besta-bōva (i.e. fisherman) community of Uṭakūra by Mummađi-Rađdi, the agent of Pedi-rājaya, and the gauḍa and eñalōvu of Uṭakūra.

cells.location: Kotmuru
cells.place: On a stone set up in front of the Channakeśavart temple
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to register a gift to the temple of Chauluru, for the merit of Dajavay, Krishna-ma-Nāyaka].

cells.location: Manepalle

cells.remarks: Mentions that Virayya son of Śivapuramaya and other grammaṇis of Epudumuru obtained certain privileges (?)

cells.remarks: Seriously damaged.

cells.location: Palur

cells.place: On a stone at Hosahalli
cells.remarks: Do. No. 49. Gift of land to the temple of Siṁhēśvaradēva at Hosavali, by the king and alas> of 40 gadyaṇas by a merchant for (repairing?) a tank.

cells.place: On a stone at Yadur
cells.remarks: Do. No. 57. Registers that Duddharasa, son of Hiriyaarasu, and Jumjaladēvi acquired whole villages, house-sites, performed many charitable deeds and died. His brother Jajarasa caused this stone to be set up.

cells.place: On the gopura of the Velidêvisîsvarasvâmin temple at Venganur, right of entrance.
cells.date: Śaka 1545, Rudhirōdgārin, Vaiyāśi 3, Rishabha śu. di. 12, Aṭṭam, Thursday (= Thursday, 1st May A.D. 1623)
cells.remarks: Records that a Reddi of the Peṇṭakula race, consecrated the shrine of Pañjamalnâthasvâmi and Periyamênai-Nâchchi at Vṛiddhâchalam alias Perumâragam, provided for lamps, provision for worship and oblations. Mentiones Sênji in Vaṁbâr-nâdu which was a sub-division of Karikalasôṇa- Valuṇâdu in Magada-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the same gopura ..
cells.date: Śaka 1591, Saumya, Śittirai 18, Daśami, Śadayam, Thursday (= Thursday, 16th April A.D. 1669).
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the different communities living at Venganur, for the merit of one of the Reddis of the same family.

cells.location: Arumbavur
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailâsanâthasvâmin temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the different communities living at Venganur, for the merit of one of the Reddis of the same family.

cells.location: Āḍuturai, Perambalūr taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south base of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a grant of land to a private individual by a certain Vāṇakōvaraiyaṉ.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Registers that the sthânattâr of this temple, Durga- Pidari and Ayyyan situated in this village and at Rajarajanaullur and Kinaippai, were made tax-free by the chief Vayakaraiyan.

cells.place: On the north base of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: The community of priests living in the districts of Vembar-naṭu, Perambalur-naṭu and Mulai-naṭu granted the taxes due to them from the dēvadāns villages, for repairs in the temples of Vaṭakayilayamudaiya-Nayaṇar and Kulottunga-Vinnugar-Emberamaṇ at Arumbar.

cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Specifies the extent of the devâdâna lands below (the tank) Sirneri and Periyari at Arugalur, as fixed by Tondaiman Perumârpillai alias Sôdivayaṇan, for repairs in the temple of Ararar.

cells.location: Perambalur
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Madanagôpalasvâmin temple
cells.remarks: States that the residents of emârî-nâtu made order that the residents of evarum-amî-nâtu are to collect vəram from the veḍparru-villages and kaḍamai from the kaḍamagarru-villages. The amount reallied by this arrangement was to be utilised, according to terms with the villagers, meeting the expenses of the followers of Sundara- Pâṇḍyadēva.

cells.location: Āḍuturai, Perambalūr taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order to the inhabitants of Meikurunâdu in Vaṁbâr-nâdu stating that the village Neikunram, a dēvadâna village of the temple of Gôpâlakôttar-Vippanar-Emberumân at Perumabalur, was assessed at some later period but was again made tax-free, by Kadalaḍaitta- Perumal alias Sundara-Pâṇḍya-Vêlôpparaiyar, a native of Ilakkuḍi in Pâdî-nâṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the south base of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Remission of jôḍi on the village of Nouchhiyam by an agent of Krishṇappa Nayaka and the residents of Vêghâr-śîrmai. The village is stated to have been abandoned by the people. Poṇṇappa-heṭṭar at Perambalur since the time of Dharmaputra! Mentions Sarappa-Nâyaka in whose time a suall amount of jôḍi used to be collected from ‘that village.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers that the residents of Perumbalur in the gianat of land for maintaining a sanddhifestival in the temple on the day of Bharaṇi which was the asterism under which, evidently, the quoon Toṇḍainaimuḍuḍaiyâl was born.

cells.location: Āḍuturai, Perambalur taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of land for maintaining the festival of Akkantirunā] which happened on Bharapi, in the same temple. The document is signed by Sundara-Paṇdya Vṭapparaiya. Evidently this gift is connected with what has been recorded in No. 11, above.

cells.location: Perambalur — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Refers to the gift registered in No. 11, viz. of 12 mâ of land south of Perumbalur, which had been lying waste for many years, by the residents of that village for conducting the festival of Bharani in honour of the birthday of the queen Tennavuḍaimuḍuḍaiyâl.

cells.place: On the north and west bases of the same shrine.
cells.date: Śake 1482, Pr-bhava (wrong by two years), Makara, Amāvāsy, Pūrādem, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the naegrahae in the same temple by Timmiyapppa-Nāyakkar Nūkki-Ruddiyār agent of Tulukkapa-Nāyakkar of Eyarnūśohi.

cells.location: Aduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Aparadhânahêsvara temple
cells.remarks: Built in, the middle. Seems to record a gift of land to the temple of Tirrukaranguṇḍuṇruḍaiya-Mahâdêva.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Gift of paddy for offerings and for oil to anoint the images every Saturday, in the temple of Tirrakkurungunduḍaiya-Mahâdêva in Tirrappunjunai, a Irâhmadeiyam in Urakrôvruttikkîr-kramam, a sub-division of Vaḍagarai-mûḍôla-vaļanâḍu, a native of Ambar in Ambar-nâdu.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of paddy for offerings to the temple of Tirukkuḍanguḍuturai-Nâyanâr at Iraiyaṇṅi.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a certain Ayyayyan of Kuļamur, to the god at Tirrukarangûḍuṭurai.

cells.place: On the north base of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp to the temple of Mahādeva at Tiraiyāyūr by a native of the village, a brāhmaṇa in Ugalūr-kūṟṟam, which was a sub-division of Muḍigoṇḍaśōḻa-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Kārguḍi, Nāmakkal taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of money for providing betel-leaves and nuts (during the paḷiyar-śānti) in the shrine of the goddess Gōmāṭṭi-Kaḍavēḷāḷan of Āykkūr in Ārūr-kūṟṟam which was a sub-division of Mūlāḍu alias Jayantha-vaḷanāḍu. The document is signed by Villavarāyan.

cells.location: Aduturai
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings. The document is signed by Villavarajan.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of money on which interest was paid in paddy and provision was made for offerings.

cells.place: On the north and west bases of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Begins with the introduction pūmādu vaḷar, etc. Gift of land.

cells.location: Kārguḍi, Nāmakkal taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Parakramapāndyanallar in Kil-kūrgu, a sub-division of Vembar-nađu, to the temple of Kugramporuttaruliya-Nāyanār at Iraiyappunjai Tirukkurangadutarai, a brahmadėya in Ugaļar-kūrgam which was a sub-division of Vadugarai Rajasiinha-vaļanađu, for celebrating a festival on the asterism Purādam (i.e. īfūvāshaļha) in the month of Puratṭa[6i], which coincided with the birth day of the king.

cells.location: Nanjai Edaiyar, Nāmakkal taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1327, Parthiva, Kauni, ba. di. Wednesday, Uttiratṭadi.
cells.remarks: Assignment of certain taxes in some specified districts of Rājanārāyaṇa-vaḷanāḍu, to the same temple, for offerings and worship.

cells.location: Aduturai
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king: Vīrapratāpa Dēvarāya-Mahārāya (II), the king (who instituted) the elephant hunt.
cells.date: Śaka 1361, [Siddharthin], Makaru, ba. di. Monday, Sodi, Sivaratri.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of a village (?) in Uttuṅgatunga-vaḷanāḍu to the temple of Kurrampuruḷariya-Nāyaṉār at Tirukkuraṅgāḍuturai, a village in Ugalūr-kūṟṟam of Viṭṭa-paṟṟu in Vaḍagarai-Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu, by a certain Dēvaṇa-Nāyaṉār, for the merit of the king, Vīra-Dēvarāya-Uḍaiyār 'Lord of the Southern Ocean'.

cells.location: Sivayam, Kulittalai taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south base of the same maṇḍapa
cells.date: Śaka 1381, Vikrama, Kārttaka, su. di. 9, Monday, Pōśam.
cells.remarks: Registers that the residents of Vēṇbā-nāḍu remitted certain taxes in favour of the temple, in the village of Kaḷaiyāśi of Kiḷ-kūṟṟu (in Vēṇbā-nāḍu) for maintaining worship and constructing a gōpura.

cells.location: Sivayam, Kulittalai taluk, Trichinopoly district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Seems to record that the residents of the eighteen divisions (porru) met together under the presidency of Ekambaranāthar, son of Nayinār, and seeing that there was a deficiency in the total areas of Ugaļar -padi-śirmayir-padu-kūru, they rectified it and had the alternation engraved on the temple at Kurangāduţurai.

cells.location: Aduturai
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Stones missing (at the end). Seems to record the gift of the village Abhangarahuttarayanallūr for maintaining a special worship, in the temple, called Abhangardhuttarāyaṇ-landi in the name of the king and also for celebrating a festival on his birth-day.

cells.place: De
cells.date: Śaka 135[1*], Saumya, Makara, su. di. Friday, Puratṭadi.
cells.remarks: Stones missing in the beginning. Gift of the village of Adiśudamangalam with all its income, for worship and repairs in the same temple, by the residents of Viṭpapparu and the community of tandirimdār.

cells.place: On the east wall of the same maṇdapa
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Talaij amangalam alias Āṭkondanallūr in Tepkarai-nādu which was a sub-division of Magadai-maṇdalam, for providing offerings in the shrine of the goddess called Ejjivārkulajiyar in the temple of Kurramporuttaruliya-Nāyaṇar at Iraivānpoñjai Tirukkurangadūturai under orders of the king and Nāyaṇar Ulagangatta-Vapakōvar-siyar.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same maṇḍapa
cells.remarks: Refers to the sale of the village Adiśaramangalam (Aḍiśaramangalam) and several patties, to the temple of Kurkamporuttis-Nāyaka. The king's gāduturai. The 27th and 28th years of the king are also quoted.

cells.location: Tiruchcheṅgāṭṭuṅguḍi, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the east wall of the same maṇdapa
cells.remarks: Registers that the dēvadāna village Ka'anivay (or Kalanivasai) in Kil-kūrru of Vembar-nādu was granted tax-free, in obedience to the orders of the king, by the residents of that nādu.

cells.place: On the east base of the same maṇdapa
cells.remarks: Built in at the bottom. Seems to record an agreement, among themselves, by the Palamgai 98 classes, and the Iļangai 98 classes of Vaļudalambattu-nāḍuvar against the Brāhmaṇas and the Vellaļas who hold revenue-free right (kāņi) over the lands of that district.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Refers to some events connected with the temple which happened in the 4th year of Vikrama-Chola and in the reign of Kulottuiga-Chola (II) and states that the residents of various divisions met together at Ugalur and arranged to conduct the worship in the temple as had been done before, by their ancestors.

cells.place: On the second gōpura of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Registers that the tenants (kuđi) in 12 villages of Ugajar-Kugumbarvāy-Śirmai had abandoned them owing perhaps to heavy taxation and consequently an agent of Viramaraśar, regulated the taxes at 5 paṇam for the first year and 10, from the following year on such plough of dry land and at 8 paṇam on every 100 kuđi of wet land.

cells.location: Kaṟguḍi
cells.place: On the east wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Tiruvīraṭṭānam temple
cells.remarks: Kāśi-Rōjanāyaka set up the image of Bhairava and provided for its worship.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same maṇḍapa
cells.date: 22nd year, Vṛishōbha, su. di. 5, Monday, Uttirāḍam.
cells.remarks: Refers to Perumāḷ Kuḷōttungadēva and to Vijaya-layadēva. Gift of the village of Uṟṟakkāḍi alias Aḻagiyakaṇṭanallūr in Vaḍagarai-Kaṟihaḻa-vaḷanāḍu, to the temple of Kayilāyamuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Tirukkaṇṇapuram, by the residents of that district for the purpose of providing offerings during the festival called Sittirai-tirunāḷ.

cells.location: Tiruchcheṅgāṭṭuṅguḍi, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: States that (the temple at) Tirukkarukāñji came into existence on the day of the asterism Rēvati.

cells.location: Kaṟguḍi — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 11th year, Mīna, su. di. 3, Wednesday, Aśvati.
cells.remarks: Registers that the temple of Kayilāyamuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār alias Vīra-Vīraśōlapuram in Vaḍagarai Kaṟihaḻa-vaḷanāḍu, by the priests of the temple of Kayilāyamuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Tirukkarukāñji alias Vīra-maśōlapuram, by Sārvabhaumachakravartin, an agent of the chief minister Sōmaya-Deṇṇāyaka.

cells.location: Kaṟguḍi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land (?) by a certain Immadi Ramachandra-Nayaka to the priests of the same temple.

cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Tiruvīraṭṭānam temple at Nañjal Eḍaiyār.
cells.remarks: Damaged and fragmentary. Seems to record a grant of land to the temple of Sri-Kailasain alias Tiraveyilvayilađaiya-Purmaśevara, by the assembly of Rajendrasiniha-ohaturvēdimaṅgelam. Mentions Iđaiyaru in Rajāgraya-valaṇādu.

cells.location: Kuṉṉamalai — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone lying to the south of the Kuppīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Registers the name of a gāmuṇḍa (i.e., gauṇḍa) who was one of the Veḷḷāḷas of Valipuram in Maḷai-nāḍu. Perhaps the stone was presented by him.

cells.location: Śivayam — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Śivapuriśvara temple
cells.remarks: Fragment. Gift of land to the priests of the temple of Śivapuriśvara at Śivayam, by the trustees of the Śēkharapuram in Kuṟumaṇ-nāḍu, by the trustees and the merchants (nagarattār) of that village.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of land to a maṭha within the premises of the temple, by the merchant Navaldrundaiyan Tiruchchirgambalamuđaiyan Gaṅgaikopda-Pillai.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: The beginning is missing. Seems to record the lease of land to a merchant by the priests of the temple of Tiramāņikkumāṇisvāmi-Nāyanar.

cells.place: On the north wall of the kitchen in the same temple.
cells.remarks: A copy of an earlier inscription [Gift of two kaśuñyu of g[i]d (tu]lar-rai-śembom) providing betel-leaf and other provisions to the temple of Tirumēņi-Nāyanar at Śivapādakēkharapuram in Ku[ṇarna]du, a sub-division of Rājarāghabīra-vaļanādu, by the merchant Navalrudaiyan Kālitadajen Tiruhōhgirumbalamudaiyan Kuļōttuṅgachōla dāyar...]

cells.location: Tiruchcheṅgāṭṭuṅguḍi, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On three pillars of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Registers that the pillars were the gift of Muppar-nāḍiyan Irunduḍikōra ōchchamaiyachakravarti, a merchant of Sõļapādyapuram.

cells.location: Tiruchcheṅgāṭṭuṅguḍi, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the second gōpura of the same temple, left and right of entrance.
cells.date: 4th year, Dhannus, su. di. 3, Thursday, Tiruvōpam.
cells.remarks: Damaged; seems to record an enquiry into the affairs of the e 'emple of Tirunāgakkhamali-uḍaiyar Nāyanar in Kayrukhai-nādu, a sub-division of Rajagambhira-valanādu. The committee of enquiry included the great minister Aliya-Sōmaya-Davamāyaka, Sovaya-Danadanayaka and Sōmanā-dha-Vittalēśvara who was a servant in the prince of Sōmāvaradeva.

cells.location: Tiruchcheṅgāṭṭuṅguḍi, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the Śu(u)klakkhi-payai rock in the same village.
cells.remarks: Registers the names Viramallan and Siyamittiran in arōnaio characters. In another place is engraved ya-karadu also in ancient alphabet. The rock has a row of five beds cut into it.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Uttarapatisvara temple
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Seems to record a gift of land to the shrines of Ganapatipuram-uḍaiyar-Nāyanar (and) Uttarāpati-Nāyaka at Tiruchōhgaṭṭangudi in Marugal-nādu, a sub-division of Gāyamaṇik[k]a-valanāḍu, by the chief Sōmaya-Daṇḍanayakkar.

cells.place: On the wall to the left of the dēvakoṭṭu images in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: [Gift of a lamp to the temple of Uttarapati-Nāyaka at Tiruchōhgangaṭṭangudi, by a native of Palaiyur, Meru[na]du in Urrukkāṭṭu-koṭṭum, a district of 'Ondri-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tiruchcheṅgāṭṭuṅguḍi, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers a gift of land and house to certain merchants connected with the treasury of Uttarapati-Nāyakar, on their having presented a throne to the temple.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same maṇḍapa
cells.remarks: Damaged. Relates to provide for a festival in the same temple by the merchants of the Choja country.

cells.place: On the west base of the Gaṇapatīśvara shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Gaṇapa[tī]śvara-uḍaiya-Mahādēva at Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi by the assembly of the village Tirukkaṇṇapuram a brāhmaṇīya-nāḍu which was a sub-division of Kṣatriya-śikhāmaṇi-vaḷanāḍu. The land was given to start a lamp in the temple of Piramīśvaramuḍaiya-Mahādēva of their village.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land for two lamps to the shrine of Śīrāladēva at Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi by a certain Veḷḷāḷan of Vāgan Śiriyan alias Tuppiḷa-Kōvēndavēḷāḷan.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land for feeding the devotees attending the festival of Šittirai-Tiruvadirai when the god Širajadévar of Tiruochehéngattākkuđi in Marugul-nađu, a sub-division of Mummudīsola-valjnađu, was taken in procession to the mandapa of Širuttonda-Nambi (in that temple).

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Gaṇapatīśvara at Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi, by a certain Tāyaṉ Tiruchchirṟambalamudaḷiyāṉ, for maintaining the same festival.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of land for the festival (stiruviđa) of Širuttonda-Nambi who was a devotee of Širajadéva of Tiruochehéngattānguđi, by two residents of Marugal. Before to the 'Revene Survey' made in the 17th year of Rajaraja.

cells.location: Tiruchcheṅgāṭṭuṅguḍi, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase, to the temple of Paramēśvara at Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi by the assembly of Marugal, in order to provide for two lamps in that temple.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Fragment containing portions of the historical introduction beginning with tingal-taru.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of land for a lamp by the assembly of Marugal.

cells.place: On the west base of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.date: 3rd year, Karka-ṭaka, su. di. 11, Monday, Attan.
cells.remarks: Built in, at the right end. Gift of land to the shrines of the two goddesses of Tirupatī-Nāyaṉu and Śirupatī-uḍaiyār in the temple of Uttaratī-Nāyaṉa by two residents of Marugūr alias Rājānārāyaṇa-chaturvēdimangalam].

cells.place: On the north wall of the same maṇḍapa
cells.remarks: Gift of land for providing garlands of red lilies to the two shrines of (Va)mpāmbavai-Uḍaiyār and Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi-uḍaiyār by the residents of Marugal-nāḍu which was a sub-division of (I)yamāṇikka-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Eradukera, Kalyāṇdrug taluk, Anantapur district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: [1] 1th year and 175th day, Vyisohika, ba. di. 14, Fri-day, Apilam.
cells.remarks: Registers that a document connected with the temple of Tiruvīraṭṭānamuḍaiyār-Uḍaiyār at Tirukkuppāpuram a brāhmaṇīya village of Marugal-nāḍu in Gēyamāṇikka-vaḷanāḍu, was engraved on the walls of the temple at Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi, as the temple of Tirukkuppāpuram was destroyed by a storm. The record refers to the 5th and 10th years of Periyadēvar Kuḷōttunga-Chōḷadēva in whose time the Tirukkuppāpuram temple came into existence.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase, for laying out a road, to carry in procession Śirāladēva-uḍaiyār from the maṇḍapa of the temple of Kayilāyamuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi to the temple of Tiru-Marugal. Refers to the land survey made in the 16th year of Kuḷōttunga-Chōḷadēva, 'who abolished tolls'.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers the remission of taxes in favour of the temple, ' for maintaining the worship of Siralapillaiyar. Refers also to the 11th year of Kulottunga-Choladeva, ' who abolished tolls.'

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records that the grants registered in Nos. 66 and 67 were caused to be made by Sāvaṇachakravartin of Veḷḷōhōri, by the lady devotee Aḻiyangōḍai-yār of the village of Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi.

cells.location: Mulakalēḍu, Kalyāṇdrug taluk, Anantapur district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the north base of the same maṇḍapa
cells.date: 24th year, Simha, ba. di. 18, Saturday, Pūśam.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by Arāsurudaiyān Tiruchchigrumbala-muđaiyān alias Tiruchochigrumbala-Pallaverayyan for providing offerings in the manđapa called Tirumuttuvānēri, to the god Uttarāpnti-Nāyaka on the occasion when he was to give salvation (to his devotee) during the festival of Sittirai-Barapi.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. The king is called Kōnērinmaikoṇḍān. Seems to record the grant of landed property to a certain Rūḍuṇḍamōḷa-Achāriyāṉ, who was perhaps the king's private Secretary (tiru-mandira-ōlai) was Rājēndra-Chōḷadēva.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Seems to record a gift of land in the villages Tiruvettaukattaui and Dināchintāmani ebaturvedimangalam, for providing offerings on every day of Bharani to the god Uttarāpnti-Nāyaka within the manđapu of Siyuttopda-Nāyayār. Much dan aged. Seems to register a number of lands acquired for constructing the third prākāra of the temple and a street round it. Reference is also frequently made to the reign of Kulottunga-Chola I, ' who was pleased to abolish tolls' and to the temple of Vikrama-Choliévara.

cells.location: Kambadūru, Kalyāṇdrug taluk, Anantapur district — Andhra Pradesh

cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. Supplies a long list of the Sanskrit _ślokas_ of the king. 'Seems to record a gift of land to the god Uttarapati-Nāyaka in the temple of the _Śampatīśvaram-Udaiyar,_ for the purpose of the _Aiyani_-festival in the months of Cittirai and Ārpadi.

cells.location: Tiruch-chengattanguḍi
cells.place: In the same place

cells.place: On the west wall of the _mandapa_ in front of the (nalli)amba shrine in the same temple .. .. .. .. .. ..

cells.place: On the main gopura of the same temple, right of entrance. .. .. .. ..
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record the fees on looms etc. fixed by an agent of Vira-[Naraśī]garāya-Ayyen.

cells.place: On the same gopura, left of entrance ..
cells.remarks: Fragment. Begin with the introduction kaṭal-būṇda etc. Refers to a certain Kađuvangundaiyan Araiyan Āṭkopda-Nayakag who was perhaps the donor.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of the _Śaṅkarōśvarasvāmin_ temple at _Erdukera_ .. .. .. .. ..

Krodhana, Phalguna, Amāvāyā, Sunday, solar colipee.
cells.remarks: Registers that when they were breaking a keah, by prince Pojalohora, a grandson of the king and lord of Kañchi, the pillar was set up by Cha-vuṇdayya of the Srivatsa-gōtra, the favourite minister of Pojalohora.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the same place

cells.place: On a pillar built into the floor, at the entrance into the same temple.

cells.king: Acyutadeva-Mahārāya †
cells.remarks: Seriously damaged. Seems to be a Vijayanagara record. Registers a royal gift of the village Tanaigalapura, named Mallikapura, made for the merit of Acyutadeva-Mahārāya on the auspicious occasion of Maha-Vīsākha.

cells.location: Rāyadrug, Rayadrug taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a pillar lying in the outer prākāra wall of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by Bayasta Konđamarasay[y]a to the temple of Mallikarjunadeva at Kambhaduru, for the merit of the king. The land was situated below the tank of Kambhaduru in Kundurapiya-fime which was the jāghir of the chief.

cells.place: On the same pillar
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Jālanvī to the same temple by Bayasta Koṇdamarasayya 'in order that Bayasta Koṇdamarasayya may, dwell in heaven.'

cells.place: On a pillar in a field to the east of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Registers that while the tank of Beddugonde was constructed, a temple for Mahādēva was also built and piunatoies were placed over it (for the merit of) Siṁgapōta, Ponṇēga and Dharmamādēvi.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field to the west of the same temple.
cells.date: Śāka 1458, Dur-mukhi, Jyeṣh-tha, ba. di. 30, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Records the villages and lands owned by the temple of Mallikārjunadeva at Kambahāduru in Kuṇḍurpiya-sīme which was the thal (nāyakatana) of Bayyapa-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Akkaṇa-gēru-gūḍi in the same village.

cells.remarks: Much damaged. Gift of land to the temple of Ātto[ra]dēva at Ku[ḍar]pi-durga.

cells.place: On a boulder in a field in the same village.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land granted by Timmaṇa-Nāyaka of Kuṇḍurpiye, to a certain Viraya of his own caste (?)

Gift of the village of Vegalatūru in Uttararandravishayadh-vishaya, by the king, to 46 brāhmanas of different gotras and sūtras on the occasion of the nitya-sraddha of his queen Mahādevī and mother Durlabhā.
Gift of land to two brāhmanas, one of whom was a doctor and the other Sōmalapura, surnamed Vīripākshapura divided into sixty shares, to a certain Virārya.
Registers the grant of the village of Chura in Karmma-rāshtra to a brāhmana, by the king encamped at Vijaya-Pulichūla.

cells.date: Regnal year (expressed by a symbol), doubtful Phalguna, Paurnamāsī, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land of the village Pulimbūru in Guddavāi-vishaya, to a certain Sivasarman who was a resident of Kundūru in Kamma-rāshtra, on the occasion when the king crossed the river Godāvari with the object of conquering the eastern region.

Gift of the village of Namiyavada in Prolu-nāṇdu to a certain Adāpi-Appana who was a devoted servant of the king. The inscription states that the king was crowned in Śaka 983, the Sun being in Tala, on the 2nd day of the bright half, Thursday, Kumbha-lagna and the Anuradha-nakshatra.

The first plate is broken at the right end. Registers a gift of Pasupubaru in Outrakura-vishaya to a Brāhmaṇa named Keśavasarman of Paruttic. The dhinapti of the grant was the chief queen Vinayamahādēvi.

Registers that Majavaraiyan (also called Kollimajavan, Piradigandan and Sundaraśolan) permanently fixed the taxes and fines due from the merchants (nagarattār) of Dūsiyūr; and evidently granted these (? in favour of the Paramēśvara temple at that village on the occasion when he constructed a stone well, for (i.e. to a please the spirit of ?) his father who died at 1am (i.e. Ceylon).

The same individual here named Oyriyaran and Piratigāḍivarman gave to the temple of Tirumūlasthānam-uḍaiya-Parmēśvarar at that village, some lands, and a village of the same name to the Amapkuḍi. The temple transferred it to the drummers (uvachchar) who made the five great sounds (pañchamahāśabda) in the temple.
Records the grant of 65 paddy-fields below the big tank of Paruvi in Paruvi-vishaya to certain Kumārasarman, of Vatsa-gōtra and Taittirīya-charaṇa.

cells.remarks: Supplies the Hoysala genealogy from Vinayāditya to Vīra-Ballāla and records that three private individuals of Mangola consecrated the temple of Śrināyaka in the middle of that village and that then theundermentioned under the permission of the king's representative (śrikāryy-ācharya), presented lands and houses for the worship of the god. Also registers grant of land by the mahāpadāyāchāryya Vasudeva-Nāyaka, for a flower-garden of Magra to the temple of Narasīngudeva.

cells.place:

(Hadagali taluk, Bellary district).
cells.language:

cells.language:
Śaka Sadharna, Phalgnup, ba.
di. [8]. Friday, Vyatipāta.
cells.remarks: Damaged in the beginning. The record first mentions that Tribhuvanamalla-Nāgāyadeva the lord of Kulunbapura was ruling over Nolambavadi 32,000 and Masavadi one hundred and forty under the king's immediate supervision. At the king's Brahman minister and dandanāyaka nāyaka. His wife Hebbahabāvi, or Hebbabalāvi, native of Pavina-Padangali (i.e., Huvinahadagalli) built in that village a temple for Kesava and gave grants of land for the worship of the god, for feeding Brahmins, and for a foodgovardhan. Other subsidiary grants were also made; viz., (1) a village for conducting repairs to the temple and for worship was granted by king Tribhuvanamalla encamped at Rājasyakara Kandanapura, on the occasion of his Kaviga-Dandānathu) on the occasion of his making the gift called Viśvachakra; and (2) of money and land by several individuals for betelleave, sandal, worship oblations, perpetual lamps Chaitrapujā, etc.

cells.place: On a rock in the Rangappana-gudda hill near Tambarahalli (Hadagalli taluk, Bellary district).
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the śrī-maṇṭapa of the god Baṇḍeya-Raṅganātha, by the three sons of a certain Sūriyaya of Kennehalli-Yiṭṭigo which was included in Koṭṭūra-sīme.

cells.location: Velagalēru, Bezwāda taluk, Kistna district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same rock
cells.remarks: Damaged at the bottom. Seems to record a private agreement between a pūjāri of Bandeya-Bangaiyya and another.

cells.location: Kambāduru
cells.place: On the same rock
cells.remarks: Mentions one Sidaiya, son of Vābaṇayya, was presented [perhaps in the form of a temple] gold, village and land for the merit of his parents.

cells.location: Kambāduru
cells.place: On the same rock
cells.remarks: Records that this deep pond (gaḍḍa-goṇḍe) was constructed by Sūriyaya, son of Vābaṇayya, the śēnabhōga (Shānabhōga) of Yiṭṭige and a devoted worshipper of Baṇḍeya-Raṅganātha.

cells.place: On a stone set up in front of the Channa-kēśavasvāmin temple at Chinnahoṭṭūr (Alur taluk, Bellary district).
cells.remarks: Records the foundation of the temple of Adikēśavanātha by [Pratāpa] Harihararāya. On this, the Śrīvaishṇavas of the 18 nāḍus and others made a gift of five kolagas of land for oblations.

cells.place: On a pillar of the Bhōgadēvasvāmin temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: States that this is the inscribed pillar of Naraseinha Sarasvati who had the adjunots Sapta-prathama dēvayuga Sambhutraya Sri-Narasinihva varapraddā Vēdāntakrimita (!).

cells.place: On a slab near a well to the west of the same temple.
cells.remarks: In archaic characters. Seems to record that the well (gūḍar) [was dug by] a certain Gumasri [Ma]-prada, son of Arjuna.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Bōnēśvara temple at Pyāpali (Dhone taluk, Kurnool district).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions a certain Veṅkaṭapa-Nayanivāru.

cells.place: On a slab at the entrance into the Channakēśavasvāmin temple at Gun-daḷa (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Registers that the mahājanas of Rāmarāja granted the villages of Jadavapāḍima in the district of Drōgāchala and Jonnagiri in the district of Guṭṭi, to the god Channarāya of Guṇḍala, for worship and festivals.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field, in the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged at the end. Registers that Dođla Veñkatanayaningāru having died, his son appointed an agent to supervise the Dođla charatics, viz. [the construction of] the prakāra-wa], pavilions, flowergardens, ponds and others in the temple of Channakeśava-Perumā! at Gundala in Dhōni-stma, and gave him some land in Tādāru with the consent of the Reqđi, Karanam, and the Tulāri of that village. Mutilated. Seems to record a grant of land to the pūjāris and danoing-women attached to some temple.

cells.place: On a slab from Dhanakōṭa preserved in the College of Arts, Guntur (Guntur taluk, Guntur district).
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Seems to record a grant of land to the pūjāris and danoing-women attached to some temple.

cells.location: Zūpuḍi, Bezwada taluk, Kistna district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a second slab preserved in the same office.
cells.remarks: Do. [Gift of sheep for a lamp to the god Bu[d]-dhadēva, by a lady.]

cells.location: Kudaravalli, Gudivāda taluk, Kistna district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: This may be a grant made in continuation of No. 140. States that a certain merchant of [Po]pūṅgonda gave for the merit of his parents and of his elder brother, [55] sheep for a perpetual lamp to the temple of Buddėśvara.

cells.location: Itaparru, Gudivada taluk, Kistna district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab brought from Yenamadala and preserved in the same office.
cells.date:
Śaka 11[7]3, Vaisakha, śu.
di. 8, giridshitri-tithi, Monday.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions (Kōti) Beta, Mahāshamandalesvara[(i.e., Vennamādala) founded the temple of Krishna in that village and granted the required land [for its upkeep]. Queen Gaupamādevi also gave land in the village of Garagapada, for the worship of the god. The management of the village assigned some tolls. The marriage fees granted by Gaupamanadēvi [to the mahājanas] of the village were also transferred by them to the temple of Gopinātha (i.e., Krishna).

cells.location: Pāṇem, Nandyal taluk, Kurnool district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of the Uttarēśvara temple at Peddakodamagundla (Palnad taluk, Guntur district).
cells.date: Śuka 1435, Sri-mukha, Sravaṇa, ba. di. 12, Friday, the Sun being in Kita (i.e., scorpion) combined with Harshaṇa (Xōga) and Bava (Karaṇa).
cells.remarks: States that a certain Mulhēsvaracharya (also called Mahēsvarayati) founded the temple of Uttareśvara with the shrine (Sankaraprasada), bull, flagstaff, minor deities, Vireśvara (i.e., Virabhadra) and Kalika. He is further stated to have built the compound-wall, the pond, the garden and the well attached to the temple and to have provided for the worship of the linga and distribution of food in charity. He was the successor in Pāṣupata-Śaṅbhavuditshā, of Sankaraguru who attained Siva-bood, on the given date and had become a linga through the great penunce of [his teacher] Mantramārtiguru.

cells.place: On a second slab set up in the same place.
cells.date: Śaka 1069, Prabbuva . . . su. di. 5, Thursday, Vishu [v]ā-Saṅkrānti.
cells.remarks: Registers that the taxes Penuankika, Vurffuruvula and others, due in and around the agrahāra of Godamagōla to Yiśanu-Peggunḍa, an officer of the king, who was of the Haihaya family and was a member of the Haihaya family, for the maintenance of worship in the temples at that agrahāra, for lamps and offerings and for supporting ascetics and students.

cells.place: On a third slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Montions the [Mahāmaṇḍulēsvara] Rāmarāja Tirumala[rāja] and the village Kārempa[ndi].

cells.place: On a fourth slab in the same place
cells.date:
thana vāsi sadi.
Śaka 1810, Sūryadhari, Margasira, ba.
di. 8, Friday.
cells.remarks: Quotes inscription No. 143 noted above and records that Lanka Saṅkhayya one of the descondants of Lanka Mantramārtiguru who was represented by a linga in the temple of Uttareśvarasāmin granted land, the income from which was to be devoted for worship and offerings to the said Mantramārtiguru. The English dates on which the gifts were made and the extent of lands in aores and cents are also given.

cells.place: On a slab set up at the entrance into the Rāmasvāmi temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Records that the same individual renovated the temple of Starāmasvami at Pedukodamagundla built by his father about 60 years prior to the date of the inscription and set apart some of his own lands at Miriyāla and Paluvāya for the exclusive use of the temple. These lands had to be onlitated by his descendants and the income therefrom was to be utilized for the worship of the god. Registers the grant of the village Zak'kīred[d]ipal[ī]e for the worship of Papavinasanadēva and Rudradava at Bejavāda and for maintaining two feeding-houses one for the Jamgaus and another for Brahmapus.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field at Zakkampūḍi (Bezwada taluk, Kistna district).
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Zak'kīred[d]ipal[ī]e for the worship of Papavinasanadēva and Rudradava at Bejavāda and for maintaining two feeding-houses one for the Jamgaus and another for Brahmapus.

cells.place: On a slab bearing the figure of an Āñja-nēya, near a well at Velagaleru (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Refors to the god Anumanta (Hanaman) near (the well) Venikatādri-kōnērn and to the gift of a lump stand (P) by a certain Singadāseri of [Red]dipalle.

cells.place: On a slab near a tank in the same village
cells.remarks: This is the chnirity-well of the son of Garigipāti Venkanna.

cells.place: Near a rock-out coll at Mogalrajapuram (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Refers to a certain Choḷa-Chāṭi Vivirāḍu.

cells.location: Mahanandi, Nandyal taluk, Kurnool district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab near a tank in the Musalman 'Agrahāra' at Mallikapuram (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: States that Musanadu-Eli Kutumana-Malka-Odaya, a friend of the Sultan, reduced by his prowess Konđupalli and other hill-fortresses and established a feeding house (langara) at Kedarathada which he had founded near Peyyalagallu, south of Konđapalli, for the helpless, blind and cripple and for derives. For the maintenance of this (langara), he gave the two villages Kavurđru and Kedarathada. "Mulik Qut-bul-Mulik set aside the income derived from certain villages for the maintenance of a langar, in memory of khwāja khizr." (Dr. J. Horovitz).

cells.place: On another face of the same pillar
cells.remarks: “Malik Qulb-ul-Mulk set aside the income derived from certain villages for the maintenance of a langar, in memory of Khwaja Khijar” (Dr. J. Horowitz).

cells.place: On a slab set up on the bund of a tank at Kavulūru (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Records that this one of the Akkannadēva pillars fixed by a certain Sēvādri Ramanappa and his elder brother, in the tank constructed by them near Kavulūru.

cells.place: On a stone lying in a palmyra tope, in the same village.
cells.date:
Śaka 1.305, Vibhava, (wrong)
Pushya ba. di.
14, Sunday.
Donbtful
cells.remarks: Records that the tank Pāṭi-Nayunḍu of Intamuk-kūru was gifted to the gods Chena-Malhatha and Varadagōpātha of Kavulūru, a flower-garden with fruit trees, for the erit of his parents.

cells.location: Bukkapaṭnam, Penukoṇḍa taluk, Anantapur district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field to the north of the village leading to Kondapalli from the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Mōgalarāju-Mahāpātra who was governing the country.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the village of Yenikepadu (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Register that the village Venakapāḍu was granted to the temple of Rājanārāyaṇan at Bejavāḍa. The Gajapati Pratāpa-Purushōttamadēva-Mahārāja Mahā-pātra apparently ratified the grant and distributed Venakapāḍu among the servants of that temple. These latter included the worshippers, accountants, purohits, goldamiths (?), dancing-girls, painters, men who rang the bell, gardeners, gate-watchmen, the blower of the conch and torch-bearer.

cells.place: On a pillar set up in the same place
cells.remarks: Registers that the king granted lands in the neighbourhood of Veṇakapūḍi to the temple of Kēśavadēva at Bejavāḍa. The grant was intended for propitiations, offerings, perpetual lamps, dancing-girl and other services. ... Mutti-gari. Mentions the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara [Obs?]-gi-Dōrayarāja.

cells.place: On a pillar in a field of the same village
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Mentions the Mahāmayđalēvara [Cha]-gi-Dōrayaraja.

cells.place: On the cross beam at the entrance into the Veṅkaṭēśvarasvāmin temple at Zupūḍi (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Records that the beam was the gift of the two pafia-sɛzmi (merchant?) brothers, Śambhurāju and Ayyappa.

cells.location: Gōraṇṭla, Hindupur taluk, Anantapur district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab lying in the Gōkḷanna-cheruvu at Kuduravalli (Gudivada taluk, Kistna district).
cells.remarks: A certain Abudalu Husenu servant of Abudulakhanu, built the sluice of the tank at Kudarapalli.

cells.remarks: In old Telugu characters. The inscription is partly mutilated at the beginning and seems to register a gift of land by Kaḍaladēva, son of Baṇdayāri, to a certain Ba'sa/riya of Bugalpūrti in the villages of Baṇdayāri and Kuḍuravalli in the Kaṇṭikē-viśaya. The second of the village is probably identical with Ilaparu.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of the Vīranārāyaṇasvāmin temple at Panem (Nandyal taluk, Kurnool district).
cells.date:
Şaka 1241, Siddharthi, Māgbn, sū. dī.
15, Monday, lunar eolipse.
cells.remarks: Registers that while the chief minister Mummadi Bhaṭṭa was governing the sovereign country including Kuḍuravalli and other places, he constructed a tank on the south side of Panya. Certain fees (māra) to be paid by the residents of Panya and a tūmu of grain (of each kind) from the markets held in the specified villages, were granted for the maintenance of the temple of Śrī-Vīrunārāyaṇadēva of the village.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of the Papāśharasvāmin temple, in the same village.
cells.date: .. Şuka 1461, Virodhi, Vaisakhnu sū. dī. 15, lunar eolipse.
cells.remarks: Vakīḍa Peḍada-Nāyuḍu, son of Bokkasam Peḍada-Nāyuḍu, a servant of Kṛiśhṇapādarāya, granted the hīvalikaṇam (police fee), for the enjoyment of the god Vīranārāyaṇa of Kurunōl, on all lands in Kaṇdanavōlu (Kurnool), held by the temple in that village and in the agrahāra villages of Bupālināḍu and Liṅgapurān.

cells.location: Aska (Asika), Aska taluk, Ganjam district — Odisha
cells.place: On a second slab set up in the same place
cells.remarks: Himmadi-Nāyuḍu, son of Bokkasam Devapa-Nāyuḍu, granted the village of Bhaddalapādu in Pānam-sīma to the worshiorship (taṁmaḍa) of the god Papī-keśvara of Pāneya for conducting oblations and other services in the temple.

cells.location: Budagulo, Aska taluk, Ganjam district — Odisha
cells.place: On a third slab set up in the same place.
cells.date:
.. Şaka 1425, Kadhirodgari, Śrāvupa, sū. dī.
16, M. nday.
cells.remarks: The same chief, for the merit of the king and Narasa-Nāvingarānu, land in the village Panem, included in Panugonda-sīva-di., to four sthānīkas of the Papikēśvara temple for 'building a millage, and conducting the services in the temple.

cells.location: Garbham, Gajapatinagaram taluk, Vizagapatam district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a fourth slab set up in the same place.
cells.date: Śaka, 1 Rūdhirōdgāri, Phālguna, śu. di. 16, Monday.
cells.remarks: This inscription records the grant registered in No. 169 with a few changes in the wording.

cells.location: Havinahalu-Virapura, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a pillar in the court-yard of the same temple.
cells.remarks: The oldest which is in Kanarese records that a certain Pallapāḍiyan obeyed the orders of the king and gave a grant of land to the three state that Vibhūti Gauraya visited the temple.

cells.place: On a pillar in the Mukha-maṇḍapa of the same temple.
cells.remarks: The visit of the same Vibhūti Gauraya is mentioned and it is stated that he was born at [Ma]hārājapalli near Orugallu, settled on the top of Śrīgiri and gave the village of Pāyavallapūḍi as a gift. Another record in Telugu on the same pillar states that a certain Akṣama paved with stone the Appālike (?) of the maṇḍapa.

cells.place: On a slab lying in the Āñjanēya temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Registers that Komara Timma-Nayuḍu, son of Narasidhva-Nayuḍu and grandson of the Nayankdahārya China-Veñkatappa-Nayuḍu granted land to a certain Anumabōyi.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the same temple
cells.date: Śaka 14[28*] Krodhana, śu. di. 3, Monday, Kanya, Bṛihaspati.
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the Inam village of Iḍḍahanti-ēma to Mallikārjuna one of the three self born liṅgas for the merit of his father Narasiṅgarāya.

cells.location: Somalāpura, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On the dhvajastambha in the Mahanandisvarasvāmin temple at Mahanandi (Nandyal taluk, Kurnool district).
cells.date:
Saka 1446, Tarapa, Magha, ba. di.
14, Monday, Śivaratri.
cells.remarks: Records that a merchant built the maṇḍapa called mukhabhadram at the southern entrance into the tank (puṣkariṇī) surrounded by Ayōga-palli, in the temple of Mahanandīśvara.

cells.location: Old-Bhatrahalli, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On an iron pillar near the western gate of the same temple.
cells.date:
Saka 1832, Vikrita, Magha, ba. di.
13, Friday.
cells.remarks: The great grandmother (?) of Tipparāju, son of Pinu-Tipparāju, son of Velugōṭi Gaṅgērāju-Chennajaṅgaru, the hero of Kroṭṭacherlakōṭa, set up the iron pillar before the shrine of Mahānandīśvara.

cells.place: On seven detached stones in the same temple.
cells.remarks: In ancient characters of the 8th and 9th centuries of the Christian era. Four in Telugu-Kanarese record the names Sōrigēśam[pu]nna-mṛidēmunī; Ayōga-palli; Śrī-Vajramahāpuruvarar and Tellapāṅgi-Apparāju. One in Nāgari, reads śrī-Lallavikāgēna [P]arāja.

cells.location: Oruvāy (Vōravāyi), Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On six other detached stones
cells.remarks: Contains the signatures of devotees, three of which seem to be rather old. Among these are [Ja]lyaravi (Chirutejōnidhi) a mine of architect-intelligence.

cells.place: On a slab set up at the entrance into the Lakshmīnārāyaṇasvāmin temple at Bukkapaṭṇam (Penukonda taluk, Anantapur district).
cells.date: Śaka 1463, Plava, Āśvija, ba. di. 13, Monday.
cells.remarks: Records that Peḍḍirāju under orders of Rāma-bhaṭ-layaru remitted the rājapulēṭu tax (?) in the (Chirutejōnidhi) for the merit of the king.

cells.place: On another slab set up in the same place
cells.date: Śaka 1464, Śuhbakrīt, Chaitra, ba. di. 6, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: Registers the remission of taxes on marriages and the offerings on the earnings of Brahmans for the merit of the king. Kānubhatlayya issued the orders and Peddirajayya conveyed them to the reddis and karṇams of the village of Krottucheruvu.

cells.location: Nalluḍi, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On the rock below the chauḍeśvari temple in the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1503, Vrishe. Bhadrapuda, ba. di. 12, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Registers that Delavāyi Veṭkuṭ:[p*]pa-Nayuḍu under orders of Mēgōti Timma-Nayuḍu the agent and minister of the king, remitted the taxes naga-ribirāṭa Asarechchālu and birudulu due on the lands owned at Bukkasāgaram and Anantapuram by the temple of Chavuđōevari of Krottacheruvu-Bukkusāga:im.

cells.location: Bailūr, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a slab lying near a sluice of the tank, in the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1455, Vija-ya, Phālguna, śu. di. 15, Saturday.
cells.remarks: Registers that Bhaṇḍārada Timmanna, son of Chikka-rāya made rent-free, the dēvadāya and brāhma-dēya lands below the tank of Hosakere, included in Penugonda, a district of Yeraṇā[ru]-rājya. These had been so enjoyed since the time of Chikka-rāya but had been neglected in course of time owing to some disturbance in the interior. The grant was made on the occasion when the king performed the Lakshahōma ceremony at Varadara-jamna-pēṭṭa. The stone was put up by Koṇḍaya under orders of Timmanna at the elephant-sluice of the tank.

cells.location: Sindigeri, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a rock near the tank in the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged at the beginning. Registers that the dēvadāya and brāhmadēya lands under the tank Krottucheruvu in Penugonda-rājya which had been held rent-free (sarvamānya) from the time of Chikka-rāya had been re-assessed on account of certain irregularities in the accounts. They are now at Śivanasamudram on state business ordered that the lands might be restored as before and this was announced on the occasion of the Lakshahōma ceremony conducted at Penugonda. Kaṇama-Nāyuḍu had this inscription engraved under orders of Rāyasam Koṇḍamarusayya-dēmarasayya.

cells.place: On the west wall of the maṇḍapa in the Madhavarāyasvāmin temple at Gorantla (Hindupur taluk, Anantapur district).
cells.date: Śaka 1446, Tarapa, Kartika, iu. di. 12, Monday, Utthana-dvadasi, Chi-(trā)-nakshatra.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Registers that the agent of Vakiṭi Adepa-Nāyuḍu granted land to the Vishnu (Peru-māḷ) temple at Gorantla for maintaining festive processions on the daśami days of the month.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions Gōraṭla-atma which was conferred as a fief (nāyankara) on the son of Vakiṭi Mallapa-Nāyuḍu.

cells.location: Kaggallu, Adoni taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Timmapa-Nayuqu, son of Vakiti Mallapa-Nayuqu ordered the sthādnikas, citizens and the temple cook to revivo the processions in the Perumal temple at Gōrantīla which had been neglected till then.

cells.location: Dammūru, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone built into the floor of a maṇḍapa in the same temple.
cells.date: Śaka 15[82], Sadharapa, Pushya, su. di. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to regis'er the grant of certain taxes (?) to the temple of Madhavesvara at Gōrantīla for the merit of the king and of Chika-Venkatappa-Nayuda.

cells.place: On the capital of a pillar in the same maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: The four pillars on the east side of the platform (jagali; were the gift of Tirupati-vāru.

cells.place: On a stone built into the floor in the Tiruvidhēvarasvāmin temple at Āśka (Āśka Zamindārī, Gañjām district).
cells.remarks: Babu Sasi Bhushan Palit, B.A., to whom this record was submitted for interpretation says that its translation is "Hundred Samvat Kanya, 15th day" and believes that "the temple was constructed or dedicated to Tiravidhesvarasvāmin" on this day. This is not likely; for the characters appear to be more modern.

cells.location: Sōmasamudram, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a rook near a hill at Boḍagullo, on the Boyaṇi-Kallikeṭa road (Ganjam district).
cells.king: Muḥammandu Kulli Kuṭb Shāh [Nijam Padshāh] (Muḥammad Quṭb Shāh).
cells.date:
Śaka 1512, Virodhin, Chaitra, first fortnight,
10 Thursday.
cells.remarks: Refers to general of the king, called Śaika Saharalli of Gujapati throne, who is the commander of the 84 forts of the Andhra Tri-liṅga (country). Mention is also made of the usurpation of the Gujapati throne by Siṅga of the Bahubalēndra family. A tank on the west bank of the Āśīka-Laṅgula (i.e., the river Laṅgulya flowing close by Āśka) called Siṅgasagaram was constructed by the Muḥammudan ohi-ul-Saha evidently in honour of the usurper Siṅga (Narasimha). Seems to mention the names of persons who had the image [of Vinayaka] out out the cross-beam.

cells.place: On the cross-beam of the inner entrance into the Mallikārjuna temple at Garbham (Gajapatinagaram taluk, Vizagapatam district).
cells.remarks: Seems to mention the name or names of persons who had the image [of Vinayaka] cut on the cross beam.

cells.location: Lotugedda — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Virabhadrasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Sōmaya-Pa[p]dalu founded this temple of Viresvara and gave to it a grove of trees (?) and a garden at Bimanapalli.

cells.place: On a stone called Kirukana-bailu gāji-kallu near Hardur (Coorg).
cells.remarks: Mentions Ereyapa at the beginning and refers to the death of a hero. The record registers also the gift of a kulnādu.

cells.place: On a stone in aramane-kađaṅga, in the reserved forest near Cheralasrimangala of the same province.
cells.remarks: The king granted the land belonging to Lakutanakote as a rent-free gift to Lingannodēru-devara who was perhaps his spiritual teacher.

cells.place: On a stone in Muddnvirapa-Puttamma's garden at Uluguli, in the same province.
cells.remarks: Gift of land to a hero who fell in the cuttle-raid of Kamayavalli.

cells.location: Bellary district, Bellary taluk : — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Anjaneya temple at Havinahalu-Virapura.
cells.date: Śaka 987, Parthiva, Śrāvaṇa, śa. di. 5, Monday.
cells.remarks: Records that Udayāditya, Sindavāra lord of Bhōgāvati-pura, and a Sāmanta of Trailokyamalla Nanni Nolamba-Pallava Permānadi lord of Khol, the best of cities who was himself a combatant, son of Chintarasa and a certain Palimayya the right of collecting the tax called manneya-sāṁyuva-āteye at Douḍavatti.

cells.location: Kuntanahalu, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On another stone in the same place
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Registers the permanent grant of diamonds of the tank at Doṇḍavāṭe to a certain Marasinga-Nāyaka on the north side with the permission of Nudana-Nāyaka who was enjoying that village as a rent-free gift (umbali). Gift of the village of Douḍavāṭi in Kupyōḍu-sime, to the god Bikkēśvaradēva consecrated by the king in the name and for the merit of Narasapa- Nāyaka's son Bukkapa. Bukkapa's grandfather Īśvar [a]-Nāyaka is also mentioned.

cells.place: On the stone built into a water channel near the same place.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Chintikamaḥla by Achyutarāya to the temple of Prasanna-Virabhadrēśvara at Honalagallu, for the merit of his father Narasarpa-Nāyaka. Gift of land by the king to the temple of Mahādēva at Arakere.

cells.location: Chintikamaḥlu
cells.place: On a Nandi-stone in front of the Anjaneya temple
cells.remarks: Registers the git of the village Chintikamaḥla by Achyutarāya to the temple of Prasanna-Virabhadrēśvara at Honalagallu, for the merit of his father Narasarpa-Nāyaka. Gift of land by the king to the temple of Mahādēva at Arakere.

cells.place: On a stone set up near a well at Somalapura.
cells.date: Śaka 95 [3], Pram[ō]da, Āshāḍha, ba. di. 10, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Incomplete and mutilated. Gives a long list of the titles of a king who belonged to the Sinda family. One of the titles was that he was born of the race of Drishṭivisha.

cells.place: On a stone 'set up in the village of Old Bhatrahalli.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions Ballakunde-nāļu and seems to record a gift of land by the Pallava chief Jagadēkamalla Nolamba-Pallava Permānadi.

cells.location: Baḍaqanahalli
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Vighnēśvara temple
cells.date: Śaka 949, Pra[bhava], Vaiśākha, ba. di. 5, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of ōrvaya to three Brāhmaṇas who had placed the body of Nolambamahādēvi in the waters of the Ganges. Mentions queen Dovaladēvi who was a Nolamba princess and the Pallava chief Udayāditya styled 'the lord of Kāñchipura'.

cells.location: Oravayi
cells.place: On a mutilated stone lying near the Rāmaliṅgēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Much damaged. This record is a duplicate of No. 200.

cells.place: On another stone lying in the same place
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.place: On a stone lying in front of the Añjanēya temple near Guttiganūru.
cells.date: Śaka 1161, Vikārin, Jyēsh[tha], ba. di. 5, Friday.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a certain named Basavarayya to the temple of Mukhyap[r]āṇadēva (Añjanēyan) which he had funded on the west side of Yennemeguru on the road from Kaynōḍu to Vijayanagara for the merit of Iliyira tirumalaianātha, amātya, son of Sahasayadeva-Mahādēvarasa. In arbhala character. Mentions certain Guṇamaṇavagapda.

cells.location: Nallādi — Karnataka
cells.place: On a hero-stone near the Niddhinēvura temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land to Dōvarāja-puṇḍa of Doppanayaka for the worship of Mallikarjuna. Mentions the Mahamandalesvara Ballaraya Bivaranu.

cells.location: Karekallu, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone set up in the verandah of Western Chāluthe Basavēśvara temple at Ballur. kya.
cells.dynasty: Western Chālukya †
cells.date: [Chālukya- Vikrama year] Dundubhi Saṁvatsara, Āshāḍha ba. di. 10, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Seems to record a gift of land at Simdamgore for a feeding house. Mentions the teacher Nirvāṇadēva.

cells.location: Sindigeri — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Mallēśvara temple
cells.date: Śaka 1125, Durmati, Bhādrapada, śu. di. 8, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a subordinate of the Sinda Mahāma[n]ḍalēśvara Bacharasa(chamanarasa)and to the teacher Nirvāṇidēva who in his turn appears to have a-signed it to the temple of Mallikārjuna at Si[n]digeri, for the merit of the Sinda chief Bacharasa and the feeding house. Nirvānidēva was the third in succession after Vānadeva alias Vākōtchinkavarari, the achārya of the temple of hyavambhidēvam at Muingumla.

cells.location: Gudadūru, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On another stone near the same temple ..
cells.remarks: (Gift of land in the district of Pallakunde 300 by (gift of land in the district of) Rēta-Mahārāja who was evidently the subordinate of the Pallava chief Trailōkyamalla Īśvaranōmbabhatāra Nursingahēdēva, 'the lord of Kañchipura'.

cells.location: Śirivaram, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone near the Basavēśvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by Udayāditya, her-band of Sigādēvi, to l'harābhyudaya for the worship of god, Mahadeva. He was entitled Jagadōkamalla Nolamba Pallava Permandi and was ruling at rumpili as his permanent capital (kaṭṭava).

cells.location: Sañjīvarāyanikōṭe, Bellary taluk, Bellary district — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone lying in the neighbourhood of Kaggallu.
cells.date: Śaka 9[5]5, Śrīmukha, Māgha, śu. di. 6, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa- Saṁkrānti.
cells.remarks: Records that this image of Virabhadra was set up by Kannamanavva, the mother of Hummujevve who was the wife of a Mahasupalēśvara.

cells.location: Dammuru — Karnataka
cells.place: On the stone pedestal of Virabhadra's shrine
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.place: On the rocky floor of the Ramalingesvara Western Chālu- Tribhuvanamalla [Vikramaditya VI], 'rultemple in the same village. kya.
cells.dynasty: Chālukya †
cells.date: Śaka [Vikramaditya VI], 31, Vaiśākha, ba. di. 6, Monday.
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.location: Kolur
cells.place: On a stone lying in the Satyanarayana-svamin temple
cells.date: 10th year, Prabhava, Phalguna, su. 2, Thursday, Uttarayana-Sankramana.
cells.remarks: Registers that while the Sinda chiefs Immađi Bhima and his brother Rāchamulla were ruling the Ballakandeśaya, a native of Kojāru, named Rēvagavupda, built temples at that village for Siva, Vishnu, Aditya (Sun), Vighnesvaru, and Bhairva. Gifts of land were made for the worship of these gods by the first of the two Sinda chiefs mentioned already.

cells.location: Somasamudram — Karnataka
cells.place: On a stone built into the mud wall in front of the Lakshminarayanasvamin temple
cells.date: Saka 1478, Nala, Ashadha, su. di. 11, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the Muhā Janas of Sōmusamudra in Kurugoda-shme, a sub-division of Mūganadā-ventheya in Hastinavati-vajita, for maintaining a palanquin-procession on Ekālaśi days, in the temple of Lakshminarāyana of that village.

cells.place: On a rock in a field of the same village
cells.date: Śaka, 161[4], Āngirns, Chaitra, ba. di. 15. Tuesday.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record the construction of a well (gajāgonda) by the residents of Sōmasamudra.

cells.location: Hirehalu
cells.place: On the eastern entrance into the old fort
cells.remarks: Partly damaged. Registers that under orders of a certain chief whose name is not clear on the impression, Sivaji Mullahari-Pant built the fort at Kiro-Hirehalu with bastions and gateway.

cells.location: Yalpi-Kaggallu
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Anjaneya temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Kaggallu, by Raghunatharayar, son of the Mahamandalesvara Ramaraja-Tirumalarajayya-Tirumala, to the temple of Mallikarjuna at Hirehalu.

cells.location: Yalpi
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Anjaneya temple
cells.remarks: Mentions that a certain Timmanna built a choultry and made provision for feeding twelve Brahmans at Yalpi which was a mukhasa-village granted to him by Krishnaraya to maintain horses. The charity was made for the merit of king Achyutaraya-Maharaya.

cells.location: Nelapalli, Punganuru taluk, Chittoor district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On another stone near the same temple
cells.date: Saka 1431, Sukla, Magha, ba. di. 14, Sivaratri.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register the remission of marriage-tax in the district Yalpi-sime for the merit of the king, by a favourite chief whose name is lost in the damaged portion of the inscription.

cells.location: Nelapalli, Punganuru taluk, Chittoor district — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a rock at the same place
cells.remarks: Records that the Mahāma. dālaśevara Rāmarajayya-deva Muhammad, the agent of the king, remitted the taxes payable by the barbers, in Yalappeya-shme

cells.place: On a stone in a field five miles east of Kuntanabalu.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions a Muhammadan chief named Ibhrahim Boku and seems to register a gift of land.

cells.location: Modalli, Kollegal taluk, Coimbatore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone in another field five miles from the same village.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions a certain muhammadan chief whose name is not clear and records grant of land to a certain Bud[da]sa of Bennakallu.

cells.location: Bupanagudi
cells.place: On a rock near the Belu-Anjaneya image
cells.remarks: Registers that this pond (kere) and the image of Hanumanta were made by a certain Malappa, son of Sirumapa of Govindavadi.

cells.place: On a stone near the Polalapayyaḍi in the ruine village.
cells.date:
Śaka 170[9], Plavuñga, Vaisakhu, su. di. 1, Wednesday.
Lost
cells.remarks: Records the building (?) of the temple of Potalingasvāmi and of a stone maṇdapa, by two private individuals.

cells.location: Uragadam, Chingleput taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone near a well in the same village.
cells.remarks: Fragment. Gift of land at Yajape to the temple of [Nara]yanadeva. To the same temple were also granted the tolls (mīlavise) on the grains passing either way through Rapalegudiya-thanya in [Yajape]ya-stme.

cells.location: Yetitina-Budehalu — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Anjaneya temple
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama year 32, Sarvajit, Karttika, śu. di. 6, Friday.
cells.remarks: Mentions that Soverasa-Kavarasa and Duggaraja built a mandupa, probably for the use of travelers, and granted land for its upkeep.

cells.place: On another stone in front of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Unfinished.

cells.place: On a stone lying in front of the Hanumāvanyu temple at the same village.
cells.remarks: In old characters; much damaged. Mentions Saluki Eynamma whose servant is stated to have split up a stone. Seems to register also a gift of land by the 80 0 of Baḍuvanahalli.

cells.place: On a stone lying near the Mallēśvara temple at Moka
cells.date: Śaka 14[31], Sukla, Magba, bu. di. 14, Sivarātri.
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.location: Karekallu — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone near the Virabhadra temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a private individual to the temple of Prasanna-Kēśvanātha at Kurōkallu.

cells.place: On a stone in a field near Karekallu- Virapura.
cells.remarks: Registers a dead granted by the Dēsāyi and Nōdūkula-karpī of Mōke stone to a certain Mallikēsāyi, son of Viramallikēsāyi. The latter was evidently to be in charge of the small bastions (hūḍe) of Mōke-stme.

cells.location: Sindavala
cells.place: On a stone set up in the Ramaliṅgēśvara temple
cells.date: 5th year, Sūdhūrapa, Kārttika, su. di. 1, Monday, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Mentions that under orders of 'o Mahāprathāna, Bānamurgade, Menevergade, Sēnādhipati and the Udandāyaka, Anantapālayya, the Mahāprathāna-hergade Bālapayya made a gift of land for worship, repairs, ste., to the temple of Sonesvaradepa built by the residents of Sindavolalu in the Sindavādi thousand district.

cells.place: On a stone in the street at Gudaduru
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the tatāradikāra ('watchman's fee') of Guuḍanjūru, a village; 'Mōke-time.

cells.location: Sirivaram — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Īśvara temple
cells.date: Śaka 966, Tāraṇa, Vaiśākha, śu. di. 5, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Kappekallu in Ballakuṇḍe 300, to the ascetic Jyēshṭharāśi-Bhaṭāra, by the chief Pallarasa, a subordinate of Oḍeyāditya for the temple of Mahādēva and for a maṭha. The Brāhmaṇas also got a share in the village. The occasion for the grant was the installation of Trailōkyamalla Nanni-Noḷambādhirāja.

cells.location: Sañjīvarāyanikōṭe — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone in a field
cells.remarks: In old characters. Refers to the 8,000 of Būdavāgilu and to the Mahāsāmantādhipati Rājiyaṇṇa Ereyammam. Records gift of land to a temple by Kadamba-Kāmarasa and other gāmuṇḍas.

cells.location: Chidambaram, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone in a street at Kolagallu
cells.date: Śaka 888, Raktākshi, Āshāḍha, śu. di. 5, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land at Sūjiṅgallu by a certain Chaṅga-gāvuṇḍa to the ascetic Satyarāśi-Bhaṭāra for maintaining a feeding house in the maṭha. The grant was confirmed by Gajadharayya, chief of Svāmi Kārttikēya-tapōvana, ruling at Kolgalu.

cells.place: On a stone near a well in the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a grant for a temple, a maṭha and vidyādāna.

cells.place: On a stone in another street of the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 889, Kshaya, Phalgupa, śu. dī. 6, Sunday.
cells.remarks: States that Kṛishṇa died (in this year) and Khoṭṭiga succeeded him. The record is a eulogy of the god Kumāra who was installed at Kolagalagrāma and whose agent was Gadādhara.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On a stone in front of the Āñjanēya temple
cells.date: Śaka 1584, Śubhakṛit, Kārttika, śu. di. 15, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village of Handarahaḷu by the king to a certain Kodam Śivabasavappa. The record states that the village was originally granted to the king (?) by Alamshanva Sāhēbu for vajīrike (i.e. for being Vazir).

cells.place: On the north wall of the ruined Īśvara temple at Adapur (Pullampet taluk, Cuddapah district), right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of money for rice offerings to the temple of Pāvanāśamuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār by a certain Pūśandai Dēvan-Āḻvān alias Dōratta Vēḷān of Māgaral.

cells.location: Chidambaram, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall, left of entrance
cells.remarks: Registers that the Mahāmaṇḍapa in the temple of Pāpanāśamuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār, at Kāmachchōḷanallūr in Mēr-Pākkai-nāḍu a sub-division of Adhirājēndra-maṇḍala, was the gift of Śēdiyarāyan a native of Tirukkachchiyūr in Ti[ru*]-Śaṅgunri-nāḍu a sub-division of Kaḷattūr-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: Chidambaram, Chīdambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.date: Śaka 1202, Pra[māthin], Mīna, śu. di. 2, Monday, Aśvinī.
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 Māḍai for a lamp, to the same temple, by Paṇḍitan Pakkiḷān Kuṇḍarādittan Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷ.

cells.location: Chidambaram, Chīdambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a mutilated stone in the hillock near the same village.
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Mentions Aḍḍappa and seems to record a gift of land. B-gins with the historical introduction pāmḍ'iu panara.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||113" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 113</button>

cells.location: Chidambaram, Chīdambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a rock in a field at Nolapalli (Vanga-nur Zamindari, Chittoor district).
cells.remarks: Registers that while the king was encamped at Ve'nvujuponne in Pagevi-nādu he conferred the title of Mummadīgavaga Pallavaditya Nojambasetti on a B-ligaga merchant of Koyaturu and presenting him with royal ineignia gave for his perpetual enjoyment as Ko'dage the village of Kolatoru in Puli-dādu converting it into a mercantile town (nagara) and named Pallavadityapura. In the same old characters as No. 242. Refers to the 48,000 (of the mercantile community?), to Mumma[di*] Uvarasetti of Kāñohipura and to his younger brother Sundurnchola-Dharmasetti.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||114" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 114</button>
