cells.place: On the same rock
cells.remarks: In the same old characters as No. 242. Refers to the 48,000 (of the mercantile community?), to Mumma[di*] Uvarasetti of Kāñohipura and to his younger brother Sundurnchola-Dharmasetti.

cells.place: On a here-slab in a field of the same village.
cells.remarks: Registers that in a face-to-face tiger hont arranged by Srikanthnyan, son of Māvnlivap--Vichchadirar alias Pujalammaraiyar, a certain Indappap pierced a tiger and died with it.

cells.place: On a stone in front of the Nandi-mandapa of the Doḍḍadēvīśvara temple at Moḍalli (Kollegal taluk, Coimbatore district).
cells.date: Śaka 1456, Jaya, Phalguna, śu. di. 5, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Registers that Mādappaṛya, the agent of Bam-p-puya, who was beating the burden of the kingdom, with the king "restored the villages and lands belonging to the temple of Mallikārjuna at Oḍi Moḍahalli in the same sime and [remitted] its taxes in his favour".

cells.place: On another stone in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the temple of M.linathadēva at Moḍaballi and seems to register a gift of tolls.

cells.place: On a stone set up in a field of the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1813, Prajōtpatti, Phālgupa, sū. di. 15, Tuesday.
cells.remarks: Gift of land to certain specified Brahmans in the village of Moḍaballi, otherwise called Vīra-Bukkapa-Rāja-pura. Refers to a previous gift by Hiriya-Kumpaya. The two imprecatory verses in the end are written in Grantha characters.

cells.place: On the south base of the Koḷandāśvami-vamin temple, at Uṛagaḍam (Chingleput taluk, Chingleput district).
cells.remarks: Gift of 30 paṇam for the celebration of a festival in the temple of Raghunātha-Perumal, in the month of Avani, by Achchamma (wife of) Paṭṭaṇgi.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of land and money (400 paṇam) by Āchchal, wife of Āgari Annaṅgar, to the temple of (hakravarttinayanagar at agaram Uṛagaḍam alias Srī-Parankusa[purum].

cells.place: On the north base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a certain Nallarāyaṇ, son of Kaṛumachcheṭṭi, a dandanāyaka to Raghunātha-Pera-māḷ temple in the same village, for conducting the Śī Hāmanavami festival.

cells.place: On a rock to the south of the Vaḍamallī-svara temple, in the same village.
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.place: On a rock to the west of the same temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of sheep for a lamp by a certain Kaṭṭai Kaṇṇan-uḍaiyān to the temple of Tiruvada-mallī-śvaramuḍaiya-Mahādēvar at Vaḍamallī-mangalam, a village in Kuḷattūr-kōṭṭam which is a sub-division of Kaḷattūr-kōṭṭam a district of Jayangoṇḍa-śōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the south base of the Somamudēś-vara temple at Vayirapuram (Tindivanam taluk, South Arcot district).
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by Sōmanāthan, to the temple of Tirumudīśvaram-uḍaiyār at Vayirapuram, a village in Oymā-nāḍu, a sub-division of Oy-mā-nāḍu in Jayangoṇḍa-śōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the same temple, by P. rrun Pīchohan for the merit of a private individual whom his arrow had killed by accident.

cells.place: On the west base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land, exempted from śilāri and gōvari, for maintaining various services in the same temple by the inhabitants (ūrōm) of Vayirapuram alias Jananāthanallūr in Oymā-nāḍu a sub-division of Oymā-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register a gift of land which was situated in Yiyūr, a hamlet of Vayirapuram, by the residents (ūrōm) of the latter village.

cells.place: On the north base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Gift of money for rice offerings to the shrines of Mūlasthānamuḍaiya-Mahādēva at Vayirapuram, by the inhabitants (ūrōm) of that village.

cells.place: On a slab lying near the Puḍiyēśvara temple at Tiruvakkulam (Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district).
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Tiruvakkulam to the shrines of Chidambaram and Śivakāmasundari Amman of the temple of Pāvanēśamuḍaiya-Nāyanār by Acyutappa-Nāyaka, son of Sēvappa-Nāyaka, for the merit of Tirumalaiyāy (i.e., the Karpaṭa king Tirumala I).

cells.place: On the south wall of the Bhīmēśvara temple at Śingāriṭṭoppu near Chi-dambaram (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Gift of land at the hamlet of, for two lamps to the temple of Tiruchirapalli-ḍi-Mahādēva at Śingāriṭṭoppu, a hamlet in Rājēndra-śōḷa-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of 9 md of land, for 5,000 kāśu to the temple of Tirukaḷañjēji-Uḍaiyār at Pappa-goḍichōri alias Parāntakēśanallūr, a hamlet of Pappa-goḍichōri-palli-yūr. The land was a field of the temple of Ilamanīr alias Sundara-śōḷapaṇḍyanallūr which was situated in Guḍi-śōḷapaṇḍiyapalli-nāḍu and the sale was witnessed by the assembly of the village.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same temple
cells.remarks: Registers an order of the king that, from this date, the assessed lands (taram-p-pāḍu) standing in the name of the Subrahmanya-Piḷḷaiyār shrine in the Aruṇoḷīśvara temple of this village be included with those of the inter, that lands declared to be superior to the eighth class be assessed and that those below the eighth class be allowed to continue as before and that the site of the temple of Tiruttoṇḍaṭṭai-Īśvaram-Uḍaiyār, its enclosure, premises and the sacred tank fill now included in the account of the temple of Aruṇoḷīśvara-Muḍaiyār. The order was executed by the 'land-survey committee (nilam-aḷavaga-pparamakkal) of the village assembly of Perumaḷappuḷiyūr. Full details of the lands (extent, boundaries, etc.) thus dealt with are recorded.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Refer to the order registered in No. 262 and states that it was issued by Viḷḷavarāyan at the request of Vaḍunbarāyan. The document is signed by ten officers of the king whom the Tirumandira-ōlai-nāyaka was Nar(kkuṇṛa)-Mūvēndavēḷāṇ.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of interest on 1100 kāśu for maintaining a lamp and a lampstand. It was stipulated that the grant was to be renewed at the end of every 6 years being produced after each period before the assembly and the temple authorities.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Seems to record the gift of a lamp.

cells.place: On the east wall of the 1st prákára, of the Naturaja temple at Chidambaram; right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Gift of land belonging to the village of Paḍiyūr alias Kuḷōttunga-śōḷa-nallūr in Kaḷattūr-kōṭṭam for maintaining the feeding house named Ayyappa-ruḷjēvi-śālai at Perumaḷappuḷiyūr in the west street called Muḍitaligopa-Perumaḷ-tiruvīthi.

cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of land for the offering called tiruppdévái on the day of Pushya in the month of Tai to the god Álúđaiyár. The inscription was ordered to be engraved on the Kulöttuågasólan-tirumaligai by the Tirumandiravólai Rajanáráyana-Múvendavełan.

cells.place: On the same wall, left of entrance
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a native of Tiramal-nādu which was a district of Uyyakkondār-valanādu, at Ōmakkuļi-kattalai, in the sabhā of Jayankondachōla-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya of Virudarājabhayankara-valanādu, for a flower garden. Also records another gift of land in Pappanudichēri alias Parakēsarimallūr which was a hamlet of Purumbargappuliyūr with four vēli (kēli) for maintaining the garden and providing offerings to the deity in the temple of Tirunōbirumbalam-Udaiyār.

cells.place: In the same place ..
cells.remarks: Registers that under the orders of Vikrama-Pāndya Oāngeyarāyan some land was set apart for building a gōpura, to be inhabited exclusively by the weavers (Siliyakkudiyar) and to maintain the tiruvānabhisheka perumālpuram, on condition that these weavers supplied four new cloths (every year) to the goddess Sivakāmasundari on the day of the tiruppudiyidu festival and five other small cloths for the shrines of Tirunānasambandap.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place ..
cells.remarks: Built at the beginning. Registers that, under orders of Udayangāryan, land was granted for supplying garlands on the occasion of the service called Rajakāruṇyan-sandi after the king, and on the day of a festival called 'Rājakāruṇyan-periya-tirunāļ'.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place ..
cells.date: Śaka 1665, Svabhānu, Pāńguni 7, Sōmavāra, and Friday, Rēvati.
cells.remarks: Records that the king repaired the big mandapa in front of the Tillai Gōvindarājasvāmin shrine in Tira-Chitrakūtam, the gōpura of the shrine, the shrines of the goddesses Sundaravalli-nāch-chhiyār and Sōdakīranāyakiyar. He also built a mandapa in front of Iruvāli-Aivan. He is alstated to have made rent-free the five villages Adar, Karunguli, Koriyamangalam, Marn-dantanallūr and Udaiyūr in which the Śrī-Vaishnavas were permanently living.

cells.place: On the south wall of the same prākāra
cells.date: Śaka 1461 Viśva (wrong), Mithuna, śu. di. 14, Rāja-yōga, Saturday, Anurādhā.
cells.remarks: The king ordered that the image of Tillai-Gōvindarāja-Perumāl at Perumbarrappuliyūr in Valadulambattu-usāvadi, a sub-division of Venganaiyūr-nādu in Rājādhirāja-valanādu, might be set up recovering to the-tiruvanam-nīru and granted 500 paṇam as the income from four villages for the upkeep of daily worship.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records that a gift of land for a flower-garden called Ponnambalakkūram, in the village of Koyilppadi, a hamiet of Perunagarppuliyūr, was made to the temple of Alagiyār by a certain [O]mpuli[yā]r, the younger brother of Arūndaiyār. The land was made tax-free. It was also provided for its upkeep by another gift of land made at Sērundi-ma[ṅg]alam, which was a hamlet of Tyāgavali-chaturvēdimangalam in Vērkā-nādu. These transactions and gifts were engraved on the walls of the temple by the order of the king's officer at the temple of Nārāyaṇa.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records an order of Villavarayans and other officers of the king that the maintenance of worship and offerings in the temple of Dēvarāgai-Nāyanār was to be met from certain grants of land made to that temple.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Registers another order of Villavarayan with reference to certain grants of land providing flower garlands to the god and goddess. One of these lattor was situated in Vikramasōjanallūr (also called Ayiragandapān[j]uramasūdanallūr) and was granted by a certain Śivandēvar. Still another grant of land, in the hamlet of Kolam alias Sōla-kōrālavanallūr was made for providing offerings on the occasion when the images were taken on procession to the sea.

cells.place: No
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Vangāttarayan to the temple authorities to engrave on the walls of vikrama-sōjan-tirumalligai the gift of lands in Pallippadai alias Vikramasō[nallōr, Erukkattūriyéri Jayangondapānjanallūr and Alagalūr alias Jayangondasōanallūr, for the flower-garden Usaga-mullaināyakamandaram which was so named after the queen.

cells.place: No
cells.remarks: Registers the founding of an agrahāra named Vikrama-Pāndya-chaturvēdimangalam on the western side of Perumbayirappuliyūr and its presentation to 108 learned Brahmans. For the maintenance of the residents of other villages in the said grāmaparikāra) the village Rājasiṁkhama[nallur alias Puliyangudi on the western bank of Ponnēri was acquired and granted being divided into 147½ shares (paṅgu).

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 11% cris of land of ādūr alias Jananātha-mangalam, to the temple of the god Naganātha-mudaiya-Nāyanār, the matha, etc., of Ulagāma-ludumulaiya-chaturvēdimangalam, a hamlet on the western side of Perunbagrappuliyur. The recipients had to measure out: kodam on each rēli of temple land.-Plate-1, nayaka as “the donces of Vikramas-Utgai-chaturvedimangalam.' Registers an order of Palla[n]tavarayan to the temple authorities to engrave on the walls of the kulot-tungsōan-tirumalligai, a gift of land for offerings to the shrine of Alagiya-T[iruchchirambalamudaiyār built by A[ra]sarkulaikesari, in the hamlet of Kaggongudi alias Parivaramkanyanallur.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Tiranīrru[chchū]r[n]thangalain by a certain Kallingarāyan, for supplying 500 jack fruits, 5,000 mangoes and 5,000 plantains to the temple and 5,000 arecanut palms. The assembly of that village agreed to make the land tax-free by changing the taxes duo on it, to the village. The Tira-mandiraōlai was Nē[y]andaichchōla-Mūvēndavēlan. Built in at the end. Gift of land by two private individuals for a flower-garden and provision was also made for the servants who looked after it. The gift was built at the end. Records that under orders of Tondaimān, a land presented at Midinikkudi alias Dānavinodanalin for a flower-garden was made to the tirumandapam. This was engraved on the walls of Vikramaśōlanallur, this grant was engraved under orders of Siyaganga, who The Tiramandiraśai being Alipand Ma[v]endavėl[y].

cells.place: On the north wall of the same prākāra
cells.remarks: Registers an order of three officers of the king, viz., Tondaimān, Tiruvāyirudaiyan and Madhurāntaka Brahmarāyan (Ceylon-Rāyar). The lands granted by a certain person, viz., Arūndan-Vēla... having 200 red lotuses to the temple and for maintaining the people who grew them, was to be engraved on the walls of Vikramasōlan-tirumalligai. The Tiramandira-sulai to be met by he Neiyudaiachchōla-Mūvēndavēlan. Still, the same person made the same person made for a flower-garden in the 13th year and the 2nd day" of the king, was also engraved, the old document having “become worn out.”

cells.place: On the same wa I

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wa I
On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of garden land at Koyilpāḍi, a hamlet of Perumbuliyūr, for providing garlands to the shrines of the god and the goddess by certain Vāgadhirājan. The order of the grant was as usual engraved on the walls of the temple.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Order of Chēdiyerāyan to engrave on the temple walls a gift of land for providing offerings, etc, in a shrine situated in one of the streets of Perumbarappuliyār.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registors an order of Topđaiman that an arrangement regarding a certain land made in order to provide flowers, cocoaruts, etc., be engraved on the wall of Vikkiramasōlan-tirumaļigai.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land. Order of Villavadarayan approving of certain arrangements about specified temple lands made by the assembly (mūlu-parushaiyār) of Perumbarappuliyār.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: The first ten lines are engraved over another inscription of Vikrama Chōlādeva beginning with the historical introduction Guardāmo-lāga, etc. Order of Topđaiman to the temple authorities remitting certain taxes on lands which had been originally granted for the maintenance of the servants of a flower garden belonging to the temple. The reason for the remission was that the said lands being close to the sea had become filled up with sand and overgrown with weeds. Mentions Virarakhasa-Vēlaikkāra.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: This is stated to be a copy of an inscription originally engraved on the opposite side of the shrine (shrine). Gift of land by purchase for supplying garlands of red lotuses to the temple.

cells.place: No
cells.remarks: Unfinished. This is evidently also a copy. Before to the purchase of a dēvadāna land by a private individual.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: No
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Villavarāyan and four other officers assigning the income in paddy from certain land originally granted for the upkeep of a flower garden, for the maintenance of the servants of the temple and the flower garden.

cells.place: No
cells.remarks: An order of the same officer remitting assessments on certain lands granted to the temple for the flower-garden. The transactions were engraved on the temple walls.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: No
cells.remarks: Registers that certain lands granted by Gangaiyāryan were made tax-free and exempted from duties. The car procession was to be maintained and the temple was to receive 100 kāśu as kuḍimai assessment and 6 kalam of paddy as vīrabhōga on each vēli of land.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Order of Kulakkis[ia]n-S[i]l[a]y exempting duties and assessments on lands presented by a certain choli-yaiyan for maintaining 36 persons employed in a water-shed in the ma[n]dapa known as Anniyēra-k-kulam south of the seven-storeyed gōpura on the southern side of Rājakāl-kai-t-tirunā[r]ai[y]al, 24 persons who were to offer water to the destitute learned Brahmanas, 64 persons who prepared offer-ings at Sikai ii[c]e, the shrine of the goddess?) and 5 persons who were to look after the upkeep of the flower garden and the maintenance, of its servants, may be engraved on the temple.

cells.place: On the north wall of the second prākāra of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Order of Kulappāyaray to registrar as to certain grants of land made for providing for conducting festivals and providing offerings in the temple of Tiruohchirambala-Makali which was founded on the south side of the road by which the god was taken in procession for the sea-bath, and engraved on the temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that, at the request of the chiefs Pottappi-chōd[a]n and Kārānai-Vilupparaiyan, the original documents pertaining to a gift of land which was made to the temple for a flower-garden were engraved in the treasury of the temple and engraved on its walls.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of land for providing flower-garlands to the temple. The grant was ordered to be engraved on the temple walls and the original documents in the temple treasury. (Tirumandira-olai). The royal secretary [Tirumandira-olai] was Rājendraēngan Māvendarāyan.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of lands for a flower-garden granted by a donor mentioned in No. 290.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: A donor and servants were both pensioned for a flower-garden and were partly benefited by the servants of the garden were included at the donor's request in the tirumandirakkudi lands of the temple and the fluot engraved on the temple walls. The samndra-olai was Neiyudaiachchōla-Mūvendu-vēlan.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king:
Sakallabhūvanachakravartin Āvanīyēla-p-pūrandan alias Kōpperunjīgadēva.
Tribhuvanachakravartin Rājarājadēva
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Porumal-Pilialai Sākaiyan and mentions the gift of land for a flower-garden. Mentions the gift of land for a flower-garden by Nandi-Pōttarasa-Nayanār, chief of Nulambapadi alias Niyāmpākkam. She had purchased the land from different people.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Śōḻakōṉ recording gift of land for a flower-garden by a dancing girl.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Śōḻakōṉ that eight śandi oblations, like those offered at the shrine of Mūlasthānam-Uḍaiyār in (the temple of) Tiruchchiṟṟambalam, be also offered at the shrine of Dakshiṇāmūrti and that the gift of land made for providing five of these eight śandis, be made tax-free.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of the king's officers passed at the request of Gāṅgēyarāyaṉ, that certain lands granted to the temple for supplying flowers and maintaining the servants of the flower-gardens, were to be made free of kuḍimai, that the documents pertaining to the lands in question were to be deposited in the temple treasury (tirukkaiōṭṭi ?), and that the transaction was to be engraved on the walls of the temple.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Śōḻakōṉ that a gift of land was made for additional offerings in the shrine of Dakshiṇāmūrtidēva (referred to in No. 305), and that this land was made a rent-free tirunāmattukkāṇi under the command of the king.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Śōḻakōṉ, that the śāliya merchants (nagara) were to be provided with land for building their houses on condition that they would supply the necessary cloths for the pariṭṭam of the god and the goddess.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.date: 12th year and 125th day; and Kumbla, 6th day (in the middle of the record).
cells.remarks: Registers that a certain Ediriliśōḻaṉ alias Iruṅgōḷaṉ having founded a temple called Vikramaśōḻīśvaram-Uḍaiyār at Parakēsarinallūr, a hamlet of Perumbaṟṟappuliyūr after acquiring the required land from various people and having provided for houses of Brāhmaṇas and temple servants, the king ordered the assessment on this land to be deducted from the revenue of the village, to be entered in the temple accounts with the original documents preserved in the temple and the whole transaction engraved on the walls of the temple.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers that a land was granted for a flower-garden and another for maintaining its four servants. It was ordered that these lands might be included with the other temple lands and that the excess (maḍakku) in measurement be deducted from the village (accounts). The Tirumandira-ōlai was Mīṉavaṉ-Mūvēndavēḷāṉ.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a flower-garden and its servants. Again the excess of land discovered by comparison with existing village accounts was granted to the temple and the village accountants (varikkūṟuśeyvār) were ordered to correct their figures. The servants of the garden were exempted from certain services usual to nilaṇḍakkārar. The tirumandira-ōlai was Rājanārāya(ṇa)-Mūvēndavēḷāṉ.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Perumāḷ-Piḷḷai alias Sōḷakōn, made for the welfare of the king. Records an exchange of land and refers incidentally to the temple (Chidambaram) and the street called Tiruvīthi-ambalam-Mākaḷi on the south side of the street, Vikkiramachōḷa-teṅgu-tiruvīthi by which the god was taken on procession to the son.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king: Tribhuvanachakravartin Kōnērimēlkondān having been pleased to stay at Madurai (Ceylon) and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya was pleased to perform the anointment of heroes and the anointment of victors.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a flower-garden. It was ordered that the land be added to the flower-garden meant for the tiruvīthi, muḷiyai, and nandiyavatta flowers to the temple regularly; when these failed other flowers had to be supplied.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.king: Tribhuvanachakravartin Kōnērimēlkondān having been pleased to stay at Madurai (Ceylon) and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya was pleased to perform the anointment of heroes and the anointment of victors.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a flower-garden to supply flowers to the temple of the goddess. Refers to a transaction which happened in the 33rd year of the king.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers an addition to a flower-garden by a certain Kūttan-Ādittan-Iḷaiyāḷvār of Āmūr for the maintenance of a flower-garden which had been already granted by himself, for supplying 700 red lotuses to the temple every day. The ten servants and others who cultivated the garden were permitted to enjoy the land given them as a kani. The transaction was engraved on the temple walls.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that a flower-garden had been founded for the temple of the goddess by a certain Ādittan-Iḷaiyāḷvār, alias Rājadharājapallavaraiyar at the hamlet of Kōḷuppūḍi surnamed Kshatriyākhamaṇi-nallūr, that land in three different villages had been granted for the purpose, and that the servants had to water the flower-plants, pick flowers and supply them to the temple, and that these lands were now included with other temple lands and that the order of the king was that the gift be being engraved on temple walls and the original documents deposited in the temple treasury.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of land for growing red lotuses and for providing food (keyyu₹) and cloth-money to the gardeners who grew them. Refers to the land-warvey made in the 16th year of Sunigandavirstu Kulottunguśōladēva and to the 25th year of Periyadēvar Tribhuvanaviradēva.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Perumal-Pillai alias Sōlakōn, that certain gifts of land for the maintenance of gardeners, be recorded on the temple walls.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sōlakōn ordered that a gift of land for a grove of trees be made a rent-free dēvadānu and so registered on the temple walls.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Vira-Pandya-Vaṇa ihirāyan that a gift of one tirucōdā together with a piece of land for the maintenance of the latter, made by a certain Dipattarniyaṇ at Sōjakulav-Jilimallār may be deducted from the accounts of Sōjakulavallinallār and added to the dēvadāna lands of the temple and that the transaction may be engraved on the temple wall. This pillar of the entrance was presented by Perumal Pillai alias Sōjakogar one of the chiefs of Avaniya-lappiyandaṇ Kōpperunjiṅga for (the merit of) his master.

cells.place: On a pillar of the western entrance into the second prākāra of the same temple; left side.
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Vira-Pandya-Vaṇa ihirāyan that a gift of one tirucōdā together with a piece of land for the maintenance of the latter, made by a certain Dipattarniyaṇ at Sōjakulav-Jilimallār may be deducted from the accounts of Sōjakulavallinallār and added to the dēvadāna lands of the temple and that the transaction may be engraved on the temple wall. This pillar of the entrance was presented by Perumal Pillai alias Sōjakogar one of the chiefs of Avaniya-lappiyandaṇ Kōpperunjiṅga for (the merit of) his master.

cells.place: On a second pillar in the main entrance
cells.remarks: Records that Tirumalaikkolundar the agent of Narasa-Nayaka, while he was in charge of the temple, enforced that ten cake-offerings and betel-leaves which must be distributed among certain specified individuals for the merit of Narasa-Nāyaka, were not to be withheld from them and used otherwise.

cells.place: At the southern entrance into the first prākāra of the same temple, left side.
cells.date: Śaka 1432, Pramodāta, Makora, la. di. Amāvāsya, Monday, Pura-qam.
cells.remarks: Gift of three villages with an income of 1,400 rēkai (gadvāṇa) for the machāpīja in the temple of Alsgiya Tiruchchirpambalanudaiya-Tembhirāgār, (included in Arasthu-kilpamu a sub-division of Vepnaiyur-nadu in Rajadhiraja-valamadu which was itself a district on the northern bank (of the Colercon) included in the province of Bhuvanekaviraṇ-paṭṭana-śirmai and for the maintenance of a feeding house, by a certain Appa-Pillai.

cells.place: On the door-post of a new entrance out close to the east gõpura of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Same as No 321 above. The pillar evidently belonged to a different part of the temple and has been put in at this entrance by the Nattukkottai Chettijes.

cells.place: On the gõpura at the main entrance into the Sivakāmi-Amman shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Same as No. 321.

cells.place: On the east wall of the Mahishasurimardani shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Sōlāyan that a gift of land for a flower-garden to the shrine of Appārharamesvarar be measured out and that the shrine and the original documents connected therewith, be preserved in the temple treasury.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Sōlāyan that a gift of land for a flower-garden to the shrine of Appārharamesvarar be measured out and that the shrine and the original documents connected therewith, be preserved in the temple treasury.

cells.place: On the base of the Nandi-mandapa opposite to the southern gõpura of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Consists of a number of mutilated and unconnected pieces. Stones out of order. Refers to an arrangement (vyavasthā) made by the temple managers.

cells.place: On the base of the Nandi-mandapa opposite to the southern gõpura of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Consists of six verses of which five refer to a battle fought evidently at Chidambaam, by a certain Monaiyaṇ Valliyaṇ Adittaṇ chief of Panaisevyar (P) on behalf of the Pandya (Minavaṇ) against the Chōja (Valavaṇ). The author of this poetry was Taynalla-Perumal Munaiyadaraiyaṇ alias Bhuvanekavira Tondaimaṇ.

cells.place: On the base of a small shrine in the western prākāra of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Contains some detailed account of land measurement.

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor in front of the Gaņapati shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Refers to a gift by purchase of some godowne, by a certain Nāgama-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On the east gõpura of the same temple; right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Conseits of two verses the first of which refers to a conquest of the Pāndya king over the Chōla, the latter being driven into the forest. The second mentions Kādavarkōṇ and the Pāndya king Sundarattōl.

cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Maṅgaraṣan granted the village of Chidambaranāthapuram (to the temple).

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.date: Šaka 1600, Parthiva (wrong), Sirhha, śu. dī. 16, Monday, Śubhayōga, Svāti.
cells.remarks: Gift of four villages to the temple of Chidambaresvara and Sivakāmasundari-Ammai to provide oblations and saored bath in early morninge, for the merit of Vaiyappa-Krishappa-Koṇdama-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Gift of 800 yoṇ for providing 20 (rice) offerings to the god Chidambaresvara and distributing the same among begging devotees. It is stated that this amount was til then being set apart by the temple for the ilakkai and koryu of the king and his followers (rājagaram?).

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Contains three verses the first of which refers to a hattle fought on the banks of Vellaju in which a certain Bhuvanekuviran was victorious. He last refers to Vikrama-Pandya.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: One verse describing the anger of Vikrama-Pandya.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: One verse in prize of Sundaru-Pandya and his weighing himself against gold.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Registers of land granted in Pūmpuņnī-Koņdana-Nasarika ordered that the 30 (rice) offerings for which he had provided 50,000 kalams of paddy in the district of Vīranārāyanachhiramai, be distributed among Saiva mendicants (tiruppunniyāntru).

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.king: Sundara-Mayan †
cells.remarks: Glorifies the prowess of Sundara-Mayan (i.e. Sundara-Pandya) who annihilated the forces of the Telīngas that surrounded him and drove the Bāna chief into the forest.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Mentions Sõlakalavalli and apparent to make provision for singing the panmālai (hymne) of the Nāyanar (Saiva saints) in the temple of Tirumālāttamuḍaiyan. Also mentions the village (?) of Kajamalam.

cells.place: In the same place, left of entrance
cells.remarks: In continuation of tractors. Registers that Suppammal mother of Ayyālammal, who was the wife of Puchchaiyappa-Mudaliyar of Kānchipuram, repaired this eastern gõpura and founded a Brahman settlement (agrahāra).

cells.place: In niches on the inner walls of the same gōpura.
cells.remarks: These labels engraved below images representing women in various dancing postures. The inscriptions are in Sanskrit poetry.

cells.place: On the south gōpura of the same temple; right of entrance.
cells.date: Śaka 1426, Bhu-dhirodgārin, Siṁha, śu. di. 14, Śrāvaṇa, Monday.
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Manguḍi Bāmanayakkär Maṇḍālayakkar gave the village of Karikkuḍi the western hamlet of Perumbappaliyur, for a double garland and offering to the god every day. The king receives the usual Vijayanagara titles.

cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Montions Pox-puliyār.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Same as No. 335, above.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Same as No. 339, above.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.date: Saka 1508, Vṛisha, Kumbhe, su. di. 14, Thursday, Sravishtha (i.e. Dhanishtha).
cells.remarks: Gift of seven villages and of income from pepper and other taxes towards daily oblations and festivals in the shrines of the god and goddess, by Vaiyappa-Kṛishṇappa-Koṇḍama-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Records that the provision made by the same ... for 20 orangas of rice distributed among the Śaiva mendicants (arādhéśi) in the temple, was placed under the supervision of Naunavāśiya-Udaiyār 'the superintendent of all services (kaimkaryam).'

cells.location: Andrahaḷu — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Sēdiyarāyan exempting certain land granted for flower-garden by certain avani-nāṭṭār in mahā-dvāra-maṇḍapa from kaḍamai and hudimai and declaring that these lands might enjoy the privileges of irrigation by channels, percolation and bailing.

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same gōpura; left of entrance
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Sēdiyarāyan that the gift of garden land made by avani-nāṭṭār towards the maintenance of 18 servants of the garden and of the water-shed within it, may be engraved on temple walls.

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab set up near the same gōpura
cells.remarks: Damaged. Provides for some specified repairs to the temple made for the merit of Mutu-Kṛishṇappa-Nāyaka, son of Vaiyappa-Kṛishṇappa-Koṇḍama-Nāyaka, son of Koṇḍama-Nāyaka on the bank of Kollidavāru, built by the same donor.

cells.place: On the west gōpura of the same temple; right of entrance.
cells.remarks: In praise of the Pāṇḍya king (Māravarman) Vikrama-Pāṇḍya.

Three verses describing the glory of king Sundara-Pāṇḍya who conquered the kings of Veṇāḍu (i.e. Travancore), those of the North (i.e., the Telingas) those of the Koṅgu (country) and killed Gaṅgādēva.

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.remarks: Same as No. 355, above.

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.king: Rāma-varma-Mahārāja, of the family of Sāramā-Peruṇāḷ-Nāyaṉār.
cells.remarks: The king is stated to have been born under the asterism Viśākha. Provides for 33 taligai (offerings) to be offered to Ānandatāpdava-Perumal Nayanār and distributed among Brahmapas, Mahésvaras and the temple cooks.

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.remarks: In praise of the Pāṇḍya king. Mentions Kōḍai (i.e. the king).
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||230" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 230</button>

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.remarks: Registers that 64 cows were granted for maintaining perpetual lamps in the presence of Nīrikaṇṭha, by the ministers Chaupāḍanāśa and Ādittāṉan.

cells.date: Śaku 1503, Vrisha, Kumbha, 6u.di. 14, Thursday, Sravishtha (i.e. Dhanishtha).
cells.remarks: Same as No. 348, above.

cells.date: Śaka 1517, Dur-mukhi, Ūḻai-ma-fall-season, Chitra, Junus eclipse.
cells.remarks: Gift of village surnamed Pūrappēṭṭai, for meeting the expenses of one day during the Appai-t-tiram festivities, in honour of the goddess.
Contains three verses and refers to the right between Sundara-Pāṇḍya and the Teluṅgas, at Madugūr in which the dead bodies were strewn up to the banks of the Pōrālai.
Same as No. 349, above.
Consists of two verses. There is apparently a reference to Sundara-Pandya's weighing himself against gold and using it for covering the templo.
Damaged. Two of the verses are in praise of the Pandya king (Marap).

Three verses extolling Vikrama-Pāṇḍya. The first says he conquered the king of Veṇāḍu (i.e. Travancore). The second in the second he is addressed as Bhuvanēkavīra (i.e. Kōḍai) and is stated to have been the enemy of Gaṅgādēva. The third advises king Vikrama-Pāṇḍya not to go to the north; for there it says he is a foe-a woman ruling with a man's name.

cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Built in at the bottom. Registers an order of Kali-garayan. Provides for offering to the god Kulôt-tuṅg-60]a-Vinayaka-Pillaiyat who is enshrined on the south side of the seven storeyed gôpura of Rajakka-tau hiran-tirumàligai. Refers to Ellandalaiyan-Perama]-tundi.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Same as No. 339, above.

cells.place: In niches on the inner walls of the same gopura.
cells.remarks: Registers the names of the various dances in Sanskrit, as in No. 343.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the same gopura
cells.date: Śaka 1516, Vijaya, Ādi, 1st day, Satur-day, Jyēshṭha.
cells.remarks: Registers that for the merit of Vaiyappa-Krishṇappa-Koṅgaṇama-Nāyaka, the districts Daṇḍamāṅ-galam, Vīranārāyaṇachaturvīramaṅgalam, Teḻku-nāḍu, Viṭaṅkakkuṉṟu and villages grouped under Aḍigalvār and others that had been exempted under the temple of Chidambarēśvara from early times, were made tax-free and that a fresh provision was made for a daily offering of 750 taḷigai.

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north gopura of the same temple; right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Same as No. 339, above.

cells.location: Erumbūr, Chidambaram taluk, Arcot South district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Registers that Vīrapratāpa Kṛiṣhṇadēva-Mahārāya after having started on a campaign against Siṁhādri-Pottaṇūru, planted a pillar of victory thereon, worshipped the god (at the shrine of Poppambalam (i.e. Chidambaram) and visited the god and built the northern gōpura of the temple.

cells.location: Andrahaḷu
cells.place: In the same place
cells.remarks: Registers that the three figures were the northern kings who wore a crown. This the northern gōpura was built by the god himself. The poet evidently means why the boat of the 371 that Krishṇaparaya built it.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the same gopura
cells.date: Śaka 1515, Vijaya, Ádi, 1st day, Saturday, Jyôshtha.
cells.remarks: Same as No. 369, above.

cells.location: Āttūr, Āttūr taluk, Salem district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the Karuṅga-Vināyaka temple, at the western gōpura of the same temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1349, Pla-vaṅga, Mā-śa, di. 5, Sunday, Rohiṇī.
cells.remarks: One stone missing. In the middle. Registers that the king ordered certain irregularities in temples and temple lands, to be set right.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a detached fragment built into the waste weir of the Vīraṭhānaṁkulaṁ
cells.remarks: Contains a portion of the historical introduction of Rājēndra-Chōla I. commencing with Sigahai-etc.

cells.place: On the south base of the central shrine in the Kadambavanēśvara temple at Erumbur (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of money for a lamp to the temple of Sīru-Tirukkōyil-Mahādēva at Urumūr alias Vikramachōla-chaturvedimaṅgalam, for the merit of (the king). — Included in the Nallāyiravanpāll-Pallaraiyān a Chālukki of Tondaimānāḍu and resident at Aṇuāvari, the eastern hamlet of Vayavanmadūra-chaturvedimaṅgalam in Virudarājabhayara-valanādu on the northern bank (of the Coleroon). Further, a grant of 80 bhōp. for a lamp, by a certain Kaliniki Kārāni, son of Maruṅgali in Kō-nādu, to the temple of Sīru-Tirukkōyil-nadigal, at Urumur in Nallayiravan-kurram on the northern bank (of the Coleroon). Gift of (money?) for a lamp, by Urumūr ('Urumar'), nādigaļ, at Urumur in Nallayiravan-kurram on the northern bank (of the Coleroon).

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by Kēra (temple mentioned in No. 379 above). The sabhā (assembly) of Urumur agreed to see the lamp regularly maintained in the temple.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of 200 palam and of 90 sheep for a lamp to the same temple by a resident of the northern suburb of the same village.

cells.location: Aragal (Aragalur), Attur taluk, Salem district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of a land-stand and of 90 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Sīru-Tirukkōyil-Mahādēva at Urumur. The donor was a certain Kurumbay Siguḥ, native of Villangay-arur in Arumbur-kūram, a sub-division of Pāṇdi-nādu.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||254" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 254</button>

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that the central shrine (śrīvimāna) was built of stone and that the gōpura with the adhi-purisvara was erected by Irun[gō]n Kuṇavan of Sīru-Tirukkōyilur. A gift of 3 veļi of land was also made by the same individual, with the permission of King Sōlērumaradigal Parāntakadēva, to the temple of Sīru-Tirukkōyil.Bhaṭāra at Urumur for dīpaḥ, chengal, archanābhōga and the maintenance of drummers (mel-ārakkhabhōga and the maintenance of drums and, at śrī-bali-nakshatra).
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||255" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 255</button>

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of a certain quantity of gold by a certain Araiyn Vichohadran of Urumur, according to which the assembly of Urumur a deadline and drained in Nalrayalur-kūram, a sub-division of Vayaranmadura-valanādu, agreed to pay them-rel fees usually collected from the drummers of the 'temple (srivchchar) [and to have the śrī-bali of the temple properly conducted].
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||256" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 256</button>

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Contains a portion of the historical introduction of Rājēndra-Chōla I. commencing with Tiruchchur-etc.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of money for a lamp to the temple of Sīru-Tirukkōyil-Mahādēva at Urumūr alias Vikramachōla-chaturvēdimangalam, for the merit of [the king]... A sum of 80 bhōp. for a lamp, by a certain Kaliniki Kārāni, son of Maruṅgali in Kō-nādu, to the temple of Sīru-Tirukkōyil-nadigal, at Urumur in Nallayiravan-kurram on the northern bank (of the Coleroon). Gift of (money?) for a lamp, by Urumūr ('Urumar'), nādigaļ, at Urumur in Nallayiravan-kurram on the northern bank (of the Coleroon). Gift of 200 palams and of 90 sheep for a lamp by a resident of the northern suburb of the same village (mentioned in No. 379 above). The lamp regularly maintained in the temple.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that lands were purchased from the assembly of Urumur alias Vikramachōla-chaturvedimaṅgalam and gravified to the temple of the goddess, tiru-mattakkulami of the Uyymar alias Vikramachōla-chaturvedimaṅgalam. The taxes kuṭamai, anṭikkal, etc., payable on these lands which amounted to 55 kalams of paddy were agreed to be paid to the temple by the assembly of the village. Refers also to loans borrowed from the temple treasury on account of 'bad time' (mine ?) and scarcity of grain (ukkan).

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: [5]th year, Simha, su. di. 8, Satnrday, Anijam.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers a sale of land to the temple as a tirumaṭṭakkāṇi of the goddess, by the sabhā of Urumūr alias Vikramachōḷachaturvēdimangalam.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of 96 sheep for a lamp and of 14 cows for curds and milk, by a native of Oḷugarai near Puṉṟai-Aṉāṉūr to the temple of Tiruvirāmēśvaramuḍaiya-Pāṇḍiyāṉār at Kṛuṁbūr which was also called Urumūr alias Vikramachōḷachaturvēdimangalam a brahmadēya in Vaḍagarai-nāḍu, a sub-division of Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Sale of land to the temple by the assembly of Urumūr a brahmadēya and brahmadēya in Naḷvōr-kūṟṟam which was a sub-division of Vaḍagarai Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu. Mentions the taxes ēchōṟu, Vāḍilkoṇḍa-kūṭṭam and.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the temple of Śīva-Tirukkōyil-Bhūtaṛa.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: [1]2th year, Vjiśākha, śu. di. 12, Wednesday, Rēvati.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the same temple by a certain Tōraṇavalḷavarāyaṉ, a servant and tenant of Kaḍavaṉuṉ.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a gift of gold for a lamp.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Registers that ten kaḷañju of tuḷai-poṉ were paid to the village assembly for making a certain land which was passed to the temple, tax-free.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp and offerings to the temple of Śīva-Tirukkōyil-Mahādēva at Urumūr, a brahmadēya in Naḷvōr-kūṟṟam, a sub-division of Vaḍagarai Rājarājēndra-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Refers to a decision (vyavasthā) arrived at by the assembly of Urumūr alias Vikramachōḷachaturvēdimangalam, a sub-division of Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu on the occasion when it met in the temple of Vaḷavamaṇḍēvi-Viṇagar-Āḷvār. Mentions Vijayagoṇḍaśōḷa-puram-uḍaiya-kōyil and the boundaries of certain lands which had been assigned for oblations.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 7th year, Mahāra, su. di. 8, Saturday, Rēvati.
cells.remarks: Registers that lands were purchased from the assembly of Uyyankonda-chôla-chaturvēdimangalam and granted to the temple of Vishnuvadanar at Pandyankuppam-āchēru-Pēriyari, and the temple of Sudi-Vudaiyan Alita Tiruchchuchyambalam-Müvendavēlan of Olugarai near Poygai-Araisür. The taxes kulamai, anikārai, etc., payable on these lands which amounted to 65 kulams of paddy were agreed to be paid to the temple by the assembly of the village. Refers also to a loan borrowed by the assembly from the temple treasury on account of "(bad) time (? unine) and scarcity of grain (ukkan).

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Begins with the introduction Prajñēsrī svasti sri, etc. The assembly of the brahmadeya village, Valangaima/devi-chaturvēdimangalam in Rajendrasingha-valanādu, a subdivision of Rajendrasingha-valanādu assembled 'velur 'in the hall called Tiruvarangadēvam within the temple and in the presence of the "annual supervision committee" agreed to pay in paddy the filters on certain lands belonging to the temples of Tiru-Tirukkōyil-udaiyār, Jīvanāgatslvaya and Mōykoy-kōyil. The income was to be utilized for lamps and offerings.

cells.place: On the south wall of the Madarāntaka-Chōlēsvara temple at Toludur (Vrid-dhachalam taluk, South Arcot district).
cells.remarks: Refers to an exchange of wet land in Toluvur granted to the temple of Madurantaka-Cholēsvara-m-udaiya-Nāyanar, in place of the one at Chandân-dōkharanallur given by (kēliyar (f.) under the tēva tank called Tiruval-Vikma-Vinuda-gandapperiya-dri.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that a certain Sēdibarayanavelar, chief of Sàmbi built the stone temple and the mandapa for the Sambai god Madurantakānvurudaiya-Nāyanar at Perun-Toluvur in Ugaiyur-küyyam, sub-division of Viranārāyana-valanādu. The land had also been presented to the same temple the processional images of the god and the goddess.

cells.place: On a slab lying in the same temple
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to record gifts of land to the temples of Madurántaku-İsvaram-Udaiyar and Araisūrdurai-Nāyanar.

cells.place: On a conch preserved in the Varadarāja-Perumal temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: To the temple of Tirunēru-Viramangalam-dēva, Taythunalla-Perumal, to the temple of Madurāntaka-Chōlēsvaram-udaiya-Nāyanar at Toluvūr.

cells.place: On the south base of the Kannaimale-svaran temple at Attur (Attur district), Salem district.
cells.date: Śaka 1435, Āshāḍha, Śuklapaksha, Śīttirai, 18th day, 3, Friday, Rōhiṇī, Saubhagya-yoga
cells.remarks: Registers that the chief Akki-Timmaiya-Nāyaka made the ruling Malaiyāla alias Jananātha-valanādu in the Magadai-mandalam, give the village called Villavaiyanātam on the northern bank of the river Nīvu, in the district of Ayyūr-kōrram, in hte-arundai to a certain Srirangara-bhaṭṭa, son of Arunāgiri-nātha, a certain share of the village. He granted village, a house-site, to the surname Akki-Timmaiya-Nāyaka-chaturvēdimangalam, after the donor. Incomplete. Needu to record the grant of a village for the merit of the king.

cells.place: On the west base of the same temple
cells.date: Śaka 14[4]0, Virodhi (wrong), śu. di. 11, Sunday, Pushya, 82nd year
cells.remarks: Registers the order of Vāṇṇūju-Perumāl that the gift of 200 kuḷi of wet land granted to the temple of Tirumālaiji-uḍaiya-Nāyanār for maintaining lamps, should be demarcated by trisūla-stones and the transaction engraved on stone.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to refer to the gift of Kallintam near Arraūr in Ārrūr-nāḍu, a sub-division of Magadai-maṇḍalam, under the name Mayilam-aḍaiyāmbhuva by a certain Arugal-Pillai, son of Nāyanār-Ayyangāra-bhaṭṭa, son of Aruparāginātha of Iraivanāraiyūr. The document was engraved on the kumudappuḍai in the temple of Tirumēṇiṭṭu-uḍaiya-Tambirān at Ārrūr.

cells.place: On the north base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Gift of paddy to the temple of Tirumēriṭṭi-Nākkar (or Aiyar) at Arral, which was a sub-division of Milaḍu, by three servants of the temple.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the same temple
cells.remarks: Incomplete. 15 pistors .... Eṛramāchi Timmaya-Nāyaka's son Tuḷukkāmu-Nāyaka, provided a car (which had not existed since the time of the Pāṇḍya kings), to the temple of Tiru-kāmeśvaramuḍaiyā-nāyanār in the Aragal-kurram, a sub-division of Magada-maṇḍalam in Malaḍu alias Jananātha-valanādu.

cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Kāmēśvara temple at Aragal (Attur taluk, Salem district).
cells.date: Śaka 1430, Do. V[i]bhava, Kumbha, śu. di. 7, Friday, Makha, Subhaga-yoga.
cells.remarks: Registers that Eraṇāchi Akki-Timmaya-Nāyaka rehabilitated the deserted village of Paṇṭalālai a brahmadēna and sirayamāya of the same temple, under the name Aragi-Tulukkāpa-Nāyakkan-pūttai and fixed the taxes which were evidently collected by the temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1435, Bhava, Siṁha, śu. di. 11, Wednesday, Svāti.
cells.remarks: Registers that the chief Akki-Timmaiya-Nāyaka made the ruling Malaiyāla alias Jananātha-valanādu in the Magadai-mandalam, give the village called Villavaiyanātam on the northern bank of the river Nīvu, in the district of Ayyūr-kōrram, in hte-arundai to a certain Srirangara-bhaṭṭa, son of Arunāgiri-nātha, a certain share of the village. He granted village, a house-site, to the surname Akki-Timmaiya-Nāyaka-chaturvēdimangalam, after the donor. Incomplete. Needu to record the grant of a village for the merit of the king.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Naraittulai-Navaitur to the temple of Tirukkāmisvaram-udaiya-Nayanar at Āragajūr in Ārūr-kūrram a sub-division of Magada-maṇdalam, for burning 160 lamps in the shrines of the god and goddess and the subsidiary shrines.

cells.place: On the south base of the same shrine
cells.date: Śaka 1430, Vibhava, Kumbha, śu. di. 10, Sunday, Āślēsha.
cells.remarks: Records that Eramañchi Tulukkaṇa-Nāyaka, seeing that the temple of Tirukkāmīśuram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Āragaḷūr was not provided with festive processions since the time of the Pāṇḍya, constructed a car for it, and fixed the days for the festivals. Also registers a grant of land by the temple authorities and a house to a certain kaikkōḷaṉ called Parayaṉ of Tamadanallūr.

cells.place: On the west base of the same shrine
cells.date:
Šaku 1426, Raktakshi, Simbha, su. di.
18, Friday, Svāti.
cells.remarks: Registers that Pakkamlaḍi, a village in Teṅkarai Narniyūr-kūṟṟam, a district of Magadai-maṇḍalam in Malāḍu alias Jananātha-vaḷanāḍu, was for a long time a dēvadāna [of the temple] and that subsequently taxes were collected from it; Eramañchi Tulukkaṇa-Nāyaka restored the village to the temple with all its income for worship and repairs.

cells.place: On the north base of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Registers the decision of Tirumalli-Nāyaka regarding the right of worship in the temple of Tirukkāmīśvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Rahuttarāyaṉ that the village Nāṭṭamaṅgalam in Śela-nāḍu which was given to him as a jīvita by the king, was now granted with all its income as a rent-free dēvadāna to the temple of Tirukkāmīśvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Āragaḷūr, for maintaining worship and repairs.

cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.date: 14th year, Rishabha, ba. di. 7, Monday, Dhanishṭha.
cells.remarks: Grant of 15,000 kāśu by a certain Nāchchi for maintaining worship, sacred bath, garlands, cloths, lamps, oil, offerings and festivals in the shrine of Kariyāṇa-Īśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār set up in the north-west corner of the first enclosure in the temple of Tirukkāmīśvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār. The donation was accepted by the servants of the temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers that the village of Ilattipāḍi which had been purchased from Malaiyanuḍai-Śambai by the trustees, was made tax-free in favour of the same temple, for maintaining worship, festivals and repairs by the trustees of that temple. The document is attested by the officers Vāṇakōvaraiyaṉ and Villavarāyaṉ.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of Ilattipāḍi to the trustees of the temple by Malaiyanuḍaiyaṉ Śambaiyāḻvaṉ, for 135 poṉ.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 29th year, Kanyā, śu. di. 2, Wednesday, Hasta.
cells.remarks: Gift of 5,000 kāśu for maintaining the sacred bath, twilight lamps, garlands, cloths and offerings to the three saints (emberumakkaḷ) (i.e. Appar, Sundarar and Śambandar) set up in the temple of Tirukkāmīśvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Āragaḷūr.

cells.place: On the south base of the same mandapa
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of 1,000 kuļi of land, made rent-free in the 13th year of the king, for the maintenance of two Brahmapas who recited the Vedas (BrBrBrBrBrBr<|490|>) in the temple, by the chief Śed[i]jrayaṇ. Aleo at the command of the king, the nāṭīr inhabiting the districts included between the rivers Vēmbarāgu and Peppai were required to assign certain specified taxes to the temple for the health of the king. The nāṭīr having however collected the kānikkai-paṇam in the 15th year of the king, they were ordered to return the collections immediately to the temple.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.date: Śaka 1427, Krōdhana, Makara, su. di. 3, Sunday, Dhanishthā, MahA-Sankrānti day. 7th year
cells.remarks: Registers that Allajanatha Īaiya-Nayaka and the inhabitants of Āgkār-naḍu and Mulaippāru-naḍu having met together provided for supplying oil to burn perpetual lamps and twilight lamps in the temple for the health of Egramāṣchi-Tulukkapa Nayaka.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Registers that the chiefs Vāpakōvaraiyaṇ and Villavarāyan granted annually 1/4 of their bull-calveas vrishabhas to the temple and assigned the remainder for work in connection with temple repairs including that of the enclosure wall called Poppareppīga Perumal-stirumadī.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Registers that mādāpadi-fici granted by Tyāgana-Nāyaka to the inhabitants of the districts (nād (ar) of Magadi-mandalam who had left the country owing to much oppression. Mentions Seam Isvara-Nayaka. Built in at the beginning. Fixes the details of mādaipadyam to be observed by the inhabitants of...

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Alambalam in Magadi-mandalam with all its income for instituting a service in the temple called Kōdaparāmar-sandi, after the king, for celebrating a festival on by Kalingaray every year for repairs.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Alambalam in Magadi-mandalam with all its income for instituting a service in the temple called Kōdaparāmar-sandi, after the king, for celebrating a festival on by Kalingaray every year for repairs.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same mandapa
cells.date: 10th year, Mine, su. di. 18, Thursday, Makhā.
cells.remarks: Registers that the king granted 1/2 [šēli] of land at Popparappi alias Rājanārāyananalir as a dīvadāna to the shrines of Kulaśekhara-Āvudaiyār and Vaļvitta-Maṅgaiyār which Kapṇdyadeva had founded in the same temple in the name of the [king's] elder brother (apṇēlvi). Attested by Adichohaṇ Ganapati Ālray alias Kadavetji of Kappalūr in Muttōrgu-kūrgam, a sub-division of Pāṇdi-maṇdalam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 3,000 kuhi of wet land below the tank Kulāśēkharan-Periyēri at Ārugaļūr, to the shrine of Kulāśēkhara-Avuḍaiyār mentioned above, for offerings.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1430, Sukla, Mina, śu. di. 7, Thursday, Viśākhā.
cells.remarks: The king receives Śaiva titles. Registers that Eṇumāni Talu(k)kapa-Nāyaka built a car for the temple which had not been in existence subsequent to the rule of the Pāṇḍya kings, instituted a festival called Sivaratri at Arugalūr and appointed individual provision with their maintenance, for carrying the god in processions (śrīpāda-tangi).

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: Śaka 1436, Yuvan, Mitbuna, su. di. 5, Monday, Āġvin1.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. The king receives Sajuva titles. Records that Akki-Timmaya-Nayaka of Epumañchi and the temple authorities together, granted to a private individual, 250 kuļi of land as īramai.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Gift of 2,000 kuhi of wet land below the tank Kulaśēkharan-Periyēri for a garden, by the king. Attested by Aichchur-Gaṇapati Ālvan alias Kaḍuveṭṭi, native of Kuppūr 'ur alias Ulaguḍaiyājanallur, on the north by the m.-r. sub-division of Pāḍu-un-ra-nilam.

cells.place: On the north base of the same gopura
cells.date: Śaka 1306, Raktākshi, Mēsha, śu. di. 'Pourṇami', Wednesday, Svāti.
cells.remarks: Registers the sale of the right (kāṇi) of worship by three priests of the temple of Tirukānīśvara- Muḍaiya-Nāyanar at Arugaļūr to a priest of the temple, Tiruvaiyāṛi-nāyanār, sub-division of Valudiyaram in Pāṇḍyakulam, sub-division of Maḍudu alias Janmanātha-vaļunāḍu, in Māngedhimaṇdalam.

cells.place: On the same tase
cells.date: Śaka 1297, Rākshasa, Vrischika, śu. di. 11, Friday, Rohiṇī.
cells.remarks: The servants of the temple, viz., the śrīvāsa, Mähēśvaras and temple accountants having assembled together, gave to certain Eṇumāṇyaṇān alias Kulāśēkhara-Muḍaiyār, the work of supervising the district services in the temple and a house for his living.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same tase
cells.date: 18th year, Mithuna, śu. di. 18, Friday, Anurādha.
cells.remarks: Refers to a dispute between the oil-merchants (sāṇiyanagarattar) and the seffis in which the latter permitted the former to manage the business of the temple. The management continued to be in the hands of the oil-merchants for some time. This having failed, the district people (u(rravor) granted the village of Tālaināvay for conducting permanently the festivals in the temple.

cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.date: Śaka 1461, Vikārin, Kanya, śu. di. 7, Fri-day, Magha, 18th year, Pathi-uppl.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record the grant of a land, and medhipatiya to a private individual for doing the duties of the temple (koyil-kāryam).

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same base ..
cells.remarks: Registers that the temples Tirukkaņņāpuram-uḍaiyār-Nāyanar, Tayilanallūrum-uḍaiya-Nāyanar and Poṇparappina-Bōlāvarayan gave tax-free ground to the Nattavar of certain Sōramāgar. Also 200 kaḻañju of wet land and 2,000 kuḻi of dry land were given to this same person in the villages of Kuruk-kaipāḍi, Pakkaṇpāḍi, Ji'bāpāḍi and Viḻalūr.

cells.place: On the east wall of the same maṇṭapa; right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Registers a political compuot given by Śengēpi Ammaiyuppaṇ Ālagiyaśolaṇ alias Ediriliśolacho-olhambuvarāyaṇ to the chiefs Ponparappiṇa. Vāṇakōvaraiyar, Kulottungasola Vāṇakōvaraiyar and brother-in-law (maiiohchuṇaṇār) Kadavarāyur. Built in at the end. Gift of 2,000 kāśu for one lamp and of 49 cows for seven other lamps to be hurnt in the temple of Tirukkamśivaram-udaiya-Nāyaṇar and subordinate shrines.

cells.place: On the wall behind the Dvārapāla-image in the same maṇṭapa; right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Gift of land for offerings to Āchchali who has been mentioned above in No. 415.

cells.location: Kokkarāyanpeṭ, Tiruchēṅgōḍu taluk, Salem district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: In the same place; left of entrance ..
cells.remarks: An order (from the king) to the managers of the temple, stating that the weavers settled by them outside the northern gate of the temple gave lands belonging to the shrine of Kulasekhara-Āḷudaiyār founded in this temple by the chief Kaṇḍiyadēvar. Attested by Ādittan Gaṇapati-Alvān alias Kaḍuveṭṭi of Kappalūr.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||311" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 311</button>

cells.place: On the south wall of the second prākāra of the same temple.
cells.remarks: The right of worship for 3½ days of a month in the temple owned by a certain lady, was ordered to be sold evidently on account of some defalsution of temple jewels. The amount 250 paṇam (= 25,000 sōliya-kāśu) was paid by the other worshippers of the temple by selling part of their own privileges and distributing among themselves the privileges that were under dispute.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same prākāra ..
cells.date:
1[2]th year, Mēsha, sū. dī.
Pūrnai, Thursday, Svati.
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Refers to the terms of a political compact between the two chiefs Rāja[rā]ja-dēvaṇ Poṇparappinār alias Kuḷōttuṅgasōla-Vāpakāvaraiyar and Kiliyūr Maḷaiyamāṇ of Tirukkovalur.

cells.place: On the east wall of the same prākāra; right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Refers to the terms of a political compact between the two chiefs Rāja[rā]ja-dēvaṇ Poṇparappinār alias Kuḷōttuṅgasōla-Vāpakāvaraiyar and Kiliyūr Maḷaiyamāṇ of Tirukkovalur.

cells.location: Kugalur, Gobichettipalaiyam taluk, Coimbatore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall; left of entrance ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 3,000 kuli of wet land reclaimed from forest in the village of Deviyakurucohi in Ārār-nādu for worship and ropairs in the shrines of Kulasēkhara-Ālađaiyār and Vājvitta-Mangaiyar in the temple of Tirukkāniśvaram-udaiya-Nāyanār at Āragalār. Attested by Kūduvetṭi chief of 6 appalār.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxviii||315" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXVIII, No. 315</button>

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall; left of entrance ..
cells.remarks: Gift of land, made tax-free, for the maintenance of the gardeners of a flower-garden belonging to the temple Tirukkāmandīsvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyanar. Attested by the same person.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall; left of entrance ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of the king to the managers of the temple stating that the service UlagamuJuduđaiyal-sandi founded in his name was to be maintained from the 8,500 kuli of land granted at Ālambalām in Naraiyār-kāram a sub-division of Milāđu alius Jananatha-valanāđu.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall; left of entrance ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 4 kuḻi of wet land in Aruḻūr, for feeding ten persons in the temple. Attested by Kaḍuveṭṭi.

cells.place: On the north base of the central shrine in the Kaiśvaradāra-Perumāḷ temple in the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1444, Darmuti, Sirihbu, i.e. di. 10, Montay, Hasta.
cells.remarks: The third figure of the Śaka year must be 2. Records that a certain Ammuna-Nayaka give to the temple of Kaiśvaram [Perumāḷ] at Āraḻūr, for the maintenance of the charitable works of the king and a female servant (pēţţi), providing for the maintenance in that shrine Aranā-Nāyaka may be victorious.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Vapakōvaruiyap that wet and dry lands in different villages were to be purchased as Vitronāđgudepperuvilai, the former at 6 kāin for one kuli and the latter at 2 kāin for kuli and granted as tirrendmattukkāpi to the temple of Kariya-Perumal at Āragalār.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: The ārādhanam (in the central shrine) of this Kariya-Perumāḷ temple called also Rājarāja-Vināgayan was built of stone by Tuṇyavantiyār wife of Rājara[ja]-Vāṇakōvaraiyan. She was the daughter of Iruṅgalakkāyi.

cells.place: On the east base of the same shrine ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 1,000 kuḻi of wet land below the tank at Poṇ-parappil alias Rājamarāyan uḷḷār, for oblations and repairs to the shrine of Śriṅga (tir. Sriṅgāra) in the temple of Kariya-Perumāḷ in order to consecrate it in the king's elder brother (vendiya) Sundara-Pāṇḍyan ... by Aḷidiyan [ti]rumpati-Ālvān of Kappaiṇūr who was surnamed Vaṇadārāyan.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.date: Śaka 1411, Pramathin, Āshāḍha, ba. di. 13, Friday, Anurādhā.
cells.remarks: Registers that three sthānīkas of the temple of Perumāḷ-Kariyavar went on a deputation to the king at Vijayanagara and petitioned (vñjñāpanam) injustice done by the authorities (adhikāris) stationed at Daviyākuruchchi a village belonging to the temple. The chief Amaram 'Iimmaraas introduced them to the king, got their grievance redressed presented them each with a garland and some pearls, and then an order was granted for 900 kuli of wet land at Ponparappi and at Daviyākuruchchi, as a sarvamānya gift.

cells.place: On the south face of the same shrine
cells.date: Śaka 1417]4, Rudhirodgarin (wrorg), Sithha, su. di. 10, Friday, Svati.
cells.remarks: A certain Tammaya-Nayaka in the name of his master Kumāra Ammapa-Nayaka granted land at Siyyeri a hamlet of Aragalār, to three worshippers in the temple of Perumāl-Kariyavar who were in the enjoyment of the privilege called Archundībhuva-kāni, for the victory of Narasa-Nayaka.

cells.place: On the south base of the maṇḍapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.date: Śaka 1446, Tarapa, Makarn, 11, Revati, Friday, Sahkramapa-ponyukaka.
cells.remarks: Gives a genealogy of the king from Tammaraayya. Registers a grant of land for services in the daily service in the temple of Kariya-Perumāḷ and a provision of 1,000 kuli of land made for their maintenance, by a certain Mrityumjaya-Nāyaka for the merit of his master Tirumali-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On the north base of the same maṇḍapa
cells.date: Śaka 145[4], Nandana, Kumbha, su. di. 3, Monday, Uttara-Bhadrapada.
cells.remarks: Kappan, a kaikōḷa of Kubhiyur having instituted a one-festival in the temple, the managers met together in the Sōpāna-maṇḍapa and decided to grant him and his descendants, a house, a loom, a piece of land and some privileges in the temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of the Kumāraṇṇai shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of 1,000 kuli of hard land the tank at Tolavur for worship and repairs in the temple of Vaiṇ-vaṇa-l[ēvaram]-uḍaiya-Nāyanār at Araiyalur.

cells.place: On the south base of the Cholēśvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Kurukkuppādi for worship and repairs in the temple of Tiruva[n]nāmalai-Uḍaiya-Nāyanār. Attested by Vāpa-kōvrai-Nāyan and Viḷuppadaraiyan and order communicated to Viḷādaraiyan and the accountants (puravariyar).

cells.place: On the north base of the same temple
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Kil-Megarār to the same temple. Attested and communicated as before.

cells.place: On the north wall of the Ekāmaranathasvāmin temple at Tadavur (Attur taluk, Salem district).
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Vira[d]dhamallur, to the temple Tiruvēgamba[m]-uḍaiya-Nāyanār at Tadavur. Attested by Tayilunalla-Perumāḷ and Viḷuppadaraiyan and communicated to Viḷādaraiyan and the accountants (puravariyar).

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of land for worship and repairs to the temples of Tiruvōga[mbam-uḍaiya-Nāyanar] and Kuṅga-merinda-Perumāḷ.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.king: Tribhuvanachakravartin Kuḷōttuṅga-Chōlādēva who was pleased to take Madurai (Madura), and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya.
cells.remarks: Registers that the temple of Tiruveṅgabuam-uḍaiya-Nāyanar (the same temple) (alias) Tuvākara-Nāyanar was built by ... chchola-Pallavaraiyan ... kuḻram, a sub-division of Miḷadu alias Janaṇātha-vaḷanādu, was built of stone, the cost being met from gold already in possession of the temple and from what was now presented by the king and ... who was to worship.

cells.place: On the north wall of the same temple ..
cells.remarks: Gift of a land which had been lying waste for many years as a dēvadāna to the same temple for worship, repair and festivals. Attested by Ādittan Gaṇapati-Alvān alias Vāpadarāyan of Kappalūr.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of 500 kuḻi of land at Taḍavūr as kōṇi to a certain Peṇṇakkalaperaiyan Pakkam-alagiyan by Magadēsan Ulagamkatta Vāṇakōvaraiyan.

cells.location: Lālāpettai, Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Tiruvēṅgāmbam-uḍaiya-Nāyanar of Taḍavūr in Miḷ-Gangapādi-nādu, a sub-division of Rājarāja-vaḷanādu, for the merit of Anātha-vaḷanādu, for worship, repairs and festivals, by Kuḷōttuṅgasōla Vāpakāvaraiyan.
